works.title: The Christian Captives
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Five Acts in a mixed manner
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's tragedy in five acts, first published in 1890. In a castle garden by the sea, Almeh, daughter of the King of Fez, meets the Christian captives of the Moorish court, among them the Portuguese princes Ferdinand and Enrique; a chorus of the captives sings Latin hymns and speaks in turn.

works.title: Christias
works.subtitle: Christiados libri sex
works.author: Marco Girolamo Vida
works.blurb: Vida's Virgilian epic on the Passion of Christ, in six books of Latin hexameters, written at the request of Pope Leo X and first printed in 1535.

works.title: Christmas Rose
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, First Series: II
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A dialect yarn that begins on a Christmas-time evening at the school in the year of the great storm of 'hunder-thirty-nine' and ends with the mystery of who or what the Christmas Rose was.

works.title: Christs Victorie and Triumph
works.subtitle: in Heaven, and Earth, over, and after Death
works.author: Giles Fletcher the Younger
works.blurb: A Spenserian poem in four parts on the redemption of man, from Mercy's plea in heaven to Christ's temptation, his death on the cross and his resurrection and ascension.

works.title: Chronicle of England
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A rhymed chronicle of about 1,040 lines in couplets, from the coming of Brutus and the giants of Albion through the British kings Lud, Bladud and Arthur and the Saxon and Danish kings to the Norman Conquest and the Plantagenets, closing with the death of Piers Gaveston under Edward II.

works.title: Chronicle of the Cid
works.author: Anonymous (Poem of the Cid)
works.blurb: Robert Southey’s English compilation of the medieval Spanish chronicles and ballads recounting the life and legend of Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, El Cid.

works.title: On the Ends of Good and Evil (De Finibus)
works.subtitle: Five dialogues on the supreme good: the Epicurean, Stoic and Peripatetic accounts examined
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Written in 45 BC, De Finibus Bonorum et Malorum sets the leading Hellenistic schools against one another on the question of what the highest good is. Torquatus defends Epicurus and Cicero replies (Books I and II); Cato expounds the Stoic view (III) and Cicero answers it (IV); Piso sets out the Peripatetic and Old Academic position (V). C. D. Yonge's literal translation (Bohn, 1853), with Cicero's chapter numbers kept at the head of paragraphs.

works.title: On Duties (De Officiis)
works.subtitle: Three books to his son Marcus: moral goodness, expediency, and the conflict between the two
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's last major work, written in 44 BC for his son Marcus, then studying at Athens: a Stoic-inspired guide to what is morally right, what is expedient, and how to choose when the two seem to clash. Walter Miller's translation for the Loeb Classical Library, with the chapter numbers kept as plain leading numbers.

works.title: On the Orator (De Oratore)
works.subtitle: Three books on the making of the perfect orator, in dialogue between Crassus, Antonius and their friends
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's dialogue on eloquence, written in 55 BC and set in 91 BC at the Tusculan villa of the orator Lucius Crassus. Crassus and Marcus Antonius, with Scaevola, Catulus, Cotta and Sulpicius, discuss what the perfect orator must know: his learning, the invention and arrangement of his matter, the use of wit, and the style and delivery of his speech. J. S. Watson's translation, with the chapter numbers kept as plain leading numbers.

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume I
works.subtitle: Letters from 68 to 52 BC, including the letters of the exile
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The first volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence: letters to Atticus, to his brother Quintus and to friends, from his candidacy for the praetorship to the year before the civil war, including the letters written in exile.

sections.title: Letters in Exile and After (58–52 BC)

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume II
works.subtitle: Letters from 51 to 49 BC, from Cicero's journey to Cilicia to the outbreak of the civil war
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The second volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence, carrying on the numbering of the first: Cicero's journey to Cilicia and his governorship of the province, the letters of his return to Italy, and the correspondence of the opening months of the civil war between Caesar and Pompey, to Atticus, to Tiro, to Terentia, to Caelius, to Appius Claudius Pulcher and to many others.

sections.title: Letters of 50 BC: The Proconsulate and the Return
Letters of 49 BC: The Outbreak of the Civil War

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume III
works.subtitle: Letters from 48 to 44 BC, from Pompey's camp in Epirus to the eve of Caesar's murder
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The third volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence, carrying on the numbering of the second: the letters from Pompey's camp in Epirus and the long wait at Brundisium after Pharsalia, through the years of Caesar's dictatorship, Cicero's retirement to his villas, his divorce, the death of his daughter Tullia and his consolation in philosophical writing, down to the winter of 44 BC. Addressed to Atticus, Terentia, Tiro, Varro, Papirius Paetus, Servius Sulpicius, Cassius and many others.

sections.title: Letters of 48 BC: Epirus and Brundisium
Letters of 47 BC: Brundisium and the Return to Italy
Letters of 46 BC: Rome under Caesar
Letters of 45 BC: Tullia's Death and the Philosophical Works
Letters of 44 BC: The Months before the Ides of March

works.title: The Letters of Cicero, Volume IV
works.subtitle: Letters from the Ides of March 44 BC to July 43 BC, from Caesar's murder to the eve of the second triumvirate
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The fourth and last volume of Shuckburgh's chronological translation of Cicero's correspondence, carrying on the numbering of the third: the letters written after Caesar's assassination on the Ides of March 44 BC. They follow Cicero's retreat to his country villas, his growing quarrel with Antony and the Philippics, the war at Mutina, and the last anxious exchanges with Brutus, Cassius, Decimus Brutus, Plancus and Lepidus, down to the summer of 43 BC. Addressed to Atticus, Tiro, Cornificius and many others, with letters to Cicero from the generals and the conspirators themselves.

sections.title: Letters of 44 BC: After the Ides of March
Letters of 44 BC: The Break with Antony
Letters of 43 BC: The Philippics and Mutina
Letters of 43 BC: Decimus Brutus, Plancus, Lepidus and the Last Letters

works.title: On Divination (De Divinatione)
works.subtitle: A dialogue on whether the future can be foretold: Quintus defends divination, and Cicero answers him
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Written in 44 BC, shortly before Caesar's death, De Divinatione is the companion to Cicero's On the Nature of the Gods. In Book I his brother Quintus defends every kind of divination, from the entrails of victims and the flight of birds to dreams and prophetic frenzy, on Stoic grounds. In Book II Cicero, speaking as an Academic sceptic, takes the argument apart, while still upholding the religious institutions of Rome. W. A. Falconer's translation (Loeb Classical Library, 1923).

works.title: On Divination (De Divinatione)
works.subtitle: A dialogue on whether the future can be foretold: Quintus defends divination, and Cicero answers him
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Written in 44 BC, shortly before Caesar's death, De Divinatione is the companion to Cicero's On the Nature of the Gods. In Book I his brother Quintus defends every kind of divination, from the entrails of victims and the flight of birds to dreams and prophetic frenzy, on Stoic grounds. In Book II Cicero, speaking as an Academic sceptic, takes the argument apart, while still upholding the religious institutions of Rome. C. D. Yonge's literal translation (Bohn, 1853), with Cicero's chapter numbers kept at the head of paragraphs and the verses he cites set as indented blocks.

works.title: On Friendship (Laelius de Amicitia)
works.subtitle: A dialogue on the nature and laws of friendship
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's dialogue on friendship, written in 44 BC and dedicated to Atticus. The aged Laelius, mourning his friend Scipio Africanus, tells his sons-in-law what friendship is, why it rests on virtue, and what its limits and duties are. Shuckburgh's translation, with the chapter numbers kept as plain leading numbers.

works.title: On Old Age (Cato Maior de Senectute)
works.subtitle: A dialogue in which Cato the Elder, in his eighty-fourth year, defends old age before Scipio and Laelius
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's late dialogue, addressed to Atticus, in which the aged Marcus Cato answers four charges against old age: that it withdraws us from active employments, weakens the body, deprives us of pleasures, and stands near to death.

works.title: On the Commonwealth (De Re Publica, with the Dream of Scipio)
works.subtitle: Six books on the best constitution, in dialogue between Scipio Aemilianus and his friends
works.author: Cicero
works.translator: trans. Francis Barham (1841), revised by C. D. Yonge (1877)
works.blurb: Cicero's dialogue on the state, composed in 54 BC and set in 129 BC in the garden of Scipio Aemilianus, where Scipio, Laelius, Philus and their friends debate the best form of government, the history of the Roman constitution, and whether justice is the foundation of a commonwealth. The work was lost until a palimpsest was found in the Vatican in 1822, so most of it survives in gaps and fragments; the Dream of Scipio, which closes Book VI, was preserved separately by Macrobius.

works.title: On the Laws (De Legibus)
works.subtitle: A dialogue between Marcus, his brother Quintus and Atticus on the nature of law, with a code of religious and civil statutes
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's companion to his Republic, set in the grove at Arpinum. In Book I he grounds law in nature and universal reason; in Book II he lays down and expounds the laws of religion; in Book III those of the magistrates and the constitution.

works.title: On the Nature of the Gods (De Natura Deorum)
works.subtitle: A dialogue on whether the gods exist and whether they govern the world
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero's last great dialogue on religion (45 BC) stages a debate among three friends: the Epicurean Velleius argues that the gods are blessed and care nothing for mankind, the Stoic Balbus defends providence and the divine order of the cosmos, and the Academic Cotta, speaking for Cicero's own sceptical school, dismantles both. Cicero himself, as narrator, leans to the Stoic view as the more probable.

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume I
works.subtitle: For Quinctius, For Sextus Roscius, For Quintus Roscius, Against Caecilius, and the Verrine Orations
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The first volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the early pleadings for Quinctius, Sextus Roscius and the actor Quintus Roscius, the Divinatio against Caecilius, and the great prosecution of Verres, governor of Sicily, in the First Pleading and the five books of the Second.

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume II
works.subtitle: For Tullius, Fonteius, Caecina, Cluentius, Rabirius, Murena, Sulla, Archias, Flaccus and Scaurus; the Manilian Law, the Agrarian Law, the Catilinarians, and the speeches after his return
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The second volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the pleadings of his consular years and after, among them the Manilian Law, the three speeches on the Agrarian Law, the four Catilinarians, and the defences of Murena, Archias, Flaccus and Sulla, with the two speeches after his return from exile.

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume III
works.subtitle: On his House, the Haruspices, Plancius, Sestius, Vatinius, Caelius, the Consular Provinces, Balbus, Piso, Milo, Postumus, Marcellus, Ligarius and King Deiotarus
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The third volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the orations of his years after exile, among them the plea for his house, the defences of Sestius, Caelius, Plancius and Milo, the invective against Piso, and the three speeches before Caesar for Marcellus, Ligarius and King Deiotarus.

sections.title: On the Answers of the Haruspices

works.title: The Orations of Cicero, Volume IV: The Philippics
works.subtitle: The fourteen speeches against Marcus Antonius
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: The fourth volume of Yonge's Bohn translation of Cicero's speeches: the fourteen Philippics of 44 and 43 BC, in which Cicero, after Caesar's murder, attacks Marcus Antonius in the Senate and before the people and urges war to save the republic, the work that cost him his life.

works.title: Tusculan Disputations
works.subtitle: Five books on death, pain, grief, the passions and the happy life
works.author: Cicero
works.blurb: Cicero, in 45 BC, recounts five days of conversation at his villa near Tusculum, in which he argues against a pupil on the great questions of the philosophical life: why death is not an evil, how pain may be borne, how grief and the other passions of the mind may be cured, and why virtue alone suffices for a happy life. The speaker's verse quotations from Ennius, Homer, the tragedians and others are given in Yonge's English renderings.

works.title: The Civile Wars betweene the Two Houses of Lancaster and Yorke
works.subtitle: Eight books in ottava rima (1609 text)
works.author: Samuel Daniel
works.blurb: Samuel Daniel's historical epic of the Wars of the Roses, from the deposition of Richard II to the marriage of Henry VII and Elizabeth of York, in eight books of eight-line stanzas. The first four books appeared in 1595; the 1609 edition corrected and continued the poem. Each book opens with a short verse argument.

works.title: Clarel: A Poem and Pilgrimage in the Holy Land
works.author: Herman Melville
works.blurb: Melville’s long narrative poem of a pilgrimage in Palestine, the longest poem in American literature: a young divinity student, Clarel, joins a company of pilgrims who travel from Jerusalem through the Judean wilderness to Mar Saba, the Dead Sea and Bethlehem, debating faith and doubt as they go. It runs to some eighteen thousand lines, chiefly in rhymed octosyllabic couplets with lyric interludes, in four parts: Jerusalem (44 cantos), The Wilderness (39), Mar Saba (32) and Bethlehem (35, the last an Epilogue).

works.title: Cleanness
works.subtitle: Clannesse
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A homily in some 1,800 alliterative lines on purity, in which God rejects those who come unclean to his presence. It tells the parable of the wedding feast and retells three Old Testament judgements: the Flood, the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, and Belshazzar's feast with the profaned vessels of the Temple.

works.title: The First Epistle of Clement to the Corinthians
works.subtitle: A letter from the Church of Rome to the Church of Corinth
works.author: Clement of Rome
works.blurb: A letter sent from the Church at Rome to the Church at Corinth, urging reconciliation after a rebellion against its presbyters; traditionally written by Clement, bishop of Rome, about AD 96.

works.title: The Second Epistle of Clement to the Corinthians
works.subtitle: An early Christian homily traditionally ascribed to Clement
works.author: Clement of Rome
works.blurb: An early Christian sermon on repentance and the keeping of the baptismal vow, handed down with the First Epistle under the name of Clement of Rome; the attribution is traditional and the work is generally thought to be by another hand.

works.title: The Tragedie of Cleopatra
works.author: Samuel Daniel
works.blurb: Daniel's Senecan closet tragedy of Cleopatra's last days, written as a companion to the Countess of Pembroke's Antonius. After Antony's death, Cleopatra, shut in her monument in Alexandria, resolves to die rather than be led in Octavius Caesar's triumph. Proculeius and Dolabella urge her to yield, her secretary Seleucus betrays her hoard, and her son Caesario is sent away and falls victim to his tutor Rodon's treachery. She feigns submission, performs her rites at Antony's tomb, and dies of an asp brought in a basket of figs. A chorus of Egyptians closes each act, and the play opens with a verse dedication to Mary Sidney, Countess of Pembroke.

works.title: Cligés
works.subtitle: Cligés
works.author: Chrétien de Troyes
works.blurb: A Greek prince of Arthur's line and his love for Fenice, framed as an answer to the Tristan story.

works.title: The Cloud-Messenger
works.subtitle: Meghaduta
works.author: Kalidasa
works.blurb: An exiled Yaksha begs a passing rain-cloud to carry a message of love across India to his wife in the Himalayas.

works.title: Dipsychus
works.subtitle: A verse drama in two parts
works.author: Arthur Hugh Clough
works.blurb: In Venice a young man, scrupulous and unsure of his faith, is shadowed by a cynical Spirit who urges him to enjoy the world, take a profession and make terms with the way things are. Dipsychus answers in blank verse, lyric and song, and at last yields in part, with reservations.

works.title: Colombe's Birthday: A Play
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A play in five acts. On her birthday Colombe, Duchess of Juliers and Cleves, learns that her right to the duchy is disputed by her cousin Prince Berthold; her courtiers desert her, and only the poor advocate Valence, who has come to plead for his town, stays true. The question is whether she will keep a crown or find a love.

works.title: The Columbiad
works.subtitle: A Poem in Ten Books
works.author: Joel Barlow
works.blurb: Barlow's patriotic epic on the American Republic: the imprisoned Columbus is shown, in vision, the history and future of the New World by the genius Hesper, in ten books of heroic couplets.

works.title: La Comédie de la mort
works.author: Théophile Gautier
works.blurb: Gautier's first major collection of verse, dominated by the long two-part meditation on death in life and life in death, with a gallery of shorter poems on art, love and melancholy.

works.title: The Comedy of Errors
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Two sets of identical twins, the sons of the Syracusan merchant Egeon and their twin servants, separated by shipwreck in infancy, are drawn into the same day in Ephesus. Mistaken for one another by wives, friends, a goldsmith and a courtesan, they bring on beatings, arrests and a supposed madness, until the Abbess who shelters one of them proves to be Egeon's long-lost wife, and the family is reunited.

works.title: Comus
works.subtitle: A Mask Presented at Ludlow Castle
works.author: John Milton
works.blurb: A masque of chastity and temptation, performed at Ludlow Castle in 1634 — a Lady lost in the wood and the enchanter Comus.

works.title: Conary
works.author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
works.blurb: Ferguson's blank-verse retelling of the destruction of the hostel of Da-Derga and the death of King Conary Mor.

works.title: Confessio Amantis
works.subtitle: Tales of the Seven Deadly Sins
works.author: John Gower
works.blurb: A lover confesses to Venus's priest Genius, who works through the Seven Deadly Sins with a great gathering of exemplary tales — classical, biblical, and romance — in eight books of octosyllabic couplets.

works.title: Congal
works.subtitle: A Poem in Five Books
works.author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
works.blurb: Ferguson's five-book heroic poem of Congal Claen, King of Ulster, and the battle of Moira (Moyra) in the seventh century.

works.title: The Conquest of Canaan
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Eleven Books
works.author: Timothy Dwight
works.blurb: Timothy Dwight's biblical epic in eleven books, the first American epic poem, follows Joshua's campaigns against Ai, Gibeon and the Canaanite kings in heroic couplets, with the love of the young warrior Irad and the maiden Selima woven through the war and a prophetic vision of later history in Book X.

works.title: The Conquest of Granada by the Spaniards
works.subtitle: Almanzor and Almahide: A Tragedy, Parts I and II
works.author: John Dryden
works.blurb: Dryden's rhymed heroic tragedy of the last days of Moorish Granada: the invincible Almanzor, a stranger in the city, falls in love with Almahide, the wife of King Boabdelin, while the Zegrys and Abencerrages feud, Lyndaraxa schemes for a throne, and Ferdinand and Isabella besiege the walls. In Part II the banished Almanzor returns, Almahide's honour is tried by combat, and Almanzor is revealed as the Duke of Arcos's long-lost son.

works.title: Constance
works.subtitle: or, The Portrait
works.author: Edward Bulwer Lytton
works.blurb: A narrative poem in five parts, in heroic couplets, of love and fate begun in a portrait and played out on an English country estate.

works.title: The Tragedy of Coriolanus
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Caius Martius, the proudest soldier in Rome, wins the name Coriolanus by taking the Volscian city of Corioles, but his contempt for the common people makes him unfit for the consulship he is pressed to seek. Tricked and banished by the tribunes Sicinius and Brutus, he goes over to his old enemy Tullus Aufidius and marches on Rome at the head of a Volscian army. Only the pleading of his mother Volumnia, his wife Virgilia and his son turns him back, and the peace he makes costs him his life at Aufidius's hands.

works.title: Count Basil
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Joanna Baillie
works.blurb: Count Basil, a young general in the Emperour's service, is kept at Mantua by his love for Victoria, the Duke's daughter, while the Duke and his minister Gauriceio plot to turn his troops against him. Basil wins the mutinous soldiers back, but when the Imperial army wins the battle of Pavia without him he can bear the shame no longer and shoots himself in a cave, dying in his friend Rosinberg's arms. This is the tragedy of love in Baillie's Plays on the Passions.

works.title: Count Julian: A Tragedy
works.author: Walter Savage Landor
works.blurb: Count Julian, the Spanish governor who has brought the Moors into Spain to avenge the dishonour of his daughter Covilla by King Roderigo, finds that his vengeance has delivered his country to the invaders. Landor's blank-verse tragedy follows Julian between the Moorish princes Muza and Abdalazis, the repentant Roderigo and the bishop Opas, as the cost of his revenge falls on his family and on Spain.

works.title: The Countess Cathleen
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: In an Irish famine of old times, two demons disguised as merchants buy the starving peasants' souls for gold. The young Countess Cathleen sells her own soul to ransom theirs, while the poet Aleel, who loves her, looks on in anguish. Yeats's first long verse play moves from the peasants' hut to her great hall and back, and ends with a vision of the soul's pardon.

works.title: The Course of Time
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Ten Books
works.author: Robert Pollok
works.blurb: Robert Pollok's blank-verse epic in ten books, in which a bard of Paradise tells a newly arrived spirit the history of mankind from the Creation to the Last Judgement; published months before the young Scottish poet's death, it went through many editions.

works.title: The Courtship of Miles Standish
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: Longfellow's hexameter tale of the Plymouth Colony, in which Miles Standish sends the young John Alden to woo Priscilla Mullins for him, and she asks why he does not speak for himself.

sections.title: V. The Sailing of the May Flower
VII. The March of Miles Standish

works.title: Csongor és Tünde
works.subtitle: Színjáték öt felvonásban
works.author: Mihály Vörösmarty
works.blurb: A fairy-tale verse drama in five acts: the young hero Csongor searches the world for the fairy Tünde, whom he loved at first sight, and meets three wanderers, a witch and devils on his way.

works.title: The Cup
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: Synorix, a Galatian exile serving Rome, is obsessed with Camma, the wife of the tetrarch Sinnatus, and sends her a cup from the temple of Artemis; when Sinnatus is murdered, Synorix plots to force her to marry him. Camma, now a priestess of Artemis, feigns consent and brings him to the altar, where the marriage cup is poisoned. She dies with her enemy, avenged and faithful to her husband.

works.title: The Curse of Kehama
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: A Hindu mythological epic in twenty-four sections, in irregular rhymed stanzas: the Rajah Kehama curses the peasant Ladurlad, who is drawn into a pursuit that reaches the Swerga and the hell of Padalon.

works.title: The History of the Wars of Alexander
works.subtitle: Books III–X, translated by John Digby, 1714
works.author: Quintus Curtius Rufus
works.blurb: Curtius's Latin history of Alexander the Great, from the war in Asia Minor after the Granicus to the king's death at Babylon and the division of his empire (the first two books and several passages are lost), in John Digby's English of 1714.

works.title: The Cyclops
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Odysseus, landing on Sicily, bargains with the old satyr Silenus for food and wine, only to fall into the hands of the one-eyed giant Polyphemus. The only complete satyr play to survive, here in Coleridge's literal prose.

works.title: Κύκλωψ (Kyklops)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Odysseus, driven by winds to the coast of Sicily, finds the old satyr Silenus and his sons labouring as slaves of the one-eyed giant Polyphemus. He offers Maron's wine in exchange for food; Silenus, delighted, sells his master's lambs and cheeses on the sly. Polyphemus returns, hears the satyrs' lies, and drinks the wine with relish, declaring his belly the only god he serves. When the giant falls asleep drunk, Odysseus, who has given his name as Nobody, blinds him with a burning stake while the satyrs, hanging back, only cheer. The only satyr play to survive entire. The Greek text is given in the order of the Nauck edition, so that it pairs with the English translations of the same play.

works.title: The Cyclops
works.subtitle: A Satyric Drama
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Odysseus and his men, landing on Sicily, bargain with the old satyr Silenus for food and wine, only to fall into the hands of the one-eyed giant Polyphemus. Euripides' only surviving satyr play, the lone complete example of the genre, is rendered by Shelley in 1819 and was first printed after his death.

works.title: The Tragedie of Cymbeline
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Cymbeline, king of Britain, banishes his daughter Imogen's secret husband Posthumus Leonatus. Tricked by the Italian Iachimo into believing her unfaithful, Posthumus orders her death; she flees in boy's disguise to Wales, where she finds her two long-lost brothers, and the play's tangled threads of war with Rome, the Queen's poison and a divine vision resolve in reconciliation. It includes the songs 'Hark, hark! the lark' and 'Fear no more the heat o' the sun'.

works.title: Cynegetica
works.subtitle: The Chase
works.author: Oppian
works.blurb: A didactic poem in four books on hunting: the hunter, his horses and hounds, and the wild beasts of the chase, addressed to the emperor Caracalla.

works.title: The Dance to Death
works.subtitle: A Historical Tragedy in Five Acts
works.author: Emma Lazarus
works.blurb: Nordhausen, May 1349: as the Black Death spreads, the Jews of the free city are accused of poisoning the wells. Susskind von Orb, a respected Jew, sees his daughter Liebhaid loved by Prince William of Meissen, while the vengeful Governor Henry Schnetzen, whose wife was once burned through Susskind, secures the Landgrave's order for their destruction. Lazarus's verse tragedy, dedicated to George Eliot, ends with the community choosing a martyr's dance of death.

works.title: Daniel
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A verse paraphrase of the Book of Daniel: Nebuchadnezzar's pride and madness, the three youths in the fiery furnace, and Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall.

works.title: Daniel (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a verse paraphrase of the Book of Daniel: Nebuchadnezzar's pride and madness, the three youths in the fiery furnace, and Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall.

works.title: Dante at Verona
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: Rossetti's narrative poem of Dante in exile at the court of Can Grande, torn between the Florence that cast him out and the Beatrice he lost.

works.title: The Economy of Vegetation
works.subtitle: The Botanic Garden, Part I
works.author: Erasmus Darwin
works.blurb: Darwin's four-canto didactic poem in heroic couplets, in which Nymphs of Fire, Gnomes, Nymphs of Water and Sylphs preside over the natural philosophy of heat, earth, water and air.

works.title: The Loves of the Plants
works.subtitle: The Botanic Garden, Part II
works.author: Erasmus Darwin
works.blurb: Darwin's four-canto poem in heroic couplets, in which the botanic Muse presents the Linnaean sexual system of plants as a comedy of courtships, marriages and rivalries among flowers.

works.title: The Daughters of Troy
works.subtitle: The Trojan Women
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Troy has fallen. In the Greek camp the captive women of the royal house wait to be shared out among the victors: Hecuba is given to Odysseus, the prophetess Kassandra to Agamemnon, and Andromache to Akhilleus' son. Their one remaining hope is taken from them when the Greeks decide to hurl Hector's little son from the walls, and the play ends as the city burns and the captives are driven down to the ships.

works.title: The Love of King David and Fair Bethsabe
works.subtitle: With the Tragedy of Absalon
works.author: George Peele
works.blurb: George Peele's verse tragedy of the Old Testament king. David spies Bethsabe bathing, sends her husband Urias to his death in the front line, and is rebuked by the prophet Nathan; his son Amnon then ravishes Thamar, Absalon avenges her by killing Amnon and finally rebels against his father, and dies hanging by his hair in the oak at Ephraim. The play opens with the song 'Hot sun, cool fire' and ends with David's lament over Absalon.

works.title: Davideis
works.subtitle: A Sacred Poem of the Troubles of David
works.author: Abraham Cowley
works.blurb: Cowley's unfinished biblical epic in rhymed couplets, telling of David's youth and his persecution by King Saul, in four books.

works.title: The Dawn in Britain
works.subtitle: In twenty-four books
works.author: Charles M. Doughty
works.blurb: Doughty's blank-verse epic of Britain from the first settlement to the Roman conquest, told in twenty-four books in a deliberately archaic, Spenserian English.

works.title: De Contemptu Mundi (Latin)
works.subtitle: Books I and II of the Latin satire in dactylic hexameters
works.author: Bernard of Cluny
works.blurb: Bernard of Cluny's Latin poem on the contempt of the world, in leonine-tailed dactylic hexameters; Book I opens with 'Hora novissima, tempora pessima sunt, vigilemus' and contains the praise of the heavenly city, 'Urbs Syon aurea'.

works.title: De Monfort
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Joanna Baillie
works.blurb: De Monfort, a proud German nobleman, is eaten up by hatred of Rezenvelt, a rival whose easy fortune and ready praise he cannot forgive. His sister Jane tries to reconcile them, but a false report that Rezenvelt means to marry her drives him past endurance, and he murders his enemy in a wood near a convent. Taken by the monks, he dies of remorse in his sister's arms. This is the tragedy of hatred in Baillie's Plays on the Passions.

works.title: De partu Virginis
works.subtitle: On the Virgin's Childbirth
works.author: Jacopo Sannazaro
works.blurb: Sannazaro's Christian epic in three books, worked on for some twenty years and published in 1526: the Annunciation, the Nativity and the visit of the shepherds, and the prophecies of the Passion, told in Virgilian hexameters. It made him the 'Christian Virgil' of the Renaissance.

works.title: De reditu suo
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus
works.blurb: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus's elegiac journey home from Rome to Gaul in 417, written in the shadow of the Gothic invasions: a hymn to Rome, a travel narrative of the Tuscan coast, and a fragment of a second book.

works.title: De Rerum Natura (Latin)
works.author: Lucretius
works.blurb: The Latin original of Lucretius's didactic poem, in six books of hexameters, setting out the atomic physics and ethics of Epicurus.

works.title: The Death of Wallenstein
works.author: Friedrich Schiller
works.blurb: Wallenstein, dismissed by the Emperor and urged by his officers toward revolt, hesitates between the stars and his own ambition and opens talks with the Swedes. Max Piccolomini chooses duty over love, and dies in battle; Thekla follows him in grief; at Egra Wallenstein is murdered by his own officers.

works.title: The Deformed Transformed
works.subtitle: A Drama
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's unfinished drama, dated Pisa, 1822, and first published in 1824, of which only two parts and the opening chorus of a third were completed. The hunchback Arnold, scorned by his mother, accepts from a mysterious Stranger a new and beautiful body, and with the Stranger, who takes the form of his former shape, joins the army of the Constable Bourbon at the sack of Rome in 1527. Byron's advertisement names an old novel, The Three Brothers, and Goethe's Faust as sources.

works.title: Deirdre
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: Sir Samuel Ferguson
works.blurb: Ferguson's blank-verse drama of the flight, return and death of Deirdre and the sons of Usnach, set between Glen Etive and the House of the Red Branch at Emania.

works.title: Deirdre
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: Fergus brings Naisi and Deirdre back to Ireland from exile, on the promise of King Conchubar's pardon. Waiting in a guest-house in a wood, while musicians sing and hint at treachery, the lovers learn that Conchubar means to take Deirdre for himself. The tragedy of the old Irish tale ends in a trap, a death, and a queen's last choice.

works.title: Demeter
works.subtitle: A Mask
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's mask on the rape of Persephone and Demeter's search for her, in three parts: Hades carries Persephone off from the flowery valley below Enna, the Oceanides mourn and Demeter defies Zeus, and a year later Hermes leads Persephone back and mother and daughter are reconciled.

works.title: Демон (Demon)
works.subtitle: Восточная повесть (An Eastern tale), in the original Russian
works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: Lermontov's narrative poem of the fallen spirit who loves the Georgian princess Tamara, kills her bridegroom, wins her with his speeches, and loses her soul to an angel at her death, in its original Russian.

works.title: The Demon
works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: A fallen spirit loves the Georgian princess Tamara, kills her bridegroom, wins her with his speeches, and loses her soul to an angel at her death.

works.title: The Demon
works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: A fallen spirit loves the Georgian princess Tamara, kills her bridegroom, wins her with his speeches, and loses her soul to an angel at her death.

works.title: Against Leptines (Or. XX)
works.subtitle: Against the repeal of grants of immunity, 355 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: An early speech in a public case, defending the grants of exemption from public services that Athens had made to its benefactors, against the law of Leptines to abolish them.

works.title: Answer to Philip's Letter (Or. XI)
works.subtitle: A reply urging war with Macedon, c. 340 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: A short speech replying to Philip's letter and urging the Athenians to prepare for war and seek allies. Its authorship is doubtful.

works.title: On the Chersonese (Or. VIII)
works.subtitle: Diopeithes and the Chersonese, 341 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes defends the general Diopeithes and urges Athens to resist Philip in the Chersonese.

works.title: On the Crown (Or. XVIII)
works.subtitle: The speech in reply to Aeschines, 330 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' defence of his public career against Aeschines' attack on the proposal to crown him.

works.title: On the Crown (Or. XVIII)
works.subtitle: The speech in reply to Aeschines, 330 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.translator: trans. C. A. Vince and J. H. Vince (1926)
works.blurb: Demosthenes' defence of his public career against Aeschines' attack on the proposal to crown him.

works.title: On the Embassy (Or. XIX)
works.subtitle: Against Aeschines on the false embassy, 343 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' prosecution of Aeschines for misconduct as an ambassador to Philip.

works.title: On the Embassy (Or. XIX)
works.subtitle: The speech against Aeschines on the false embassy, 343 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.translator: trans. C. A. Vince and J. H. Vince (1926)
works.blurb: Demosthenes' prosecution of Aeschines for treachery and misconduct on the embassies that negotiated the Peace of Philocrates.

works.title: The First Olynthiac (Or. I)
works.subtitle: Help for Olynthus, 349 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: The first of three speeches urging Athens to send help to Olynthus against Philip.

works.title: The First Philippic (Or. IV)
works.subtitle: The first speech against Philip of Macedon, 351 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' first attack on Philip of Macedon, calling on the Athenians to raise a proper citizen force.

works.title: Fourth Philippic (Or. X)
works.subtitle: Against Philip and for resistance, c. 341 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: An appeal to the Athenians to meet Philip's advance with action rather than speeches, and to fund the war. Its authenticity has been questioned, and part of it repeats the Third Philippic.

works.title: On Halonnesus (Or. VII)
works.subtitle: Against Philip's letter about the island, 342 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: A speech answering Philip's letter on the island of Halonnesus, which he offered to give the Athenians rather than restore. Traditionally ascribed to Demosthenes, though the attribution is doubtful.

works.title: For the Megalopolitans (Or. XVI)
works.subtitle: Athens and the Arcadian city, c. 353 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes argues that Athens should support Megalopolis against Sparta while keeping Thebes weak.

works.title: On the Naval Boards (Or. XIV)
works.subtitle: The Athenian navy and the Persian threat, 354 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' first public speech, urging Athens not to rush into war with Persia and proposing a reform of the Boards that equipped the fleet.

works.title: On Organization (Or. XIII)
works.subtitle: On the reform of the state's finances and forces, c. 353 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: An early political speech urging the Athenians to organise their funds and military forces, and to hold their politicians to account.

works.title: On the Peace (Or. V)
works.subtitle: The Peace of Philocrates, 346 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes counsels the Athenians to keep the peace made with Philip rather than go to war over Delphi.

works.title: Philip's Letter (Or. XII)
works.subtitle: The letter of Philip II to the Athenians, c. 340 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: The letter in which Philip of Macedon sets out his grievances against Athens. Transmitted among the speeches of Demosthenes, it is generally thought not to be his.

works.title: For the Freedom of the Rhodians (Or. XV)
works.subtitle: The Rhodian democracy, c. 351 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes urges the Athenians to help the Rhodian democrats against a Carian-backed oligarchy.

sections.title: For the Freedom of the Rhodians (Or. XV)

works.title: The Second Olynthiac (Or. II)
works.subtitle: Help for Olynthus, 349 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: The second speech urging Athens to support Olynthus against the growing power of Philip.

works.title: The Second Philippic (Or. VI)
works.subtitle: Philip and the Peace, 344 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes warns the Athenians against Philip's intrigues in the Peloponnese.

works.title: The Third Olynthiac (Or. III)
works.subtitle: Help for Olynthus and reform at home, 349 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: The third Olynthiac, urging military aid for Olynthus and the reform of the Theoric Fund.

works.title: The Third Philippic (Or. IX)
works.subtitle: The call to resist Philip, 341 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: Demosthenes' call for Athens to rouse the Greek states against Philip.

works.title: On the Treaty with Alexander (Or. XVII)
works.subtitle: Against the terms of the Macedonian settlement, 331 BC
works.author: Demosthenes
works.blurb: A speech on Alexander's breaches of the general peace and the oaths sworn under it. It is not generally accepted as the work of Demosthenes.

sections.title: On the Treaty with Alexander (Or. XVII)

works.title: Des Knaben Wunderhorn
works.subtitle: Alte deutsche Lieder: a selection from the second volume (1808)
works.author: Achim von Arnim and Clemens Brentano (eds.)
works.blurb: The great Romantic anthology of German folk songs, broadsides and ballads, gathered and freely reworked by Arnim and Brentano, and the source of many of Mahler's songs.

sections.title: Schwimm hin, schwimm her du Ringlein
Wettstreit des Kukuks mit der Nachtigal
Babeli sieht den Wald vor lauter Bäume nicht

works.title: Deutschland. Ein Wintermährchen
works.subtitle: Neue Gedichte (1844)
works.author: Heinrich Heine
works.blurb: Heine's satirical verse journey home from exile in Paris to Hamburg in twenty-seven cantos, mocking Prussian authority and German nationalism. Original German text, 1844.

works.title: The Didache, or Teaching of the Twelve Apostles
works.subtitle: The Lord's teaching to the heathen by the Twelve Apostles
works.author: The Apostolic Fathers
works.blurb: An anonymous early Christian church manual, rediscovered in 1873, setting out the Two Ways, rules for baptism, fasting, the Eucharist and church order.

works.title: Dido
works.subtitle: Translated from Metastasio's Didone abbandonata
works.author: Pietro Metastasio
works.blurb: The tragedy of Dido abandoned by Aeneas, in the blank verse and songs of John Hoole's translation of 1800.

works.title: Didone abbandonata
works.subtitle: Dramma per musica
works.author: Pietro Metastasio
works.blurb: Metastasio's tragedy of Dido and Aeneas in three acts, the opera libretto that made his name.

works.title: Βασίλειος Διγενὴς Ἀκρίτης
works.subtitle: Digenis Akritas, the Trebizond version (ed. Sathas and Legrand, 1875)
works.author: Anonymous (Byzantine Greek)
works.blurb: The Byzantine frontier epic of Basil Digenes Akrites, whose Arab father abjured his faith for a Greek bride, in the Trebizond manuscript: the lament of the five brothers, the emir's journey into Romania, the hero's boyhood hunts, his duels with the apelatai and Maximo, his palace on the Euphrates and his death.

works.title: The Historical Library, Volume I: Books I–V and XI–XIV
works.subtitle: Volume I: Books I–V and XI–XIV, with Booth's translation of 1700 as reprinted in 1814
works.author: Diodorus Siculus
works.blurb: Diodorus Siculus's universal history, from the myths and marvels of Egypt, Asia and early Greece to the Greek affairs of the fourth century BC, in George Booth's English prose (volume I).

works.title: The Historical Library, Volume II: Books XV–XX and Fragments
works.subtitle: Volume II: Books XV–XX and the fragments of the lost books
works.author: Diodorus Siculus
works.blurb: Diodorus Siculus's history of Greece, Sicily and the wars of Alexander's successors (Books XV–XX), with the fragments of the later books, in George Booth's English prose (volume II).

works.title: Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Books I–X
works.subtitle: Diogenes Laertius, lives, sayings and doctrines of the Greek philosophers from Thales to Epicurus
works.author: Diogenes Laertius
works.blurb: The chief ancient source for the lives, sayings and doctrines of the Greek philosophers, from the Seven Sages and the Ionians through Socrates, Plato, Aristotle and the Cynics and Stoics to Pythagoras, the Sceptics and Epicurus, in R. D. Hicks's complete English of 1925, in ten books.

works.title: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, Books I–V
works.subtitle: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of the Greek philosophers from Thales to Heraclides of Pontus
works.author: Diogenes Laertius
works.blurb: The chief ancient source for the lives and sayings of the Greek philosophers, from the Seven Wise Men through Socrates, Plato and the Academy to Aristotle and his school, in C. D. Yonge's English prose of 1853.

works.title: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, Books VI–X
works.subtitle: Antisthenes and Diogenes through Epicurus
works.author: Diogenes Laertius
works.blurb: Laertius's lives of the Cynics, Stoics, Pythagoreans, Eleatics, Sceptics and Epicurus, with the three letters and the maxims of Epicurus, in C. D. Yonge's English prose of 1853.

works.title: La Divina Commedia
works.subtitle: Italian original
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's three-part poem of Hell, Purgatory and Paradise in the original Italian terza rima: 100 cantos, 34 in the Inferno and 33 each in the Purgatorio and Paradiso.

works.title: The Divine Comedy
works.subtitle: La Divina Commedia
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Cary's blank-verse version of the Commedia, the standard English Dante of the nineteenth century, rendered canto by canto in Miltonic pentameter.

works.title: The Divine Comedy
works.subtitle: La Divina Commedia
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's vision of the afterlife in a hundred cantos, from the dark wood through Inferno and Purgatorio to the Paradiso, in Longfellow's blank-verse tercets.

works.title: The Divine Comedy (Norton)
works.subtitle: Translated by Charles Eliot Norton
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: A literal, unrhymed prose version of the Commedia by the Harvard scholar Charles Eliot Norton, long valued by students for its fidelity to Dante's sense; each canto opens with a brief summary of its argument.

works.title: The Divine Comedy (Plumptre)
works.subtitle: Translated by E. H. Plumptre
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.translator: trans. E. H. Plumptre (1886–87; text of the Isbister edition, 1899)
works.blurb: The Commedia in English terza rima by Edward Hayes Plumptre, Dean of Wells, keeping Dante's three-line stanzas and line count; each cantica was published with extensive notes, which are omitted here.

works.title: Christus: A Mystery. Part I: The Divine Tragedy
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: The first part of Longfellow's trilogy Christus: A Mystery, a dramatic poem on the life of Christ. After an Introitus in which an Angel carries the prophet Habakkuk to Babylon, three Passovers follow the Gospel story from John the Baptist's preaching and the temptation in the wilderness through the miracles, the raising of Lazarus, the Last Supper, trial and Crucifixion, to the appearances after the Resurrection. The Epilogue gives the Apostles' Creed, spoken line by line by the Twelve. Part II is The Golden Legend.

works.author: Guillaume de Salluste Du Bartas
works.blurb: Du Bartas's Huguenot epic of the Creation and of sacred history, in Sylvester's rhyming English couplets: the seven Days of the First Week, and four Days of the Second Week from Adam to David.

works.blurb: Palamas's national-lyric epic of a Gypsy-minstrel who builds, wanders and loves; the first three of its twelve Logoi (The Coming, The Worker, Love).

works.title: Domesday Book
works.author: Edgar Lee Masters
works.blurb: A verse narrative in blank verse that opens with a coroner's inquest into the death of Elenor Murray, a nurse found dead by the Illinois River. Witness after witness is called, and each account lays bare the hidden lives of a Midwestern town and of America.

works.title: Don Juan
works.author: Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's unfinished comic epic in ottava rima follows a young Spaniard through seductions, shipwreck, war and the courts of Europe, mocking cant, politics and poetry itself along the way.

works.title: The Doom of Devorgoil: A Melo-Drama
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: In the decayed Castle of Devorgoil the impoverished Baron Oswald, his peasant-born wife Eleanor, their daughter Flora and her cousin Katleen are visited on a stormy night by a pedantic young preacher, the huntsman Leonard and the old beggar Durward, while Katleen and the forester Blackthorn play goblin tricks. An old prophecy says the armour of the wicked Lord Erick will fall at a feast, and the spirit of Erick offers Oswald a hoard of treasure if he will put away his wife. He refuses, the lost key is found, and the treasure passes to Leonard, the true Heir of Aglionby, who is to marry Flora.

works.title: Dorottya, vagyis a dámák diadalma a fársángon
works.subtitle: Furcsa vitézi versezet négy könyvben
works.author: Mihály Csokonai Vitéz
works.blurb: Csokonai's mock-heroic epic in four books, running from dinner to dawn on the last day of Carnival, in which the aged spinster Dorottya leads an army of women against the young men and the Carnival revellers. Rhymed couplets, with an archaic-spelled summary preceding each book.

works.title: The Dream of Gerontius
works.author: John Henry Newman
works.blurb: Newman's dramatic poem of a dying man's passage through death and judgment, in seven parts: the prayers at the deathbed, the soul's journey with its guardian Angel, the Demons, the choirs of Angelicals, and the soul's entry into Purgatory.

works.title: The Dreaming of the Bones
works.subtitle: A play for dancers
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: In the aftermath of the Easter Rising of 1916, a young man fleeing from the Dublin fighting meets two strangers among the ruins of Corcomroe Abbey in County Clare. They are the ghosts of Dermot and Dervorgilla, whose adultery brought the Norman invasion to Ireland seven hundred years before, and they ask for his forgiveness.

works.blurb: Thirty-five lays of Fionn mac Cumhaill and the Fiana, from the abduction of Eargna to Goll's war-vaunt, in Eoin MacNeill's 1908 English version of the Book of the Lays of Fionn.

works.title: The Duchess of Malfi
works.author: John Webster
works.blurb: The widowed Duchess of Malfi secretly marries her steward Antonio against the commands of her brothers, the violent Duke Ferdinand and the scheming Cardinal. Their spy Bosola uncovers the marriage, and the brothers imprison, torment and finally strangle her, along with her children and her maid. Bosola, sickened by the deed, turns on his masters, and the play ends in a bloodbath of revenge and ruin.

works.title: The Earthly Paradise
works.subtitle: Parts II–IV: May to February
works.author: William Morris
works.blurb: Morris's frame story of wanderers who, seeking an earthly paradise, settle in a western city whose elders swap classical and medieval tales with them month by month. Part II holds the tales of Cupid and Psyche, Alcestis, the Son of Croesus, Pygmalion and Ogier the Dane. Parts III and IV add the autumn and winter tales: the Death of Paris, the Land East of the Sun and West of the Moon, Acontius and Cydippe, the Man who never Laughed Again, Rhodope, the Lovers of Gudrun, the Golden Apples, Aslaug, Bellerophon, the Ring given to Venus and the Hill of Venus.

works.subtitle: Part I: The Prologue, March and April
works.author: William Morris
works.blurb: Morris's frame story of Norse wanderers who sail in search of the earthly paradise and end their days in a western city whose elders trade tales with them month by month. Part I holds the Apology (‘the idle singer of an empty day’), the Prologue in which the wanderers tell their own story, and the tales of March and April: Atalanta's Race, the Man Born to be King, the Doom of King Acrisius and the Proud King.

works.title: Eclogae
works.subtitle: Two Latin eclogues to Giovanni del Virgilio
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's two Latin pastoral poems, written near the end of his life in reply to the Bolognese humanist Giovanni del Virgilio, who had urged him to abandon the vernacular and be crowned poet with a Latin work: Dante, as Tityrus, declines the invitation and promises the completed Paradiso, then in the second eclogue weighs a journey to Bologna against the dangers of 'Polyphemus'.

works.title: The Troublesome Reign and Lamentable Death of Edward the Second
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: Edward II, newly king, recalls his favourite Gaveston from exile and showers him with titles, driving the barons under the younger Mortimer into open revolt. After Gaveston is killed and the king turns to the Spensers, Queen Isabella and Mortimer invade, depose Edward and have him murdered in Berkeley Castle. His son, the young Edward III, then brings Mortimer to the block.

works.subtitle: Translated from the Papyri, XVIIIth to XIXth Dynasty
works.author: Ancient Egyptian (anonymous)
works.blurb: Four tales from the New Kingdom papyri: the stratagem by which Tahutia took Joppa, the prince doomed to crocodile, serpent or dog, the quarrel of the brothers Anpu and Bata, and Setna's theft of the magic book of Thoth.

works.title: الهی‌نامه (Elahi-nameh)
works.author: Farid al-Din Attar
works.blurb: Attar's Book of God, a Sufi mathnavi in rhymed couplets framed as a story: a king questions his six sons about their dearest wish, and the father answers each in turn with a sermon and illustrative tales on the vanity of desire, drawing the princes toward the one true longing, the knowledge of God.

works.title: Electra
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Orestes returns to Mycenae in disguise, sent by Apollo to avenge Agamemnon. Electra, who has mourned her murdered father for years, believes her brother dead until he reveals himself; together they kill their mother Clytemnestra and then her lover Aegisthus.

works.title: Ἠλέκτρα (Elektra)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Euripides' Elektra has been given in marriage to a poor farmer far from the palace at Argos. Her brother Orestes returns in secret with Pylades; brother and sister are reunited, and together with an old servant they lure Aigisthos and then Klytaimestra to their deaths. The Dioskouroi appear at the end to judge the matricide and to arrange the futures of the survivors. The Greek text is given in the order of the Nauck edition, so that it pairs with the English translation of the same play.

works.title: Electra
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Years after Agamemnon's murder, his daughter Electra still keeps vigil at the palace gates of Mycenae, scorned by her mother Clytaemnestra and her mother's lover Aegisthus. Her brother Orestes returns in secret with a false tale of his own death, and the siblings' recognition scene turns grief into revenge. Jebb's plain English prose carries the play's cold fury and its choral laments.

works.title: Ἠλέκτρα (Elektra)
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Years after Agamemnon's murder, Elektra mourns him in her mother's house until her brother Orestes returns in disguise, and together they avenge their father on Klytaimestra and Aigisthos. The Greek text is given in the order of the Storr edition, so that it pairs with the English prose translation of the same play.

works.title: Electra
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: In a poor peasant's cottage on the borders of Argos, Agamemnon's daughter Electra waits in squalor for her exiled brother Orestes to return and avenge their father on Klytemnestra and Aegisthus. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of recognition and vengeance in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Elene
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: Cynewulf's retelling of the legend of St. Helena, mother of the Emperor Constantine, and her journey to Jerusalem in search of the True Cross, opening with Constantine's vision of the Cross before his battle at the Milvian Bridge.

works.title: Elene (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: Cynewulf's retelling of the legend of St. Helena and her journey to Jerusalem in search of the True Cross, in the original Old English.

works.title: Emare
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Emare, daughter of the emperor Artyus, wears a marvellous robe embroidered with famous lovers; when her father conceives a sinful passion for her she is set adrift in a boat and comes ashore in Galys, where the king marries her. His mother's lies drive Emare and her child into exile at sea again, until a penitent pilgrimage to Rome reunites the whole family.

works.title: The Emigrants
works.subtitle: A Poem in Two Books
works.author: Charlotte Smith
works.blurb: Charlotte Smith's blank-verse meditation on the French Revolution and the refugee clergy and nobility who fled to the Sussex coast, set against her own grief and the English countryside.

works.title: Περὶ φύσεως · Καθαρμοί (Fragments)
works.subtitle: The verse fragments, Greek text
works.author: Empedocles
works.blurb: The surviving hexameter fragments of Empedocles of Acragas, in Greek: On Nature (the four roots, Love and Strife, the Sphere, the cycles of the cosmos) and Purifications (the daimon's exile, the golden age of Cypris, the ban on bloodshed), in the numbering of Diels.

works.title: The Fragments of Empedocles
works.subtitle: Translated into English verse
works.author: Empedocles
works.blurb: The surviving fragments of Empedocles' two hexameter poems, On Nature and The Purifications, in William Ellery Leonard's English verse: the four roots, Love and Strife, the cycles of the cosmos, and the wandering of the soul.

sections.title: Last Echoes of a Song Half Lost

works.title: Empedocles on Etna
works.subtitle: A Dramatic Poem
works.author: Matthew Arnold
works.blurb: On the slopes of Mount Etna, the young harp-player Callicles and the physician Pausanias attend the philosopher Empedocles, who is exiled, weary of men and of his own restless thought. Callicles sings of the gods and of Chiron's teaching of Akhilleus, Pausanias hopes to cure his friend, and Empedocles on the summit, in a long meditation on mind, desire and the unity of things, leaps into the crater, while Callicles' song rises from below.

works.title: Endymion
works.subtitle: A Poetic Romance
works.author: John Keats
works.blurb: Keats's four-book retelling of the myth of the shepherd prince Endymion, loved by the moon goddess and wandering the earth, sea and underworld in search of her.

works.title: Енеїда (Eneida)
works.subtitle: A travesty of Virgil's Aeneid in Ukrainian
works.author: Ivan Kotliarevsky
works.blurb: Kotliarevsky's burlesque retelling of Virgil's Aeneid in six parts, which turns the Trojans into Cossacks and is counted the first work of modern literary Ukrainian.

works.title: Annales
works.subtitle: The fragments
works.author: Quintus Ennius
works.blurb: The fragments of the first Latin epic on Roman history, in hexameters, from the fall of Troy to Ennius's own day.

works.title: The Seven Tablets of Creation
works.subtitle: Enuma Elish
works.author: Anonymous Babylonian Poets
works.blurb: The Babylonian epic of creation, in which the god Marduk slays the sea-goddess Tiamat, fashions the world from her body, and receives his fifty names.

works.title: The Epic of Hades
works.subtitle: In Three Books
works.author: Sir Lewis Morris
works.blurb: A Victorian dream-vision in three books: the poet walks through Tartarus, Hades and Olympus, hearing the shades of Greek myth tell their own stories and the gods reveal what they stand for.

works.title: The Epic Songs of Russia
works.subtitle: The Byliny of the Kiev and Novgorod Cycles
works.author: Anonymous (Russian Byliny)
works.blurb: The great heroic songs of the Russian north: Ilya of Murom and the Nightingale the Robber, Dobrynya the Dragon-slayer, Sadko beneath the sea, and the champions who defend Prince Vladimir's Kiev.

works.title: The Works of Epictetus: Discourses, Enchiridion and Fragments
works.author: Epictetus
works.blurb: The lectures of the Stoic teacher Epictetus as recorded by his pupil Arrian, with the Enchiridion, or Manual, and the surviving fragments, in Thomas Wentworth Higginson’s revision of Elizabeth Carter’s translation.

works.title: The Discourses of Epictetus
works.subtitle: with the Encheiridion and Fragments
works.author: Epictetus
works.blurb: The lectures of the Stoic teacher Epictetus as recorded by his pupil Arrian, with the Encheiridion, or Manual, and the surviving fragments, in George Long’s translation.

works.title: The Epigoniad
works.subtitle: A Poem in Nine Books
works.author: William Wilkie
works.blurb: An epic in nine books on the war of the Epigoni, the sons of the Seven, against Thebes, in heroic couplets modelled on the Iliad.

works.title: The Epistle of Barnabas
works.subtitle: Traditionally ascribed to Barnabas
works.author: The Apostolic Fathers
works.blurb: An anonymous early Christian letter of c. AD 100–130, long ascribed to Barnabas, the companion of Paul, urging a spiritual reading of the Hebrew scriptures and setting out the Two Ways.

works.title: The Epistle to Diognetus
works.subtitle: An early Christian apologetic letter
works.author: The Apostolic Fathers
works.blurb: An anonymous Greek apologetic letter to a certain Diognetus, setting out why Christians reject pagan idols and Jewish observance, how they live in the world as the soul does in the body, and what the revelation of the Son means.

works.title: Erec and Enide
works.subtitle: Erec et Enide
works.author: Chrétien de Troyes
works.blurb: The first Arthurian romance in French verse, telling how Erec wins Enide and then must prove himself again.

works.title: Erechtheus
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Algernon Charles Swinburne
works.blurb: A tragedy on the Greek model. Athens is besieged by Eumolpus and his Thracians, and an oracle demands that King Erechtheus sacrifice one of his daughters to save the city. Swinburne's choruses sing of Athens, the sea and the sun, and the play ends with Athena's promise of the city's glory.

works.title: The Erle of Tolous
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme Breton lay of about 1,220 lines: Barnard, earl of Tolous, defeats the emperor Dyaclysyon, wins a sight of the empress Beulybon through the knight Trylabas, and later, disguised as a monk, takes up her cause when two knights falsely accuse her. After the emperor's death he becomes emperor and marries her.

works.title: Eros and Psyche
works.subtitle: A narrative poem in twelve measures
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's narrative poem of Psyche and Eros, drawn from the story in Apuleius and told in seven-line stanzas across the twelve months of the year, from Psyche's earthly parentage in the spring to her reception into heaven in the winter.

works.title: اسکندرنامه (Eskandarnameh)
works.subtitle: The Persian original of Nizami's Iskandarnama: Sharafnama and Iqbalnama (Khiradnama)
works.author: Nizami Ganjavi
works.blurb: Nizami's Persian epic romance of Alexander the Great, composed between about 1194 and 1202: the Sharafnameh, the hero's conquests and travels, and the Khardnameh (Iqbalnameh), his wisdom and the sages who attend him. The original text, in Ganjoor's section order.

works.title: An Essay on Man
works.subtitle: In Four Epistles to Henry St John, Lord Bolingbroke
works.author: Alexander Pope
works.blurb: Pope’s attempt, in polished couplets, to ‘vindicate the ways of God to Man’ — four epistles on man’s place in the universe, himself, society, and happiness.

works.title: An Essay on Mind
works.author: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
works.blurb: Written when she was about twenty, Elizabeth Barrett's first published volume is a didactic poem in heroic couplets on the powers of the human mind: genius, history, science and philosophy in the first book, metaphysics, poetry and mortality in the second.

works.title: Евгений Онегин (Evgenii Onegin)
works.subtitle: A novel in verse, in the original Russian
works.author: Alexander Pushkin
works.blurb: Pushkin's verse novel of the bored St Petersburg dandy Onegin, the provincial girl Tatiana who loves him, and the duel that kills his friend Lensky, in its original Russian.

works.title: Eugene Onéguine
works.subtitle: A Romance of Russian Life in Verse
works.author: Alexander Pushkin
works.blurb: Pushkin's verse novel of the bored St Petersburg dandy Onegin, the provincial girl Tatiana who loves him, and the duel that kills his friend Lensky.

works.title: Εὐμενίδες (Eumenides)
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: The Greek text of this tragedy by Aeschylus in the Smyth Loeb edition, set out by episode and choral division, so that it can be read beside the English verse translation of the same play.

works.title: Europe: A Prophecy
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Enitharmon's eighteen-hundred-year sleep, the reign of Urizen's law over Europe, and the coming of the revolutionary fire of Orc.

works.title: Europe
works.subtitle: Lines on the War
works.author: Reginald Heber
works.blurb: Heber's verses of 1809 on the war against Napoleon, opening in a grove at Dresden and ending in hope for Spain.

works.title: Evangeline
works.subtitle: A Tale of Acadie
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A story of a young Acadian woman who is separated from her promised husband when their people are driven from their homes, and who spends her whole life searching for him.

works.title: Ève
works.author: Charles Péguy
works.blurb: Péguy's vast poem of some nineteen hundred rhymed quatrains, spoken from the mother of mankind to her children and through her to the fallen of France, among them the celebrated run beginning 'Heureux ceux qui sont morts pour la terre charnelle'.

works.title: Everyman
works.subtitle: The Summoning of Everyman
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: God, displeased that mankind has forgotten him in worldly prosperity, sends Death to summon Everyman to a reckoning. Abandoned in turn by Fellowship, Kindred and Goods, and later by Beauty, Strength, Discretion and Five-Wits, Everyman is accompanied to the grave only by Good-Deeds. The best-known English morality play, in rhyming verse of the late fifteenth century.

works.title: Epistulae ex Ponto
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid’s verse letters from exile in the original Latin: four books of epistles to friends, patrons and his wife, written from Tomis.

works.title: The Pontic Epistles
works.subtitle: Ovid's Letters from the Black Sea, Books I–IV, prose translation by Henry T. Riley
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid's four books of verse epistles from exile, each addressed by name to a friend or patron in Rome, pleading for help and describing life among the Getae, in Riley's prose.

works.title: Exodus
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A dense, martial retelling of the Israelites' flight from Egypt and crossing of the Red Sea, cast largely in the diction of Old English heroic poetry.

works.title: Exodus (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: The Old English verse of the Junius Manuscript in the Krapp and Dobbie edition: a dense, martial retelling of the Israelites' flight from Egypt and crossing of the Red Sea, cast largely in the diction of Old English heroic poetry.

works.title: Fables (Ysopet)
works.subtitle: Old French text, ed. B. de Roquefort (1820)
works.author: Marie de France
works.blurb: One hundred and three fables in Old French octosyllabic couplets, with a prologue and epilogue, in which Marie de France says she turned the tales of 'Ysopet' from English into French for Count William.

works.title: The Faerie Queene
works.subtitle: Books I–VI, with the Mutabilitie Cantos
works.author: Edmund Spenser
works.blurb: Spenser's vast allegorical epic of knights, virtues, and the Faerie court — six completed Books (Holinesse, Temperaunce, Chastitie, Friendship, Iustice, Courtesie) plus the fragmentary Mutabilitie Cantos, in the original 1590s spelling.

works.title: The Fairy Godmother-in-Law
works.author: Oliver Herford
works.blurb: A comic sequel to Cinderella, in which the Prince and Princess are visited by her fairy godmother, who proves an even more formidable relation than the average mother-in-law.

works.title: The Falcon
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: The impoverished Count Federigo, living in a cottage with his foster-brother and nurse, loves the Lady Giovanna, who has come to his door to beg the gift of his falcon for her dying son. Having nothing else fit to serve her at dinner, he has already killed the bird for the meal, and so cannot grant her wish. The lady is moved by his devotion and the play ends in their union.

works.title: The Fall of Robespierre
works.subtitle: An Historic Drama
works.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
works.blurb: A three-act historical drama on the overthrow of Robespierre in July 1794, published at Cambridge in 1794 as a pamphlet under Coleridge's name. In the first act Tallien, Legendre and Barrere plot against the dictator; in the second he is denounced in the Convention and led off under arrest; the third follows the aftermath of his rescue by Henriot. The first act is Coleridge's; the second and third are Southey's.

works.title: The Fall of Troy
works.subtitle: Posthomerica
works.author: Quintus Smyrnaeus
works.blurb: Quintus Smyrnaeus continues the Iliad from the funeral of Hector through the deaths of Akhilleus, Paris and the Amazon queen Penthesileia, the wooden horse and the sack of Troy, to the Greeks' storm-wrecked voyage home.

works.title: The Farmer's Boy
works.subtitle: A Rural Poem
works.author: Robert Bloomfield
works.blurb: A rural poem in four seasons, following the labours and pleasures of a farm boy through the year.

works.title: Fasti
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid’s poem on the Roman festival calendar in the original Latin elegiacs: the six surviving books, January to June.

works.title: The Fasti
works.subtitle: Ovid's Roman Calendar, Books I–VI, prose translation by Henry T. Riley
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid's poem on the Roman festival calendar, here in Riley's prose: the six surviving books, January to June, with the rites, myths and star-risings of each month.

works.title: The Fates of the Apostles
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: A brief martyrology recounting, in turn, the missionary travels and deaths of Christ's twelve apostles, closing the Vercelli Book poem with Cynewulf's runic signature.

works.title: The Fates of the Apostles (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: A brief martyrology recounting the missionary travels and deaths of Christ's twelve apostles, closing with Cynewulf's runic signature, in the original Old English.

works.title: Faust. Der Tragödie erster Teil
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: The German text of Faust I as first printed in 1808. Dr. Faust, a scholar sick of the limits of human knowledge, is wagered over in Heaven and then bargains his soul to Mephistopheles in return for a moment of fulfilment; the devil draws him through the tavern, the witches' kitchen and the Walpurgis Night, and into a love affair with the young Gretchen, who is destroyed in its wake. Each scene pairs with the same scene of Bayard Taylor's English translation.

sections.title: Walpurgisnachtstraum oder Oberon’s und Titania’s goldne Hochzeit. Intermezzo

works.title: Faust: The First Part
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: Dr. Heinrich Faust, a scholar sick of the limits of human knowledge, is wagered over in Heaven and then bargains his soul to the devil Mephistopheles in return for a moment of fulfilment. Mephistopheles draws him through the tavern, the witches' kitchen and a Walpurgis-Night revel, and into a love affair with the young Margaret, whose mother, brother and child are destroyed in its wake. Margaret, imprisoned for infanticide and awaiting execution, refuses Faust's offer of escape and gives herself up to God; a voice from above declares her saved.

sections.title: Walpurgis-Night's Dream (Oberon and Titania's Golden Wedding)

works.title: Faust. Der Tragödie zweiter Teil
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: The German text of Faust II as first printed in 1832. Faust serves the Emperor's court, calls up Helen of Troy and follows her through the Classical Walpurgis Night to a marriage that ends with the death of their son Euphorion, wins land from the sea, and dies at the hour his work is complete, as angels carry off what is immortal in him. Each scene pairs with the matching scene of Bayard Taylor's English translation.

works.subtitle: Translated in the original metres by Bayard Taylor
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: The Second Part of Goethe's Faust in Bayard Taylor's translation in the original metres: Faust serves the Emperor's court, follows Helen of Troy through the Classical Walpurgis-Night to a marriage that ends with the death of their son Euphorion, wins land from the sea, and dies at the hour his own labour is complete, as the angels carry off what is immortal in him.
