works.title: The Feast of Bacchus
works.subtitle: A Comedy in the Latin manner, partly translated from Terence
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's comedy in the Latin manner, privately printed at Oxford in 1889 and published in 1894, partly translated from Terence. The action takes place in a single day in a suburb of Athens, on the feast of Bacchus, among the households of Menedemus and Chremes.

works.title: Fifine at the Fair
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Don Juan's long, teasing defence of inconstancy to his wife Elvire at a Breton fair, framed by the Prologue "Amphibian" and the Epilogue "The Householder".

works.title: Il Filostrato
works.subtitle: The love of Troilo and Griseida, in nine parts
works.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
works.blurb: Boccaccio's early narrative poem in ottava rima on Troilo's love for Griseida and her desertion of him, the source of Chaucer's Troilus and Criseyde.

works.title: Fingal: An Ancient Epic Poem
works.subtitle: In Six Books
works.author: James Macpherson
works.blurb: Ossian's epic of Fingal's rescue of Ireland from Swaran, king of Lochlin, in measured prose.

works.title: The Fire-Bringer
works.author: William Vaughn Moody
works.blurb: After Deukalion's flood the survivors huddle in darkness on a mountain, the fire gone from the earth; Prometheus, who has failed to bring it back from heaven, is given a hollow fennel stalk by the singer Pandora, and in three acts the king Deukalion dies, the people's demand for a child sacrifice is broken, and the stolen fire is carried down to the altar before Prometheus goes to wrestle with the eagle of God.

works.title: The Fleece
works.subtitle: A Poem in Four Books
works.author: John Dyer
works.blurb: Dyer's didactic poem in four books of blank verse on the English wool trade, from the care of sheep and the shearing to the loom, the markets and the ships that carry cloth to the world.

works.title: Floris and Blauncheflur
works.subtitle: Middle English text of the Trentham manuscript, ed. J. Lumby (1866), re-ed. G. H. McKnight (1901)
works.author: Anonymous
works.blurb: A Middle English romance of two children, the Christian Blauncheflur and the king's son Floris, who are raised together and then parted when his father sells her to merchants; Floris sets out for Babylon and wins her back from the Emir's tower.

works.title: The Foray of Queen Meave
works.subtitle: Five Fragments of an Ancient Irish Epic (The Táin Bó Cuailgne)
works.author: Aubrey de Vere
works.blurb: De Vere’s blank-verse retelling, in five fragments with a prologue, of the Táin Bó Cuailgne: Queen Meave of Connacht invades Ulster for the Brown Bull, and the young Cuchullain holds the ford alone.

sections.title: Fragment I: The Cause of the Great War
Fragment II: The Deeds of Cuchullain
Fragment III: The Combat at the Ford
Fragment IV: The Invasion of Uladh

works.title: The Forest Sanctuary
works.author: Felicia Hemans
works.blurb: A Spanish Protestant, fleeing religious persecution in the sixteenth century, tells his story from a North American forest where he has taken refuge with his child.

works.title: The Four PP
works.subtitle: A Merry Interlude of a Palmer, a Pardoner, a Poticary and a Pedlar
works.author: John Heywood
works.blurb: A Palmer, a Pardoner, a Poticary and a Pedlar fall to arguing over whose calling does most good, and the Pedler proposes a contest: the one who tells the greatest lie shall win. The Pardoner shows his absurd relics and tells how he went to hell to fetch a woman out of it; the Poticary boasts of his medicines. When the Palmer calmly says that in all his travels he never saw a woman out of patience, the others cry out that this is the biggest lie of all, and the Pedler awards him the prize. A broad, jesting satire on pilgrimages, pardons and false relics, ending in a plea for plain faith.

works.title: Fragments of Psalms (Old English)
works.subtitle: Metrical psalm passages from the Benedictine Office: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: Short passages of Old English verse translation from twenty-five psalms, found in the Benedictine Office.

works.title: The French Revolution
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's unfinished poem on the fall of the Bastille; only the first of its seven projected books was printed, in 1791.

works.title: Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay
works.subtitle: The Honourable History of Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay
works.author: Robert Greene
works.blurb: Prince Edward, hunting near Fressingfield, falls in love with Margaret, the Keeper's daughter, and sends Lacy, Earl of Lincoln, to woo her on his behalf; Lacy falls for her himself. Meanwhile Friar Bacon of Oxford, a scholar of magic, builds a brazen head to wall England in brass, defeats the German conjurer Vandermast in a contest of spirits, and shows Edward the distant courtship in a glass. The play ends with Edward's renunciation of Margaret, her marriage to Lacy, and Bacon's prophecy at a royal wedding.

works.title: Fridthjof's Saga
works.subtitle: A Norse Romance
works.author: Esaias Tegnér
works.translator: trans. Thomas A. E. Holcomb and Martha A. Lyon Holcomb (1876)
works.blurb: Tegnér's Swedish romantic epic in twenty-four cantos, drawn from an Icelandic saga: the farmer's son Fridthjof loves Ingeborg, daughter of King Bele, and is parted from her by her brothers, outlawed, and finally reconciled, here in English verse by the Holcombs.

works.title: The Tale of Frithiof
works.subtitle: Frithiof's Saga
works.author: Esaias Tegnér
works.blurb: Tegnér's Swedish romantic epic in twenty-four cantos, drawn from an Icelandic saga: the farmer's son Frithiof loves Ingeborg, daughter of King Bele, and is parted from her by her brothers, outlawed, and finally reconciled, here in the English verse of Captain Spalding, a second translation, in the original measures, of 1872.

works.title: The Furies
works.subtitle: The Oresteia
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: Pursued by the Furies of his murdered mother, Orestes flees to Apollo's shrine at Delphi and then to Athens. Athena sets up a jury of Athenian citizens to try him; the votes tie, and her own vote acquits him. She persuades the angry Furies to stay in Athens as the kindly Eumenides, honoured guardians of the city.

works.title: Gammer Gurton's Needle
works.author: William Stevenson (attributed)
works.blurb: Gammer Gurton loses the needle with which she was mending her servant Hodge's breeches, and the mischievous vagabond Diccon the Bedlam persuades her that her neighbour Dame Chat has stolen it. Accusations, a brawl and the arrival of the curate, Doctor Rat, and the bailiff follow, until Hodge, struck by Diccon, finds the needle sticking in his own breeches. One of the earliest English comedies, it opens Act II with the drinking song 'Back and side go bare, go bare'.

works.title: گرشاسپ‌نامه (Garshaspnameh)
works.subtitle: Asadi of Tus's Persian epic of the hero Garshasp (Garshasp-nama), completed in 1066
works.author: Asadi of Tus
works.blurb: Asadi of Tus's Persian epic of Garshasp, the dragon-slaying hero of the Sam dynasty and ancestor of Rustam, told in some nine thousand couplets and completed in 1066, a generation after Firdausi's Shahnameh. The original Persian text.

works.title: The Gentle Shepherd: A Pastoral Comedy
works.author: Allan Ramsay
works.blurb: Set in a Lowland village in the years after the Restoration, Ramsay's pastoral follows Patie, a shepherd who loves Peggy, a foundling he takes for a poor girl, while his friend Roger woos Jenny and the dull Bauldy plots against them. Sir William Worthy, the exiled laird, returns in disguise and the secret of Peggy's birth comes out, so that the lovers may marry. The play is built of Scots dialogue in couplets, with twenty-one songs set to old tunes.

works.title: The Forerunner
works.subtitle: His Parables and Poems
works.author: Kahlil Gibran
works.blurb: Gibran's second book in English: a sequence of short parables and prose poems, opening with the Forerunner's own address and closing with his last watch over a sleeping city, in which the preacher-prophet, the saint, the poet, the king and the fool are each shown at the edge of what they claim to know.

works.title: The Prophet
works.author: Kahlil Gibran
works.blurb: Gibran's best-known work, written in English: the prophet Almustafa, about to sail home after twelve years in the city of Orphalese, answers the townspeople's questions on love, work, joy and sorrow, death and other matters of life, in twenty-six poetic discourses framed by his arrival and his farewell.

works.title: Gil Perez, the Gallician

works.title: The Golden Legend
works.subtitle: Christus: A Mystery, Part II
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A dramatic poem set in medieval Germany, drawn from Hartmann von Aue's tale of Poor Henry. Prince Henry of Hoheneck, wasting with a mysterious sickness, is told that only a maiden's willing death can cure him. Elsie, a peasant girl, offers hers, and the two travel through Strasburg, the Black Forest convent of Hirschau, the Alps and Italy to the medical school at Salerno, where Henry prevents the sacrifice. Lucifer in disguise tempts the travellers throughout, and a Miracle Play of the Nativity is performed inside the Strasburg scenes. Longfellow made the poem the second part of his trilogy Christus: A Mystery.

works.title: 感天動地竇娥冤 (Gan tian dong di Dou E yuan) — The Injustice to Dou E
works.author: Guan Hanqing
works.blurb: The young widow Dou E, sold into the house of the moneylender Granny Cai to pay her scholar father's debt, refuses the advances of the ruffian Zhang Lü-er and is framed by him for poisoning his own father. Tortured by a corrupt magistrate and condemned to die, she swears that her blood will fly up the flagpole, that snow will fall in midsummer and that drought will grip the district for three years, and all three come to pass. Her father, now a high official, hears her ghost and reverses the verdict. Guan Hanqing's most famous zaju, a wedge and four acts of sung arias and spoken dialogue, is a landmark protest against official injustice.

works.blurb: Shevchenko's narrative poem of the 1768 Koliivshchyna uprising, in which the haidamaks, led by Zalizniak and Honta, rise against Polish landlords in Right-Bank Ukraine.

works.title: Hájnikova žena
works.subtitle: The Gamekeeper's Wife
works.author: Pavol Országh Hviezdoslav
works.blurb: Hviezdoslav's great lyrical-epic of the Slovak forest, telling the life and death of a gamekeeper's wife through a cycle of cantos, songs and nature scenes.

works.title: Halidon Hill: A Dramatic Sketch from Scottish History
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: On the morning of the battle of Halidon Hill (1333), the Scottish host is drawn up on the slope to face Edward III's army, while its leaders quarrel over precedence. The Knight Templar De Vipont meets his old friend Sir Alan Swinton, whose feud with the young Lord of Gordon he tries to keep from blood. The Regent refuses Swinton's counsel; Swinton and Gordon, reconciled, lead a charge of their own, and both fall as the day is lost.

works.title: Halieutica
works.subtitle: On Fishing
works.author: Oppian
works.blurb: A didactic poem in five books on the natures, habits and capture of sea creatures, addressed to the emperors Marcus Aurelius and Commodus.

works.title: The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Prince Hamlet, summoned home to Elsinore by his father's death, is told by the Ghost that Claudius, now king and married to Hamlet's mother, murdered him. Feigning madness and staging a play to catch the king's conscience, Hamlet delays his revenge while the court around him unravels: Polonius is killed, Ophelia is driven to drowning, and Laertes returns for vengeance. The final duel leaves almost the whole court dead and the throne to Fortinbras of Norway.

works.title: The Code of Hammurabi
works.subtitle: The Oldest Code of Laws in the World
works.author: Hammurabi
works.blurb: The best-known law code of ancient Mesopotamia, issued by the king of Babylon c. 1750 BC: laws on theft, land, trade, marriage, injury and the hire of labour.

works.title: Harold: A Drama
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: Tennyson's verse drama of the last Saxon king. Harold, Earl of Wessex, is shipwrecked on the Norman coast and forced to swear an oath to Duke William, a vow that haunts him when the dying Edward the Confessor names him heir. Crowned king, he defeats his brother Tostig and the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge, then marches south to meet the Normans at Hastings, where he falls and Edith finds his body on the field of the dead.

works.title: Harold the Dauntless
works.subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A verse romance of the Danish settlement of Northumbria: the fierce heathen Harold, son of Count Witikind, is drawn through blood, magic and a warning from the grave toward repentance and the love of the Danish maid Eivir.

works.title: The Lay of Havelok the Dane
works.subtitle: Middle English verse romance, ed. W. W. Skeat (EETS, 1868)
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: An English verse romance of about 3,000 lines in which Havelok, the dispossessed son of a Danish king, is raised by a fisherman, marries the English princess Goldeborw, and wins back both kingdoms.

works.title: Heaven and Earth
works.subtitle: A Mystery
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's biblical drama on the eve of the Flood, begun at Ravenna in October 1821 and first published in The Liberal in 1823. Anah and Aholibamah, descendants of Cain, are loved by the angels Samiasa and Azaziel, while the patriarch Noah's son Japhet loves Anah. As the waters rise, the angels carry the two women away and Japhet is left on a rock as the Ark floats towards him. Only the first part of the work was written.

works.title: Ἑκάβη (Hekabe)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: After the fall of Troy the Greek fleet lies becalmed on the Thracian shore. Hekabe, a captive queen, sees her daughter Polyxene sacrificed on Achilles' tomb, then finds the body of her youngest son Polydoros, murdered for his gold by the Thracian king Polymestor, and takes a terrible revenge. The Greek text is given in the order of Nauck's edition, so that it pairs with the English translation of the same play.

works.title: Hecuba
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: After the fall of Troy, the captive queen Hecuba loses her daughter Polyxena to sacrifice at the tomb of Akhilleus, then finds the body of her youngest son Polydorus, murdered for his gold by the Thracian king who was sheltering him. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of grief turned to vengeance in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.blurb: The Punjabi retelling of the love of Heer and Ranjha, the best-loved qissa of Punjab, set in Sufi imagery.

works.title: Ἑλένη (Helene)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: The real Helen has spent the Trojan War in Egypt, sheltered at the tomb of King Proteus, while Hera sent a phantom of her to Troy for Greeks and Trojans to die over. Menelaos, shipwrecked and ragged, is turned away from the palace by an old woman, then meets his wife and at first cannot believe her. The prophetess Theonoe, sister of the king Theoklymenos who wants to marry Helen, is persuaded to keep silent. Helen and Menelaos trick the king with a false funeral at sea and sail away, and the Dioskouroi appear to calm his anger.

works.title: Helen of Troy
works.author: Andrew Lang
works.blurb: Lang's retelling of the story of Helen in six books of rhyme royal, from the coming of Paris to Sparta to the sack of Troy and the return of Helen to Menelaus, with Helen conceived as the unwilling victim of the gods.

sections.title: Book I: The Coming of Paris
Book II: The Spell of Aphrodite
Book III: The Flight of Helen
Book IV: The Death of Corythus
Book VI: The Sack of Troy. The Return of Helen

works.title: Helen
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Euripides follows the Recantation of Stesichorus: the Helen who went to Troy was only a phantom of cloud, while the true Helen waited in Egypt, chaste, at the tomb of King Proteus. When shipwrecked Menelaus arrives, husband and wife must trick the king who wishes to marry her. Arthur Way renders this romantic tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: The Ethiopics; or, Adventures of Theagenes and Chariclea
works.subtitle: Smith translation, 1855
works.author: Heliodorus of Emesa
works.blurb: The Greek romance of the lovers Theagenes and Chariclea, parted by pirates, priests and kings from Delphi to Egypt and Ethiopia: the best-known ancient novel, in Rowland Smith's English prose of 1855.

works.subtitle: A Lyrical Drama
works.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
works.blurb: Shelley's lyrical drama of the Greek War of Independence, set in the Sultan's Constantinople, closing with the chorus 'The world's great age begins anew'.

works.author: Voltaire
works.translator: trans. Tobias Smollett, Thomas Francklin and others (1762)
works.blurb: Voltaire's epic of Henri IV and the French Wars of Religion, from the St Bartholomew massacre to the siege and surrender of Paris.

works.title: The First Part of King Henry the Fourth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: The Percy family, who helped Henry IV to the throne, rise against him, led by the fiery Hotspur. Meanwhile the king's son, Prince Hal, wastes his days in Eastcheap taverns with the fat knight Sir John Falstaff and his thieving companions. Hal at last turns to honour, takes up arms for his father, and kills Hotspur at the battle of Shrewsbury.

works.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Fourth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: The Archbishop of York and his allies rise in a second rebellion, and Prince John of Lancaster crushes it at Gaultree Forest by a false promise of peace and a prompt arrest. Falstaff, sent recruiting into Gloucestershire, trades old memories with Justice Shallow and takes bribes from the men he chooses to spare. Meanwhile the dying king, troubled by a crown that has cost him sleep, makes his peace with Prince Hal, who on his accession rejects Falstaff in the street.

works.blurb: Hartmann's tale of a nobleman struck with leprosy and the peasant girl who offers her life for his cure, in Rossetti's rhymed paraphrase.

works.title: The Life of King Henry the Fifth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry V presses his claim to the throne of France, exposes the traitors Cambridge, Scroop and Grey at Southampton, takes Harfleur, and wins against heavy odds at Agincourt, with the Chorus asking the audience to supply what the stage cannot show. The war ends in the comic, halting wooing of Katherine of France.

works.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: The play opens at the funeral of Henry V, as the English hold France only by the valour of Talbot, whom Joan la Pucelle and the French confront at Orleans and beyond. In the Temple Garden the red and white roses are plucked, and the quarrel of York and Lancaster begins. Suffolk, meanwhile, woos Margaret of Anjou on the young king's behalf, with designs of his own.

works.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Sixth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry VI's marriage to Margaret of Anjou opens a reign of faction: the Duchess of Gloucester's sorcery brings down the good Duke Humphrey, murdered at the instigation of Suffolk, who is himself killed at sea by pirates. Jack Cade's rabble rising sweeps London in prose and carnage, while Richard of York throws off his pretence and openly claims the crown, winning the first battle of St Albans and opening the Wars of the Roses.

works.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry VI, weak and pious, disinherits his own son in favour of the Duke of York, setting the Wars of the Roses ablaze: York is taunted and slain at Wakefield, the king watches the carnage from a molehill at Towton, and Warwick the Kingmaker changes sides when Edward IV marries for love. Edward's victory at Tewkesbury closes the play, with Gloucester, the future Richard III, murdering the captive Henry in the Tower.

works.title: King Henry the Eighth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Henry VIII's court sees the proud Duke of Buckingham brought down by Cardinal Wolsey's schemes, until Wolsey's own power turns to ruin when the king's eye falls on Anne Bullen. Queen Katherine defends her marriage at the Blackfriars trial and dies with dignity at Kimbolton. The play ends with the king's marriage to Anne and Cranmer's prophecy of greatness at the christening of the infant Elizabeth.

works.title: Ἡρακλεῖδαι (Herakleidai)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: The aged Iolaos has fled from city to city with the children of the dead Herakles, hunted by King Eurystheus of Argos, and has taken refuge at the altar of Zeus at Marathon. Eurystheus’ herald tries to drag them away, but Demophon, king of Athens, takes up their cause. An oracle then demands the sacrifice of a noble maiden before Athens can win, and Makaria, a daughter of Herakles, offers her life. In the battle that follows Iolaos, made young again by the gods, captures Eurystheus, whom Alkmene condemns to death. The Greek text is given in the order of the Nauck edition, so that it pairs with the English translation of the same play.

works.title: Ἡρακλῆς (Herakles)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: In the absence of Herakles, who has gone down to Hades on his last labour, the usurper Lykos threatens to kill his wife Megara, his sons and his old father Amphitryon, who have taken refuge at the altar of Zeus. Herakles returns in time to rescue them and to kill Lykos. Then Hera sends Iris and Madness (Lyssa) against him, and in his frenzy he murders his own children and Megara. Waking to the horror of what he has done, he is persuaded by his friend Theseus not to take his own life, and he is led away to Athens. The Greek text is given in the order of the Nauck edition, so that it pairs with the English translation of the same play.

works.title: Hercules Furens
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Juno's hatred drives Hercules mad on his return from the underworld, and in his frenzy he kills his own wife and children.

works.title: Hercules Furens
works.subtitle: Mad Hercules
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Juno, furious that Hercules has returned alive from the underworld, sends a madness upon him. While the tyrant Lycus presses Hercules’ wife Megara and old Amphitryon at the altar, the hero comes home, kills the usurper, and is then driven by Juno to slaughter his own wife and children, taking them for the family of his enemy Eurystheus. He wakes in his right mind to see what he has done, and only the entreaties of his friend Theseus keep him from suicide.

works.title: Hercules Oetaeus
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Hercules, victorious over the world, is destroyed by the poisoned robe sent by his jealous wife Deianira and dies on Mount Oeta.

works.title: Hercules

works.blurb: An allegory in Swedish hexameters on the choice of Hercules: at the start of his youth the hero is courted by Pleasure and by Virtue, and must decide how to live. 1658 spelling.

works.title: Ἱππόλυτος (Hippolytos)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Aphrodite, scorned by the chaste huntsman Hippolytos, who honours only Artemis, makes his stepmother Phaidra fall in love with him. Phaidra's old nurse betrays her secret to Hippolytos; Phaidra hangs herself and leaves a tablet accusing him, and Theseus, trusting it, curses his son with a wish granted by Poseidon. Hippolytos is dragged to death by his own horses, and Artemis appears to reveal the truth and to reconcile father and dying son. The Greek text is given in the order of the Nauck edition, so that it pairs with the English translations of the same play.

The lovers plan to elope, the villainous Dick Deadeye betrays them, and Little Buttercup's confession of a baby-swap long ago puts every rank in its right place.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.translator: trans. William Cowper (1791; Southey’s edition, New York 1860)
works.blurb: William Cowper’s blank-verse translation of the Iliad, first published in 1791, here in the 1860 New York edition of Robert Southey’s text.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: The Earl of Derby, three times Prime Minister, rendered Homer’s epic of the wrath of Akhilleus into stately Victorian blank verse.

works.title: Ἰλιάς (Iliad, Greek text)
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: The Iliad in the original Homeric Greek, in twenty-four books of dactylic hexameter, from the Oxford Classical Text of Monro and Allen (1908-1920), with the polytonic accents and breathings as printed.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Thomas Hobbes's rhymed-quatrain translation of the Iliad, first published in 1676 when the philosopher of the Leviathan was in his late eighties, here in the 1676 London edition of William Crook.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.translator: trans. Andrew Lang, Walter Leaf and Ernest Myers (1911)
works.blurb: The prose translation of the Iliad by Walter Leaf, Andrew Lang and Ernest Myers, in a deliberately archaic, Authorised-Version-flavoured English, here in the 1911 revised edition.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: A. T. Murray’s literal prose translation of the wrath of Akhilleus and the last year of the siege of Troy, from the Loeb Classical Library of 1924.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Alexander Pope’s celebrated heroic-couplet translation of the Iliad, one of the great achievements of Augustan English verse.

works.title: The Iliad (Way)
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Arthur S. Way’s rhymed verse translation of the Iliad, in long swinging anapaestic lines, published in two volumes in 1886 and 1888.

works.title: Illuminations
works.subtitle: In the original French, from the 1886 La Vogue edition
works.author: Arthur Rimbaud
works.blurb: Rimbaud’s prose poems and free-verse pieces of 1873–75, first collected and printed in 1886: brief, dazzling sketches of cities, childhood, dawn and departure.

sections.title: Chanson de la plus haute tour

works.title: In a Balcony
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A short drama in one scene. Norbert, a young statesman, has won the Queen's favour and asks Constance, her cousin and companion, to let him claim her hand as his reward. Constance advises a cautious approach; the Queen, hearing him speak, mistakes whom he loves, and the evening ends in discovery.

works.title: In the Name of Time
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Michael Field
works.blurb: A tragedy in five acts set in eighth-century Francia and Italy. Carloman, Frankish Mayor of the Palace, is torn between his wife Geneviva and his vow to renounce the world, and leaves for Rome and Monte Cassino to take the monastic habit while his brother Pepin works toward the crown. Written by Katharine Bradley and Edith Cooper, who published as Michael Field, it was issued posthumously in 1919.

works.title: Indian Idylls
works.subtitle: from the Sanskrit of the Mahabharata
works.author: Vyasa
works.blurb: Eight episodes from the Mahabharata in Sir Edwin Arnold's English verse, from the love of Savitri and the tale of Nala and Damayanti to the last journey of the Pandavas and Yudhisthira's entry into heaven.

works.title: The Inferno (Carlyle)
works.subtitle: Prose translation by John Aitken Carlyle, revised by H. Oelsner (Temple Classics)
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.translator: trans. John Aitken Carlyle (1849), revised by H. Oelsner (Temple Classics, 1900)
works.blurb: Dante's journey through Hell in John Aitken Carlyle's plain, literal prose, revised for the Temple Classics by Hermann Oelsner, whose added words are kept in square brackets.

works.title: The Inferno (Sibbald)
works.subtitle: Translated by James Romanes Sibbald
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's journey through Hell, in James Romanes Sibbald's Victorian terza rima, the form and rhyme of the original kept.

works.title: The Inferno (Wright)
works.subtitle: Translated by Ichabod Charles Wright
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's journey through Hell in Ichabod Charles Wright's rhymed tercets, the three-line stanza of the original kept.

works.title: Iolanthe
works.subtitle: Or, The Peer and the Peri
works.author: W. S. Gilbert
works.blurb: The fairy Iolanthe, banished for marrying a mortal, is reunited with her son Strephon, a half-fairy shepherd who loves Phyllis, a ward of Chancery. When the Lord Chancellor and the peers of the realm contest Phyllis's hand, and Strephon enters Parliament, the Fairy Queen's magic turns the House of Lords upside down.

works.title: Ion
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: At Delphi, the temple servant Ion does not know that he is the son of Apollo and Creusa, the Athenian queen who exposed him as a newborn. When she and her husband Xuthus come to the oracle, a false answer, a poisoned cup and a recognition at the altar bring mother and son together. Coleridge's literal prose translation.

works.title: Ἴων (Ion)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: At Delphi the foundling Ion serves as a temple attendant of Apollo, unaware that he is the child Kreousa once bore to the god and exposed in a cave beneath the Athenian Acropolis. When Kreousa and her childless husband Xouthos consult the oracle, Apollo's answer hands Ion to Xouthos as his son, and Kreousa, believing herself betrayed, sends a poisoned cup against the young man. The plot fails, and Ion, pursuing her to the altar, is stopped when the Pythia produces the basket and tokens in which he was found. Athena then appears to confirm the recognition and to foretell the Ionian descent of his line. The play is given here in Greek, in Nauck's Teubner text, so that it pairs with the English translations.

works.title: Ion
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: At Delphi, a temple servant named Ion, once a foundling left in the sanctuary of Apollo, meets the childless Athenian queen Kreusa and her husband Xuthus. A muddled oracle, a failed poisoning and an ark of hidden tokens bring mother and son to recognise one another. Arthur Way renders Euripides' play in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Iphigeneia at Aulis
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: At Aulis the Greek fleet lies windbound, and the seer Kalchas declares that the goddess Artemis will release the winds only if Agamemnon sacrifices his daughter. Lured to the camp with the promise of a marriage to Akhilleus, Iphigeneia must choose between her mother's grief and her own willing death. Arthur Way renders Euripides' last tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Iphigeneia in Taurica
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Snatched from the altar at Aulis by Artemis, Iphigeneia serves as priestess in the savage land of the Taurians, where every Greek who lands is sacrificed to the goddess. When two strangers are seized on the shore, she finds that one of them is her brother Orestes, and together they plot an escape with the goddess's image. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy of recognition in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Ἰφιγένεια ἡ ἐν Αὐλίδι (Iphigeneia en Aulidi)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: At Aulis the Greek fleet lies windbound, and the seer Kalchas declares that Artemis will release the winds only if Agamemnon sacrifices his daughter Iphigeneia. Lured to the camp with the promise of a marriage to Akhilleus, she must choose between her mother's grief and her own willing death. Euripides' last tragedy, produced after his death, is given here in Greek in the order of Nauck's Teubner text, so that it pairs with the English verse translation of the same play.

works.title: Ἰφιγένεια ἡ ἐν Ταύροις (Iphigeneia en Taurois)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Iphigeneia, saved from sacrifice at Aulis by Artemis, serves as the goddess's priestess among the Taurians, where every Greek stranger must be offered at the altar. Orestes and Pylades, driven there by Apollo's command to fetch the sacred image of Artemis, are seized and brought to her for sacrifice. Through a letter she wishes to send home to Argos, brother and sister recognise one another, and together they plot an escape by sea with the image, under cover of a rite of purification. When King Thoas pursues them, the goddess Athena appears above the stage to end the quarrel and to send them to found Artemis's cult in Attica.

works.title: Iphigenia in Tauris
works.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
works.blurb: Goethe's verse drama in five acts. Iphigenia, saved from sacrifice at Aulis and made priestess of Diana among the Taurians, longs for Greece. When her brother Orestes, pursued by the Furies, arrives with his friend Pylades as captives destined for the altar, she must choose between truth and escape, and between loyalty to the king who sheltered her and the call of her family.

works.author: Anonymous (Iroquois)
works.blurb: The speeches, hymn and roll of founders of the Condoling Council of the Iroquois League, in the Canienga (Mohawk) and Onondaga texts recorded by Horatio Hale in 1883.

works.title: Speeches
works.author: Isaeus
works.blurb: Eleven speeches and a large fragment of a twelfth by the Athenian orator Isaeus, nearly all of them inheritance cases, in Forster's Loeb translation.

works.blurb: The Jangnama, or Jang Singhan te Farangian, is Shah Mohammad's Punjabi account of the Anglo-Sikh war of 1845-46, from the death of Ranjit Singh and the quarrels at the Lahore court to the battle of Sobraon. It is a set text in Punjabi literature, in 105 stanzas, and the poet sees the Sikh defeat as a catastrophe for the Punjab.

works.title: The Jew of Malta
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: Barabas, the richest Jew of Malta, is stripped of his wealth by Governor Ferneze to pay the tribute owed the Turks, and sets out on a course of revenge that costs him his daughter Abigail, a convent of nuns, two friars and his own accomplices. Prefaced by Machiavel in person, Marlowe's savage comedy of greed, religion and policy ends with Barabas boiled in the very cauldron he prepared for the Turkish prince.

works.title: John Brown’s Body
works.author: Stephen Vincent Benét
works.blurb: Benét’s narrative poem of the American Civil War opens with an invocation to the American muse and follows the war from John Brown’s raid on Harpers Ferry to Appomattox and its aftermath, through eight books. It weaves the fortunes of imagined families, Jack Ellyat of Connecticut, Clay Wingate of Georgia and the mountain boy Luke Breckinridge, together with Lincoln, Davis, Lee, Grant and the battles from Bull Run to Gettysburg, and carries inset songs and lyrics within its books.

works.author: Henry Jones
works.blurb: Henry Jones's topographical poem on Clifton and the Hotwells near Bristol, praising its spa, its houses and its company in heroic couplets.

works.title: The Isle of Wight
works.subtitle: a Poem, in Three Cantos
works.author: Henry Jones
works.blurb: Henry Jones's topographical poem in three cantos on the Isle of Wight, its scenery and towns, written in heroic couplets.

works.title: Against Apion
works.subtitle: Josephus's defence of the antiquity of the Jewish people against Apion and other Greek detractors, in two books
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's reply to the slanders of Apion, Manetho, Apollonius Molon and others, setting out the antiquity of the Jews and the excellence of their law, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: The Antiquities of the Jews
works.subtitle: The Jewish Antiquities, in twenty books, from the Creation to the twelfth year of Nero
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's history of the Jewish people from the Creation to the eve of the revolt against Rome, in twenty books, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: The Wars of the Jews; or, The History of the Destruction of Jerusalem
works.subtitle: The Jewish War, in seven books, from the capture of Jerusalem by Antiochus Epiphanes to the fall of Masada
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's eyewitness account of the Jewish revolt against Rome (AD 66–73), from the siege of Jotapata to the burning of the Temple and the end at Masada, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: The Life of Flavius Josephus
works.subtitle: Josephus's autobiography, written about AD 100 as an appendix to the Antiquities
works.author: Flavius Josephus
works.blurb: Josephus's account of his priestly descent, his schooling among the Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes, his command in Galilee during the revolt against Rome, and his later life, in William Whiston's English of 1737.

works.title: Diwan of Judah Halevi: Hebrew poems (Wikisource)
works.subtitle: Fifty-seven further Hebrew poems, mostly liturgical
works.author: Judah Halevi
works.blurb: Fifty-seven more Hebrew poems of Judah Halevi, the great poet of medieval Spain: penitential prayers and laments, Sabbath and festival hymns, wedding songs, love songs and an elegy.

sections.title: אשרי עין ראתה כהן בהוד עטרת
הקבצו ושמעו בני יעקב דת יוצרכם

works.title: Judas Maccabaeus
works.subtitle: A Play in Five Acts
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A verse play on the Jewish revolt against the Syrian king Antiochus Epiphanes. Antiochus, with the renegade High-Priest Jason, tries to force Greek gods on Jerusalem; a mother and her seven sons endure martyrdom; Judas Maccabaeus rallies the Jews, defeats the general Nicanor and retakes the Temple; and the play closes with the death of Antiochus.

works.title: Judita
works.subtitle: Libar Marka Marula Splićanina u kom se uzdarži istorija svete udovice Judit u versih harvacki složena kako ona ubi vojvodu Oloferna po sridu vojske njegove i oslobodi puk israelski od velike pogibli
works.author: Marko Marulić
works.blurb: The first epic in Croatian: the biblical widow Judith beheads the Assyrian general Holofernes and delivers her people, told in six books of rhymed twelve-syllable verse.

sections.title: Ča se u kom libri uzdarži

works.title: Judith
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.translator: trans. Cosette Faust Newton & Stith Thompson (1918)
works.blurb: A retelling, in the Nowell Codex alongside Beowulf, of the apocryphal Book of Judith: the widow Judith beheads the drunken Assyrian general Holofernes and delivers her people, recast in the heroic idiom of Old English verse.

works.title: Judith (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: A retelling, in the Nowell Codex alongside Beowulf, of the apocryphal Book of Judith, in the original Old English: the widow Judith beheads the drunken Assyrian general Holofernes and delivers her people, recast in the heroic idiom of Old English verse.

works.title: Juliana
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: One of Cynewulf's four signed poems: the passion of the virgin martyr Juliana of Nicomedia, who resists both an unwanted marriage to a pagan prefect and torture by a demon sent to break her faith.

works.title: Juliana (Old English)
works.subtitle: Old English text
works.author: Cynewulf
works.blurb: The Old English verse of one of Cynewulf's four signed poems: the passion of the virgin martyr Juliana of Nicomedia, who resists both an unwanted marriage to a pagan prefect and torture by a demon sent to break her faith.

works.title: The Civil War
works.subtitle: Commentaries on the civil war between Caesar and Pompey, 49–48 BC, in three books (De Bello Civili)
works.author: Julius Caesar
works.translator: trans. W. A. McDevitte and W. S. Bohn (1869)
works.blurb: Caesar's own account of the outbreak of the war with Pompey and the Senate: the crossing of the Rubicon, the Italian and Spanish campaigns, the siege of Massilia, and the struggle in Illyricum, Africa, Epirus and Thessaly down to the eve of the Alexandrian war.

works.title: The Gallic War
works.subtitle: Commentaries on the war in Gaul, 58–52 BC, in eight books (De Bello Gallico)
works.author: Julius Caesar
works.translator: trans. W. A. McDevitte and W. S. Bohn (1869)
works.blurb: Caesar's own account of his campaigns against the Gauls, Germans and Britons, from the Helvetian migration to the siege of Alesia and the final pacification of Gaul, with Hirtius's continuation.

works.title: The Tragedy of Julius Caesar
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Rome's leaders fear that Julius Caesar, fresh from his triumph over Pompey's sons, will make himself king. Cassius draws the honourable Brutus into a conspiracy, and the conspirators stab Caesar in the Capitol on the Ides of March. Brutus justifies the killing to the crowd, but Mark Antony's funeral speech turns the people against the assassins and they are driven from the city. Brutus and Cassius quarrel, then are overwhelmed by Antony and Octavius at Philippi, where both die by their own hands.

works.title: The Kalevala
works.subtitle: The Epic Poem of Finland
works.author: Elias Lönnrot
works.blurb: Fifty runes of Finnish folk song gathered into one epic: the birth of the sage Wainamoinen, the rivalry of Finns and the people of Pohjola for the Sampo, the doomed Kullervo, and the hero's departure as a new age arrives.

works.blurb: The Finnish national epic in its definitive 1849 form: fifty runos in the trochaic tetrameter of the old rune-songs, telling of Väinämöinen, Ilmarinen, Lemminkäinen, the forging of the Sampo and the struggle with Pohjola.

works.subtitle: The Land of the Heroes
works.author: Elias Lönnrot
works.blurb: Kirby's 1907 English version of the Finnish national epic in fifty runos, from the birth of the sage Väinämöinen through the forging and theft of the Sampo and the doomed Kullervo to the hero's departure as Marjatta's child is made King of Carelia.

works.title: कामायनी (Kamayani)
works.subtitle: महाकाव्य, पंद्रह सर्ग
works.author: Jaishankar Prasad
works.blurb: Jaishankar Prasad's Hindi epic of the survivor of the great flood, Manu, and his two companions, Shraddha (faith) and Ida (intellect), in fifteen sargas from Chinta (Anxiety) to Ananda (Bliss): the founding poem of Chhayavad and a landmark of modern Hindi literature. Published 1936.

works.title: கம்பராமாயணம் — ஆரணிய காண்டம் (Kamba Ramayanam, Aranya Kandam)
works.subtitle: Ramavataram, Book 3
works.author: Kambar
works.blurb: The third book of Kambar's Tamil Ramayana: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana in the Dandaka forest, the encounters with Viradha, Agastya and Jatayu, Surpanakha's humiliation, the slaying of Khara, Ravana's plot, the golden deer and the abduction of Sita, in four-line stanzas.

works.title: கம்பராமாயணம் — அயோத்தியா காண்டம் (Kamba Ramayanam, Ayodhya Kandam)
works.subtitle: Ramavataram, Book 2
works.author: Kambar
works.blurb: The second book of Kambar's Tamil Ramayana: the plot against Rama's coronation, his exile with Sita and Lakshmana, Dasaratha's death, and Bharata's attempt to bring him home, in four-line stanzas.

works.title: கம்பராமாயணம் — பால காண்டம் (Kamba Ramayanam, Bala Kandam)
works.subtitle: Ramavataram, Book 1
works.author: Kambar
works.blurb: The first book of Kambar's Tamil Ramayana, from the invocation to the encounter with Parashurama, in four-line stanzas.

works.title: கும்பகருணன் வதைப் படலம் (Kambaramayanam, Yuddha Kandam: Kumbhakarna Vadhai Padalam)
works.subtitle: Yuddha Kandam, the death of Kumbhakarna
works.author: Kambar
works.blurb: The canto of Kumbhakarna's death from Kambar's Tamil Ramayana: Ravana's council, the giant's waking, his refusal of Vibhishana's plea, and his last battle against Rama.

sections.title: தூதரை அழைத்து வரக் கஞ்சுகியை இராவணன் ஏவுதல்
எண்திசைச் சேனைகளையும் கொணரத் தூதர்களை இராவணன் பணித்தல்

works.title: The Kasîdah of Hâjî Abdû El-Yezdî
works.author: Sir Richard Francis Burton
works.blurb: A philosophical quatrain-sequence in which a desert traveller, Haji Abdu, reflects on faith, fate and the vanity of creeds. Burton's own composition, offered as a rendering from the Persian.

works.title: Катерина
works.subtitle: Поема
works.author: Taras Shevchenko
works.blurb: Shevchenko's narrative poem of the village girl Kateryna, seduced and abandoned by a Russian soldier, cast out by her parents, and driven to drown herself, while her son is left to wander with a blind kobzar.

works.title: Keep Your Own Secret
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: At the court of Parma the Prince, his secretary Don Cesar and the courtier Don Felix each hide a love from the rest, and every secret confided to the wrong ear tangles the plot further. The comedy ends with Nisida's hand placed in Felix's and a moral against trusting even a friend with a secret.

works.title: Kerkhofblommen
works.subtitle: Geplukt en bewaerd ter nagedachtenesse van zaliger Mijnheer Eduard Van den Bussche
works.author: Guido Gezelle
works.blurb: Written in two days in May 1858 after the funeral of a pupil, Eduard Van den Bussche, at the minor seminary of Roeselare: a funeral narrative that alternates prose meditation with verse, followed by a gathering of memorial verses (Zielgedichtjes) written for funeral cards.

works.title: כתר מלכות
works.subtitle: Keter Malkhut (The Royal Crown)
works.author: Solomon ibn Gabirol
works.blurb: A long devotional hymn on the greatness of God, the order of the heavens and the soul's penitence, sung in the Sephardi rite on the eve of the Day of Atonement.

works.title: خسرو و شیرین (Khosrow o Shirin)
works.subtitle: The Persian original of Nizami's Khosrow o Shirin
works.author: Nizami Ganjavi
works.blurb: Nizami's Persian romance of the Sasanian king Khosrow Parviz and the Armenian princess Shirin, completed around 1180: the original text, in Ganjoor's section order.

works.title: King Arthur
works.subtitle: Books I to XII
works.author: Edward Bulwer Lytton
works.blurb: Bulwer Lytton’s twelve-book romantic epic in Spenserian stanzas, following Arthur and the wizard Merlin through the three labours of Fable-land.

works.title: King Edward the Third
works.subtitle: A dramatic fragment from Poetical Sketches
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: An unfinished historical drama from Blake's first book, set during Edward III's French campaign. Edward invokes Liberty before landing in Brittany; Prince Lionel and his lords debate commerce at the English court; at Cressy the blunt Sir Thomas Dagworth jests that the King is afraid of Philip, and the young Black Prince and Sir John Chandos talk of glory, age and experience. On the eve of battle Sir Walter Manny weeps for the men who must die, and a minstrel sings the war song of the sons of Trojan Brutus, which ends with Liberty standing on the cliffs of Albion.

sections.title: Scene 6: In the Camp: the Minstrel's Song

works.title: King Horn
works.subtitle: Middle English text of Cambridge University Library MS Gg.4.27.2, ed. J. R. Lumby (1866), re-ed. G. H. McKnight (1901)
works.author: Anonymous
works.blurb: The earliest surviving English verse romance: the exiled prince Horn, cast adrift as a boy after Saracens kill his father, wins the love of Rymenhild, proves himself in Ireland, and returns to reclaim his kingdom.

works.title: The Life and Death of King John
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: King John holds the English crown against the claim of his nephew Arthur, whom France backs, and the play follows the quarrel through the siege of Angiers, the bargained marriage of Louis and Blanche, and the grief of Arthur's mother Constance. Philip Faulconbridge, the Bastard, acknowledged as Richard Lionheart's son, becomes the play's sardonic commentator on politics and 'commodity'. Arthur dies leaping from the castle walls, the barons turn against John, and the king is poisoned at Swinstead Abbey, leaving England to young Henry.

works.title: The Tragedy of King Lear
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: King Lear, old and weary of rule, divides his kingdom among his daughters according to their professions of love, banishing the plain-spoken Cordelia and Kent. Goneril and Regan soon strip him of his retinue and turn him out into the storm, where he goes mad upon the heath beside his Fool and the disguised Edgar. Meanwhile Gloucester, deceived by his bastard son Edmund, is blinded for helping the king. Cordelia returns with a French army, but Lear and she are defeated, and the play ends in the deaths of Cordelia, Lear and almost all the rest.

works.title: King Victor and King Charles: A Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A historical tragedy of the House of Savoy. In 1730 the aged Victor Amadeus, first King of Sardinia, abdicates in favour of his timid son Charles; within a year he regrets it and tries to take the crown back, and the second half of the play follows the son's struggle to keep his throne against his father and the minister D'Ormea.

sections.title: First Year, 1730: King Victor, Part I
First Year, 1730: King Victor, Part II

Second Year, 1731: King Charles, Part II

works.title: The Kingis Quair
works.author: King James I of Scotland
works.blurb: A fifteenth-century dream-vision in 197 rhyme-royal stanzas, attributed to James I of Scotland. A prisoner in a tower sees a lady walking in the garden below, falls in love, and is carried in a dream to Venus, Minerva and Fortune before waking to a sign of favour.

works.title: The King’s Threshold
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: Seanchan, chief poet of Ireland, lies fasting on the steps of King Guaire’s palace because the king has stripped poets of their place at his council. His pupils, the court ladies, a monk and the king himself urge him to eat, and the poet will not give way, even for his sweetheart Fedelm. Yeats’s one-act play, drawn from an old Irish tale, argues the dignity of poetry against power.

works.title: 金槐和歌集 (Kinkai wakashū)
works.subtitle: Collection of the Golden Hall Poems
works.author: Minamoto no Sanetomo
works.blurb: The private collection of the third Kamakura shogun, Minamoto no Sanetomo (1192–1219): 716 waka of the seasons, love and everyday life, in the order of the 1937 edition.

works.title: किरातार्जुनीयम् (Kiratarjuniya)
works.subtitle: Canto I (प्रथमः सर्गः), in the original Sanskrit
works.author: Bharavi
works.blurb: The Arjuna and the Kirata (the hunter-god Shiva in disguise): the great court epic opens as a spy returns to King Yudhishthira in the forest of Dvaitavana with news of Duryodhana's prosperous rule, and Draupadi urges the exiled Pandavas to war. Bharavi's ornate canto is the model of the Sanskrit mahakavya.

works.title: Kitty of the Sherragh Vane
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, Second Series: 2
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A two-part dialect yarn set at the Sherragh Vane, a farm high up Sulby glen, with Kitty and Saul at its centre.

works.title: The Knight of Curtesy
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A poem of 500 lines in four-line stanzas, an English version of the story of the Chastelain de Couci and the lady of Fayel: the knight of Curtesy and the lady of Faguell love in chastity, her jealous husband sends him to fight at Rhodes, and after the knight is killed the husband serves his heart to her at table.

works.title: 古今和歌集 (Kokin wakashū)
works.subtitle: Collection of Ancient and Modern Japanese Poems
works.author: Ki no Tsurayuki
works.blurb: The first imperial anthology of Japanese waka, in twenty books of seasons, love, grief and travel, with its 1,100 poems taken in order.

works.title: Кому на Руси жить хорошо (Komu na Rusi zhit khorosho)
works.subtitle: An epic poem, in the original Russian
works.author: Nikolay Nekrasov
works.blurb: Seven peasants, freed from serfdom in 1861, set out along the high road to find out who in Russia lives happily and at ease: the priest, the landowner, the merchant, the minister or the Tsar.

works.title: 桃花扇 (Taohua shan) — The Peach Blossom Fan
works.author: Kong Shangren
works.blurb: In Nanjing in 1643 the scholar Hou Fangyu, a member of the reformist Restoration Society, falls in love with the courtesan Li Xiangjun and gives her a painted fan as a pledge. The powerful minister Ma Shiying and the eunuch-party schemer Ruan Dacheng, enemies of the Society, force her into marriage with another; she refuses and strikes her head on the floor, and her blood spatters the fan, which a painter turns into peach blossoms. As the Ming court is lost to rebels and Manchus, the lovers are parted and meet again only at the end, when a Daoist priest tears up the fan and sends them both away to the religious life. Kong Shangren's 1699 play, in forty-four scenes of sung verse and speech, sets a love story against the fall of the Southern Ming.

works.title: Konrad Wallenrod
works.subtitle: An Historical Poem
works.author: Adam Mickiewicz
works.blurb: Mickiewicz's narrative poem of 1828 in six cantos: a Lithuanian taken as a boy by the Teutonic Knights rises to be their Grand Master, and, hiding his vengeance behind a mask, leads the Order to ruin. Read in its day as a parable of Poland under Russian rule. Translated by Maude Ashurst Biggs.

works.title: Konrad Wallenrod
works.subtitle: Powieść historyczna z dziejów litewskich i pruskich
works.author: Adam Mickiewicz
works.blurb: Mickiewicz's narrative poem of 1828 in six cantos, in the original Polish: a Lithuanian taken as a boy by the Teutonic Knights rises to be their Grand Master, and, hiding his vengeance behind a mask, leads the Order to ruin. Read in its day as a parable of Poland under Russian rule.

works.title: Kordian
works.subtitle: Część pierwsza trylogii. Spisek koronacyjny
works.author: Juliusz Słowacki
works.blurb: Słowacki's Romantic verse drama of 1834, the first part of a trilogy on the coronation conspiracy: Kordian, a young Pole, passes through love, despair and the Alps to a plot against the Tsar, Nicholas I, in Warsaw, written in answer to the failure of the November Rising.

works.title: Krst pri Savici
works.subtitle: Povest v verzih
works.author: France Prešeren
works.blurb: Prešeren's verse tale of the pagan Slovene chieftain Črtomir, defeated in war against the Christian Valjhun, and of his love for the priestess Bogomila, who has become a Christian. It opens with a sonnet of dedication to the poet's friend Matija Čop, an introduction in terza rima and the narrative proper in ottava rima.

works.title: Kullervo
works.subtitle: Näytelmä viidessä näytöksessä
works.author: Aleksis Kivi
works.blurb: Kullervo (1864) is Aleksis Kivi's verse tragedy in five acts, drawn from the Kullervo cycle of the Kalevala. It won the Finnish state literary prize and is among the foundational works of Finnish drama. This is the original Finnish text, with no English version in the archive.

works.title: कुमारसम्भवम् (Kumarasambhava)
works.subtitle: The Birth of Kumara, cantos 1-8, in the original Sanskrit
works.author: Kalidasa
works.blurb: The courtship of Shiva and Parvati: the goddess's birth to the mountain king Himalaya, the burning of Kama by Shiva's eye, Parvati's penance, her wooing, wedding and wedding night. The eight cantos accepted as Kalidasa's; the later cantos on the birth of Kumara are not included.

works.title: ಕರ್ಣಾಟ ಭಾರತ ಕಥಾಮಂಜರಿ: ಕರ್ಣಪರ್ವ (Karna Parva)
works.subtitle: Karnataka Bharata Kathamanjari, Karna Parva
works.author: Kumaravyasa (Gadugina Naranappa)
works.blurb: The Karna Parva of Kumaravyasa's fifteenth-century Kannada Mahabharata: the seventeen-day war under Karna's command, his duel with Arjuna and his death, in bhamini shatpadi stanzas.

works.title: The Kyng of Tars
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: The Christian king of Tars refuses his daughter to the Sultan of Damascus, who attacks his kingdom; to save her father's people she marries the heathen lord, and bears him a shapeless lump of flesh. Christian baptism turns the lump into a living, fair child, the Sultan renounces his gods and is himself baptised, and the converted Sultan then conquers the lands of his enemies.

works.title: La Araucana
works.subtitle: Epic of the conquest of Chile, in three parts (Cantos I–XXXVII)
works.author: Alonso de Ercilla
works.blurb: Ercilla's epic in 37 cantos of ottava rima on the Spanish war against the Mapuche of Arauco, written by a soldier who took part in it, and the first great epic to give its enemies heroic stature.

works.title: La Jeune Parque
works.author: Paul Valéry
works.blurb: Valéry's first long poem in verse after years of silence, some five hundred alexandrines in which a young Fate, bitten by a serpent, wakes in the night and moves through the stages of a single consciousness towards the dawn.

works.title: Laberinto de Fortuna
works.subtitle: o Las trescientas
works.author: Juan de Mena
works.blurb: Juan de Mena's visionary poem in three hundred coplas de arte mayor, in which a poet is carried by Providence to the palace of Fortune and shown the wheels of past, present and future, with the great figures of Castilian history, addressed to King Juan II.

works.title: The Lady of La Garaye
works.author: Caroline Norton
works.blurb: A verse narrative of the Count and Countess de la Garaye of Brittany, who after her illness and disfigurement gave their lives and fortune to nursing the sick and teaching the poor at Dinan. Norton adds a dedication to the Marquess of Lansdowne, a prologue among ruins and a closing conclusion.

sections.title: Dedication to the Marquess of Lansdowne

works.title: The Lady of the Lake
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A romance of the Scottish Highlands, unfolding over six days on the shores of Loch Katrine, that made Sir Walter Scott the most popular poet in Europe.

works.title: Laili and Majnun
works.subtitle: A poem from the original Persian of Nizami, translated by James Atkinson
works.author: Nizami Ganjavi
works.blurb: The Arab tale of Qays, who is driven mad by love and called Majnun, and of Laili, who is married to another and dies of longing, as Nizami told it in the twelfth century and Atkinson first rendered it into English verse.

works.title: Lalla Rookh
works.subtitle: An Oriental Romance
works.author: Thomas Moore
works.blurb: Thomas Moore's best-selling Oriental romance: four verse tales told to a princess on her journey from Delhi to Kashmir, by the young poet Feramorz.

works.title: Lalla-Vakyani
works.subtitle: The Wise Sayings of Lal Ded
works.author: Lal Ded (Lalleshwari)
works.translator: George A. Grierson and Lionel D. Barnett
works.blurb: The 109 vakhs of the fourteenth-century Kashmiri mystic Lal Ded, in the 1920 English translation of Grierson and Barnett.

works.title: Lamentations
works.subtitle: Authorized Version of Lamentations.
works.author: The Bible (Authorized King James Version)
works.blurb: Five laments for the fallen city of Jerusalem.

works.title: The Lamp and the Bell
works.subtitle: A Drama in Five Acts, written for the Fiftieth Anniversary of the Vassar College Alumnae Association
works.author: Edna St. Vincent Millay
works.blurb: A verse drama set in the kingdoms of Fiori and Lagoverde, in the spirit of the fairy tale of Snow-White and Rose-Red. Beatrice, 'Rose-Red', daughter of King Lorenzo, and Bianca, 'Snow-White', daughter of his second wife Octavia, are stepsisters who love each other dearly, and the play follows their bond across its five acts. It was written for the fiftieth anniversary of the Vassar College Alumnae Association, and includes the songs that Millay also gathered as Three Songs from The Lamp and the Bell.

works.title: Lancelot, or the Knight of the Cart
works.subtitle: Lancelot, ou Le Chevalier de la charrette
works.author: Chrétien de Troyes
works.blurb: Lancelot braves shame and peril to rescue Queen Guinevere from Meleagant; concluded by Godefroi de Leigni.

works.title: Lancelot of the Laik
works.subtitle: A Scottish Metrical Romance
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A Middle Scots romance in decasyllabic couplets, after the French prose Lancelot. A lovesick poet is bidden by a vision to write of Lancelot, then tells of King Arthur at Carlisle, his dreams, the war with Galiot, and Lancelot’s love for Guinevere. The manuscript breaks off in mid-battle.

works.title: Lancelot
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
works.blurb: Blank-verse Arthurian narrative in nine parts: Lancelot, Gawaine, Guinevere and the fall of Arthur's kingdom, as Lancelot rides out in search of the Light.

works.title: The Land of Heart's Desire
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: On a May Eve in the Barony of Kilmacowen, County Sligo, young Mary Bruin, absorbed in an old book of faery tales, is called away from her husband Shawn and her household by a Faery Child who claims her for the land of heart's desire. Father Hart's crucifix and the family's blessings are set against the child's songs of a land where nobody grows old, and Mary must choose between hearth and faeryland.

works.title: L'Atlàntida
works.subtitle: Poema
works.author: Jacint Verdaguer
works.blurb: Verdaguer's epic of the sunken continent: Hercules' crossing of Spain, the drowning of Atlantis through the opened Strait of Gibraltar, and the vision of a new world that is told to the young Columbus.

works.subtitle: A Modern Poem in Twelve Chapters
works.author: William Allingham
works.blurb: Allingham's verse novel of Irish rural life: a young landlord returns to his Ulster-bordering estate and confronts agents, tenants, secret societies and evictions, in twelve chapters of heroic couplets.

works.blurb: The only surviving epic of medieval Kievan Rus', telling of Prince Igor Svyatoslavic's ill-fated raid on the Polovtsy in 1185, his defeat and capture, the lament of his wife Yaroslavna, and his escape home.

works.title: The Lay of the Last Minstrel
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A verse romance of Border feud, magic and thwarted love in sixteenth-century Branksome Hall, framed as the song of the last of the old minstrels.

works.title: Le Bone Florence of Rome
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme romance of about 2,190 lines in twelve-line stanzas: Florence, daughter of the emperor Otes of Rome, is sought in marriage by the aged emperor Garcy, and after her father's death she marries the knight Emere. In his absence she is slandered, driven out and sold at sea, and at last becomes a nun at Beverfayre, where she heals her husband and her enemies.

works.title: Le Grazie
works.subtitle: Tre inni
works.author: Ugo Foscolo
works.blurb: Foscolo's unfinished hymn-cycle to the three Graces, written for the sculptor Canova: Venere tells how the goddess brought the Graces to Italy and tamed its people, Vesta shows them hallowing the home and the Tuscan hills, and Pallade has them weave the veil of the arts and fate.

works.title: A Legend of Florence
works.subtitle: A Play in Five Acts
works.author: Leigh Hunt
works.blurb: In Renaissance Florence the jealous, superstitious Francesco Agolanti suspects his wife Ginevra of loving Antonio Rondinelli, and his cruelty drives her to a seeming death and burial. She wakes in the vault, comes back to life and finds that the only door open to her is the house of the man she was accused of loving. Hunt's blank-verse tragedy takes its story from Boccaccio and the old Florentine legend of the lady who was buried alive.

works.title: The Legend of Good Women
works.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
works.blurb: Commanded by the God of Love to atone for Troilus and Criseyde, the poet dreams a Prologue among daisies and then tells nine legends of women who were faithful in love and betrayed by men.

works.title: The Legends of Saint Patrick
works.author: Aubrey de Vere
works.blurb: Fifteen narrative poems on the conversion of Ireland, from the infant baptism of Patrick to his dying Confession, drawn from the ancient Lives of the saint.

works.title: Leoline and Sydanis
works.subtitle: A Romance of the Amorous Adventures of Princes
works.author: Sir Francis Kynaston
works.blurb: Kynaston's rhyme-royal romance of the Welsh prince Leoline and the Princess Sydanis, enchanted lovers parted by sorcery and reunited after many adventures, first printed in 1642 with the Cynthiades.

works.title: The Lesser Testament
works.subtitle: Le Lais, translated by John Payne
works.author: François Villon
works.blurb: Written at Christmas 1456, as Villon prepared to leave Paris, this is a comic will in which he bequeaths his imaginary property, and his scorn, to friends, enemies and officials of the city.

works.title: Leylâ vü Mecnûn
works.subtitle: Dâstân-ı Leylî vü Mecnûn
works.author: Fuzuli
works.blurb: Fuzuli's mesnevi of the lovers Leylâ and Mecnûn, composed in 1535: the classic Ottoman Turkish telling of the Arab legend of the poet driven mad by love for a woman he cannot marry.

works.title: Χοηφόροι (Choephoroi)
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: The Greek text of this tragedy by Aeschylus in the Smyth Loeb edition, set out by episode and choral division, so that it can be read beside the English verse translation of the same play.

works.title: The Libation-Bearers
works.subtitle: The Oresteia
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: Orestes, banished since boyhood, comes back to his father's tomb at Argos and meets his sister Electra there among the women bearing offerings for the dead. At Apollo's bidding he kills his mother Clytemnestra and her lover Aegisthus to avenge Agamemnon, and is driven out of his wits by the avenging Furies.

works.title: Liberty
works.subtitle: A Poem in Five Parts
works.author: James Thomson
works.blurb: Thomson's blank-verse vision in five parts, in which the Goddess of Liberty traces her course from ancient Greece and Rome through the dark ages to her settled home in Britain.

works.year: c.1330-1343 (ed. Tomás Antonio Sánchez, Poesías del Arcipreste de Hita, Madrid: Antonio de Sancha, 1790)
works.blurb: The Archpriest of Hita's great medieval Castilian poem: a fictional autobiography of failed loves, with beast-fables, the battle of Don Carnal and Doña Cuaresma, the go-between Trotaconventos, mountain-girl songs and hymns to the Virgin.

works.title: The Life and Death of Jason
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: William Morris
works.blurb: Morris's first long narrative poem, in seventeen books of rhymed couplets: Jason's boyhood among the Centaurs, the voyage of the Argo, the winning of the Golden Fleece with Medea's help, and the tragedy of their later life at Iolchos and Corinth.

works.title: The Light of Asia

works.title: The Light of the World
works.subtitle: or, The Great Consummation

works.author: Juliusz Słowacki
works.blurb: Słowacki's verse tragedy, dated Paris 1840 and dedicated to Zygmunt Krasiński, of the legendary Polish past: the conquered Wenedi, a harp-playing people, fall before the Lechites of King Lech and his wife Gwinona, and the king's daughters Lilla and Roza Weneda carry the tragedy of the harp, vengeance and sacrifice through a night of storm.

works.title: The Little Clay Cart
works.subtitle: Mrcchakatika
works.author: Sudraka
works.blurb: The poor Brahman merchant Charudatta and the courtesan Vasantasena love each other in the city of Ujjayini. When she is strangled by the king's brother-in-law Sansthanaka, who then accuses Charudatta of the crime, Charudatta is condemned to death, until Vasantasena, who has survived, appears at the place of execution and a revolution in the kingdom brings his rescue.

works.title: The History of Rome, Books XXXIX–XLV
works.subtitle: Books XXXIX–XLV: Ab Urbe Condita, from the Bacchanalia to the fall of Macedonia
works.author: Livy
works.translator: trans. Rev. Canon William Masfen Roberts (1912-1924)
works.blurb: Livy's narrative from the suppression of the Bacchanalia and the quarrel of Perseus and Demetrius, through the Third Macedonian War, to Pydna and the fall of Macedonia, in the English translation of Canon W. M. Roberts.

works.title: The History of Rome, Books I–VIII
works.subtitle: Ab Urbe Condita, from the founding of the city to 293 BC
works.author: Livy
works.blurb: Livy's narrative of Rome from Aeneas and the foundation of the city, through the kings and the early Republic, to the Samnite wars, in the English translation of D. Spillan.

works.title: The History of Rome, Books IX–XXVI
works.subtitle: Ab Urbe Condita, from the Samnite wars to the fall of Capua
works.author: Livy
works.translator: trans. D. Spillan and Cyrus R. Edmonds (1849-50)
works.blurb: Livy's narrative from the Caudine Forks and the later Samnite wars, through the Pyrrhic and First Punic wars (known for Books XI–XX only from short epitomes), to Hannibal's invasion and the fall of Capua in the Second Punic War, in the English translation of D. Spillan and Cyrus R. Edmonds.

works.title: Locrine: A Tragedy
works.author: Algernon Charles Swinburne
works.blurb: Swinburne's blank-verse tragedy of the legendary British king Locrine, who forsakes his queen Guendolen for the captive princess Estrild. Guendolen raises an army with her son Madan; Locrine is defeated and dies, and Estrild and her daughter Sabrina drown themselves in the river that takes Sabrina's name. A verse dedication to the poet's sister Alice opens the play.

works.title: On the Sublime
works.subtitle: Peri Hupsous
works.author: Longinus
works.blurb: The Greek treatise on what makes writing great, by an anonymous first-century critic traditionally called Longinus, with quoted passages of Homer, Sappho, Plato and Demosthenes.

works.title: Daphnis and Chloe
works.subtitle: A Pastoral Novel
works.author: Longus
works.blurb: Two foundlings, a boy suckled by a goat and a girl nursed by a ewe, are raised by humble herdsmen on Lesbos, and as the seasons turn they discover love, with the help of pirates, rivals, shepherds and Pan, until their birth is revealed and they marry.

works.title: The Lord of the Isles
works.subtitle: A Poem in Six Cantos
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A verse romance of the Scottish Wars of Independence, from Robert the Bruce's return to the Hebrides in 1307 to his victory at Bannockburn, woven round the story of Edith of Lorn.

works.title: Love is Enough, or The Freeing of Pharamond: A Morality
works.subtitle: A Morality
works.author: William Morris
works.blurb: Morris's verse morality, played before a newly wedded Emperor and Empress, tells of King Pharamond, who leaves his throne to seek Love and finds that Love is enough. The play is framed by the peasant couple Giles and Joan and by lyric interludes sung by the Music.

sections.title: Giles and Joan: The Stage Set

Pharamond: In the King's Chamber of Audience
Love, as a Maker of Pictured Cloths
Pharamond: In a Forest among the Hills of a Foreign Land
Love, with the Cup of Bitter Drink
Pharamond: On a Highway in a Valley
Love, Holding a Crown and Palm-Branch
Giles and Joan: After the Play
Giles and Joan: The Way Home

works.title: Love's Labour's Lost
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: The King of Navarre and his three lords swear off women, wealth and sleep for three years of study, only for the Princess of France and her ladies to arrive on an embassy and overturn the oath. Berowne, Longaville and Dumaine each write secret love-verses and are found out in turn, and the lords disguise themselves as Muscovites to woo the ladies, who mock them. A pageant of the Nine Worthies is interrupted by news of the French king's death, and the ladies set the lovers a year's penance, ending with the songs of Spring and Winter.

works.title: The Loves of the Angels
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Thomas Moore
works.blurb: Moore's 1823 poem in which three fallen angels, conversing on a hillside at evening, each tell the story of the mortal woman for whose love he lost heaven.

works.title: Луча микрокозма
works.subtitle: The Ray of the Microcosm (Serbian original)
works.author: Petar II Petrović-Njegoš
works.blurb: Njegoš's philosophical epic on the fall of man, the soul and the cosmos, in the original Serbian: the dedication to Sima Milutinović and six cantos.

works.title: The Works of Lucian of Samosata, Volume I
works.subtitle: Satires and dialogues, from The Vision to the Voyage to the Lower World
works.author: Lucian
works.translator: trans. H. W. and F. G. Fowler (1905)
works.blurb: Fifteen pieces by the Syrian satirist of the Antonine age: his autobiographical Vision, the dialogues of gods, sea-gods and the dead, and the comic fantasies in which Charon, Hermes and Zeus show up the follies of philosophers, priests and the rich.

sections.title: Trial in the Court of Vowels

works.title: The Works of Lucian of Samosata, Volume II
works.subtitle: The Dependent Scholar to Lexiphanes: essays, dialogues, declamations and The True History
works.author: Lucian
works.translator: trans. H. W. and F. G. Fowler (1905)
works.blurb: Seventeen pieces by the Syrian satirist of the Antonine age: the essays on the dependent scholar and on writing history, the philosophical dialogue Hermotimus, the oracle-monger Alexander, the dance-essay Of Pantomime, and The True History, the travellers' tale of a voyage to the moon.

sections.title: A Slip of the Tongue in Salutation

works.title: The Works of Lucian of Samosata, Volume III
works.subtitle: The Life of Demonax to The Fly: biography, dialogues, essays and lectures
works.author: Lucian
works.translator: trans. H. W. and F. G. Fowler (1905)
works.blurb: Nineteen pieces by the Syrian satirist of the Antonine age: the Life of Demonax, the two Portrait-Study essays, Toxaris on friendship, the Zeus dialogues, Icaromenippus and its flight to heaven, The Parasite, Anacharsis, and the comic lectures on Dionysus, Heracles, the Fly and the book-collector.

sections.title: The Parasite, a Demonstration That Sponging Is a Profession
Anacharsis, a Discussion of Physical Training
Remarks Addressed to an Illiterate Book-Fancier

works.title: The Works of Lucian of Samosata, Volume IV
works.subtitle: Slander, a Warning to The Purist Purized: essays, dialogues, the Peregrine and the Saturnalia
works.author: Lucian
works.translator: trans. H. W. and F. G. Fowler (1905)
works.blurb: Fifteen pieces by the Syrian satirist of the Antonine age: the essays on Slander, the Hall and Patriotism, the voyage-and-wishes dialogue The Ship, the Dialogues of the Hetaerae, the death of the Cynic Peregrine, the Saturnalia with its festival laws and letters, the quarrelsome philosophers' banquet of A Feast of Lapithae, and the comic assemblies of The Gods in Council and The Purist Purized.

works.title: Lucifer (Lucifer)
works.subtitle: Treurspel
works.author: Joost van den Vondel
works.blurb: Vondel's Lucifer (1654) stages the revolt of the angels in Heaven, in Dutch alexandrines. Each of the five acts closes with a chorus of angels.

works.title: Lucifer: A Theological Tragedy
works.author: George Santayana
works.blurb: Santayana's only verse tragedy, in five acts. Lucifer, exiled from Heaven, lives in loneliness on a frozen mountain island, with Hermes as his unlikely companion. Zeus sends Hermes to him, Mephistopheles schemes to bring him back to the old wars, and at last he stands before the Risen Christ at the gates of Heaven. The play, in the end, is a meditation on pride, love and the passing of the gods.

works.title: Lucifer
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Joost van den Vondel
works.blurb: Vondel's Lucifer (1654) stages the revolt in Heaven. When the herald Gabriel announces that God means to set man, still unborn in Paradise, above the angels, the proud Lucifer and his followers, Belzebub, Belial and Apollion among them, resolve to rebel. Michael leads the loyal host against them, the rebels are cast down into hell, and the angels' chorus closes the play with the promise of a Redeemer. The Dutch poet's drama has long been compared with Milton's Paradise Lost.

works.title: Lucile
works.author: Robert Bulwer-Lytton, Earl of Lytton (Owen Meredith)
works.blurb: A verse novel in twelve cantos: the Comtesse de Nevers, once the lover of Lord Alfred Vargrave, calls him to Luchon on the eve of his marriage, and a story of renunciation and loyalty unfolds.

works.title: Ludus Coventriae (N-Town Plays)
works.subtitle: The Coventry Mysteries, ed. J. O. Halliwell (1841)
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A cycle of forty-two mystery plays in East Anglian Middle English, written down in the fifteenth century (British Library, Cotton MS Vespasian D. VIII) and long known as the Ludus Coventriae because Halliwell and earlier antiquaries took it for the Corpus Christi plays of Coventry. It is now called the N-Town cycle, from the Banns' call for players to appear 'in N. towne'. A Proclamation by three banner-bearers announces the pageants, which run from the Creation and the Fall through the life of Mary, the birth, ministry, trial and Crucifixion of Christ, to the Resurrection, the Assumption of the Virgin and Doomsday.

sections.title: The Trial of Joseph and Mary
The Condemnation and Crucifixion of Christ
The Descent of the Holy Ghost

works.title: Luria: A Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A tragedy of Renaissance Florence. Luria, a Moorish general serving the Republic against Pisa, wins his campaign but learns that the Florentine commissary Braccio has already prepared the charges that will destroy him once the war is over. Loyal to the end, he chooses his own way out.

works.title: The Lusiad, or Portugals Historicall Poem
works.subtitle: Os Lusíadas
works.author: Luís de Camões
works.blurb: Camões's national epic of Vasco da Gama's voyage to India and the story of Portugal, in ten cantos of ottava rima, first Englished by Sir Richard Fanshawe in 1655.

works.title: The Lusiad; or, The Discovery of India
works.subtitle: Os Lusíadas
works.author: Luís de Camões
works.translator: trans. William Julius Mickle (1776), rev. E. Richmond Hodges (1877)
works.blurb: Camões's national epic of Vasco da Gama's voyage to India and the story of Portugal, in ten books, rendered into English heroic couplets by William Julius Mickle.

works.title: The Lusiads
works.subtitle: Os Lusíadas
works.author: Luís de Camões
works.blurb: Camões's national epic of Vasco da Gama's voyage to India and the story of Portugal, in ten cantos of ottava rima, rendered into English by Sir Richard Francis Burton.

works.title: Lybeaus Disconus
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Gawain's son, raised in a forest by his mother and not knowing his own name, takes the armour of a slain knight and is knighted by King Arthur as Lybeaus Disconus, the Fair Unknown. He rides out with the lady Elene and her dwarf to free the Lady of Synadowne, defeating Maugys, Lambard, Gyffroun and other champions on the way, and at last frees the lady from her enchantment by a kiss.

works.title: Lycidus; or, The Lover in Fashion
works.subtitle: The songs
works.author: Aphra Behn
works.blurb: The verse songs of Behn's prose tale of Lycidus, a fashionable rake's account of his own voyage to the Isle of Love, with its amorous pursuits and its farewell to love.
