works.title: Ane Dialog betuix Experience and ane Courteour
works.subtitle: The Monarche
works.author: Sir David Lyndsay
works.blurb: A long dialogue in Middle Scots, written in 1553, in which the old courtier-turned-sage Experience instructs a Courteour on the misery of the world, rehearsing the history of the four great monarchies from Creation to the Last Judgement and attacking idolatry and the abuses of Church and state.

works.title: Speeches
works.author: Lysias
works.blurb: Thirty-four law-court speeches by the Athenian speech-writer Lysias, from the murder trial of Eratosthenes to the Funeral Oration, in Lamb's Loeb translation.

works.title: 破幽夢孤雁漢宮秋 (Han gong qiu) — Autumn in the Han Palace
works.author: Ma Chih-yüan
works.blurb: Ma Zhiyuan's Yuan zaju in a prologue and four acts: the Han emperor Yuan sends his beloved consort Wang Zhaojun to the Xiongnu khan, and mourns her after she drowns herself in the Amur.

works.title: The Sorrows of Han
works.subtitle: Autumn in the Han Palace
works.author: Ma Chih-yüan
works.blurb: John Francis Davis's 1829 English version of Ma Zhiyuan's Han gong qiu, the first Chinese play published in English, as reprinted in Epiphanius Wilson's Chinese Literature (1900).

works.title: The Tragedy of Macbeth
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Returning from battle, the Scottish general Macbeth is hailed by three witches as future king. Urged on by Lady Macbeth, he murders King Duncan in his sleep and seizes the throne, then kills Banquo and Macduff's family to secure it. Haunted by guilt, and by Banquo's ghost, he falls to the English army and Macduff at Dunsinane, as Birnam Wood seems to come against him. The play ends with Malcolm proclaimed king.

works.title: Macduff's Cross
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: Two monks of Lindores keep watch at MacDuff's Cross, a Fife sanctuary for any kinsman of the Thane who has killed in sudden quarrel. Maurice Berkeley, who is said to have slain Lord Louis Lindesay of Edzell over Lindesay's wife, claims its protection, and Lindesay's brother Richard comes after him with drawn sword. Then the second monk, Waldhave, throws back his cowl and proves to be Louis himself, alive, and the feud is ended.

works.title: The Madness of Herakles
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: While Herakles is away in the Underworld on his last labour, the usurper Lykus threatens to kill his wife, sons and aged father; the hero returns in time to save them, only for Hera to send Madness upon him. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy in English verse, with the choral odes in rhymed lyric measures.

works.title: Madoc
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Two Parts
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: The Welsh prince Madoc sails west across the Atlantic, finds a new land, and returns to Wales for settlers; on his second voyage he wars with the Aztecs and overthrows their bloody gods.

works.title: Mador of the Moor
works.author: James Hogg
works.blurb: A romance of fourteenth-century Scotland in Spenserian stanzas, in five cantos with an introduction and a conclusion, of the lost Mador and a king's night in the Highlands.

works.title: Magnyfycence
works.subtitle: A Goodly Interlude and a Mery
works.author: John Skelton
works.blurb: A morality interlude in rhyme royal. The prince Magnyfycence, advised by Measure, is flattered by the courtiers Counterfet Countenaunce, Crafty Conueyaunce and Cloked Colusyon, who lead him to dismiss restraint and spend with Lyberte and Fansy. Adversity strikes him down and Poverty, Despair and Mischief bring him to the edge of self-murder, until Goodhope, Redresse and Sad Circumspeccyon raise him up and restore him to his state. Skelton's warning to the court of Henry VIII on the fall of great men.

works.title: Maha-bharata
works.subtitle: The Epic of Ancient India Condensed into English Verse
works.author: Vyasa
works.blurb: Romesh Chunder Dutt's condensed English rendering of the great Sanskrit epic of the Kuru and Pandava war, in twelve books of rhymed couplets, from the tournament at Hastina to the sacrifice of the horse. Published by J. M. Dent and Co., Aldine House, London, 1899.

sections.title: Book XII: Sacrifice of the Horse

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 1: Adi Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Beginning
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 1 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta, from 1883. The Adi Parva tells how the epic came to be recited, the stories of the Bharata line, the birth and upbringing of the Kauravas and Pandavas, and the winning of Draupadi, down to the burning of the Khandava forest.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 10: Sauptika Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Sleeping Warriors
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 10 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Sauptika Parva recounts the night massacre: Ashvatthama, resolving on revenge for the dying Duryodhana, kills the sleeping Pandava camp, and the Aishika weapon is loosed and turned aside.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 11: Stri Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Women
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 11 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Stri Parva is the lament of the women: Dhritarashtra's grief and anger, Gandhari's curse, the widows moving over the field of Kurukshetra among the dead, and the funeral rites for the fallen.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 12: Santi Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of Peace
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 12 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Santi Parva, the longest book of the epic, opens with Bhishma lying on his bed of arrows after the war, instructing the grieving Yudhishthira on the duties of kings, on conduct in times of distress, and on the paths to liberation.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 13: Anusasana Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of Instructions
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 13 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Anusasana Parva gives Bhishma's further teaching on gifts, duties and the merit of deeds, ending with his death and ascent.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 14: Aswamedhika Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Horse Sacrifice
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 14 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Aswamedhika Parva tells of the horse sacrifice by which Yudhishthira, once the war is over and the kingdom secure, claims the sovereignty of the earth. Before it Krishna relates the Anugita, a philosophical discourse to Arjuna, and Arjuna follows the sacrificial horse on its wanderings, fighting its opponents.

works.title: Book 15: Asramavasika Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Hermitage
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 15 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Asramavasika Parva follows the old king Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Kunti as they leave the city for a hermitage in the forest, where the dead of the war are briefly seen again, and ends with the forest fire in which they die.

works.title: Book 16: Mausala Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Clubs
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 16 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Mausala Parva records the destruction of the Vrishni clan, who slaughter one another with iron clubs thirty-six years after the war, and the departure of Krishna and Balarama from the world.

works.title: Book 17: Mahaprasthanika Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Great Journey
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 17 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. In the Mahaprasthanika Parva the Pandavas renounce the kingdom and walk north toward the Himalaya, and one by one Draupadi and four of her husbands fall by the way.

works.title: Book 18: Svargarohanika Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Ascent to Heaven
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 18 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Svargarohanika Parva brings the epic to its close: Yudhishthira's trial at the gates of Heaven, his sight of Hell, the reunion of the heroes, and the closing words on the merit of hearing the Mahabharata.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 2: Sabha Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Assembly Hall
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 2 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Sabha Parva tells of the building of Yudhishthira's great assembly hall, the Rajasuya sacrifice, the death of Sisupala, and the fateful game of dice.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 3: Vana Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Forest
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 3 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Vana Parva tells of the twelve years of the Pandavas' exile in the forest after the game of dice, with the tale of Nala and Damayanti, the pilgrimages, Arjuna's quest for celestial weapons, and the Yaksha's riddling questions.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 4: Virata Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of Virata
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 4 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Virata Parva tells of the thirteenth year of exile, when the Pandavas live in disguise at the court of King Virata, the slaying of Kichaka, and the great cattle raid and battle against the Kauravas.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 5: Udyoga Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of the Effort
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 5 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Udyoga Parva tells of the Pandavas' return from exile and the fruitless diplomacy that precedes the war: the embassies and Krishna's failed peace mission to the Kuru court, the counsel of Vidura and Sanat-sujata, the story of Amba, and the marshalling of the two armies at Kurukshetra.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 6: Bhishma Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of Bhishma
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 6 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Bhishma Parva opens the great war at Kurukshetra and holds the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna's teaching to Arjuna on the eve of battle; it follows the first ten days of fighting under Bhishma's command until he falls on a bed of arrows.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 7: Drona Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of Drona
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 7 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Drona Parva narrates the five days of battle under Drona's command: the death of Abhimanyu in the wheel formation, the slaying of Jayadratha, the night battle in which Ghatotkacha falls, and the stratagem by which Drona himself is killed.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 8: Karna Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of Karna
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 8 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Karna Parva narrates the two days of battle under Karna's command as Kaurava commander: the long single combats, Karna's quarrel with his charioteer Shalya, the death of Dushasana at Bhima's hands, and Karna's fall to Arjuna when his chariot wheel sinks in the earth.

works.title: The Mahabharata, Book 9: Shalya Parva
works.subtitle: The Book of Shalya
works.author: Vyasa
works.translator: trans. Kisari Mohan Ganguli (published by Pratap Chandra Roy, 1883–1896)
works.blurb: Book 9 of Kisari Mohan Ganguli's complete English prose translation of the Mahabharata, published in parts by Pratap Chandra Roy, Calcutta. The Shalya Parva tells of the last day of the great battle: Shalya's brief command and death at Yudhishthira's hands, the fall of Shakuni, Duryodhana's flight and hiding in the lake, Baladeva's pilgrimage along the Sarasvati, and the mace duel in which Bhima breaks Duryodhana's thigh.

works.title: The Maid's Tragedy
works.author: Francis Beaumont and John Fletcher
works.blurb: At the court of Rhodes the young lord Amintor is commanded by the King to abandon his betrothed Aspatia and marry Evadne, only to learn on his wedding night that his bride is the King's mistress and has married him as a screen. Evadne's brother Melantius, a soldier, is drawn into the secret and resolves on revenge. Evadne herself, shamed into repentance, kills the sleeping King, while the forsaken Aspatia, disguised as a man, seeks death at Amintor's hands. The play ends in a heap of corpses.

works.title: Máj
works.author: Karel Hynek Mácha
works.blurb: Mácha's Romantic lyrical-epic poem of love, murder and execution, in four cantos with two intermezzos, set on a May evening by a lake.

works.blurb: Nizami's first poem and the opening book of the Khamsa, a didactic masnavi in twenty discourses, completed around 1176: the original text, in Ganjoor's section order.

works.title: 万葉集 (Man'yōshū)
works.subtitle: Collection of Ten Thousand Leaves
works.author: Otomo no Yakamochi
works.blurb: Japan's oldest anthology of poetry, in twenty books of court songs, love poems, laments and eastern folk verse, with its 4,516 numbered poems taken in order.

works.title: Meditations
works.subtitle: The Thoughts of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus
works.author: Marcus Aurelius
works.blurb: The private notebook of the Stoic emperor, twelve books of reflections on duty, mortality and the governing mind.

works.title: Mari Magno; or, Tales on Board
works.author: Arthur Hugh Clough
works.blurb: Tales told by passengers on an Atlantic steamer, on the subject of love and marriage: here the traveller’s own tale and the lawyer’s second.

sections.title: My Tale: A la Banquette; or, a Modern Pilgrimage

works.title: Maria
works.subtitle: Powieść ukraińska
works.author: Antoni Malczewski
works.blurb: A Ukrainian tale in two cantos: the love of Maria and Wacław on the steppe, ended by the will of her father, the voivode, and by death. The classic poem of the Polish Ukrainian school of Romanticism.

works.title: Marien’s Pilgrimage
works.subtitle: A Fire-Side Story
works.author: Mary Howitt
works.blurb: Howitt’s story of a child, Marien, who wanders across the world on a mission of Christian love, told in twelve parts.

works.title: Marína
works.subtitle: Ľúbostná básnická skladba
works.author: Andrej Sládkovič
works.blurb: The great Slovak Romantic love poem of the Štúr generation: a hundred ten-line stanzas in praise of Marína, the poet's beloved, in whom Tatra landscape, nation and ideal beauty are joined.

works.title: Marino Faliero, Doge of Venice
works.subtitle: An Historical Tragedy
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's tragedy in five acts, first published in 1821, on the fourteenth-century Doge of Venice. Marino Faliero, an old man whose appeal for justice against the patrician Michel Steno's insult is dismissed by the Forty as a trifling punishment, is drawn by the plebeian leader Israel Bertuccio into a conspiracy to overthrow the aristocratic Council. The plot is betrayed, the conspirators are condemned by the Council of Ten, and the Doge is sentenced to death and beheaded on the Giants' Staircase.

works.title: Marlowe: A Drama in Five Acts
works.author: Josephine Preston Peabody
works.blurb: Christopher Marlowe, fresh from the triumph of Doctor Faustus, meets Alison, a Canterbury girl who is struck by his poetry and by the man himself, while a great lady at court draws him the other way. Three years on, with the plague in London, the lady has disowned him, the informer Richard Bame is gathering evidence of his atheism, and Alison has married her faithful neighbour Gabriel. Marlowe makes a last pilgrimage to her farmhouse near Canterbury, then returns to the Deptford tavern where, on 1 June 1593, a quarrel starts and he is killed.

works.title: Marmion
works.subtitle: A Tale of Flodden Field
works.author: Sir Walter Scott
works.blurb: A verse romance of treachery and doomed love set against the Scottish army's march to its catastrophic defeat at Flodden in 1513.

works.title: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's satirical prophetic book, engraved in the early 1790s, overturns the moral order of Heaven and Hell: Energy is Eternal Delight, and the Devil's party speaks for Genius and Imagination. Blending verse, aphorism, parable and prose, it sets the Proverbs of Hell beside five Memorable Fancies and closes with A Song of Liberty, a visionary salute to the revolutions of his age.

works.title: El gaucho Martín Fierro
works.author: José Hernández
works.blurb: A gaucho of the Argentine pampas sings the story of his conscription, his flight and his outlawry, in six-line stanzas.

works.title: The Martyrdom of Polycarp
works.subtitle: A letter of the Church of Smyrna
works.author: The Apostolic Fathers
works.blurb: The earliest surviving account of a Christian martyrdom, written by the Church of Smyrna to the Church of Philomelium: the arrest, trial and burning of the aged bishop Polycarp.

works.title: Mary Quayle
works.subtitle: The Curate's Story
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: The Curate's Story: a tale in English verse that opens with a climb up Barrule on the north-east side of the Isle of Man.

works.title: مثنوی معنوی، دفتر اول: سرآغاز (Masnavi, Book 1: opening)
works.author: Jalal al-Din Rumi
works.blurb: The opening of Rumi's Masnavi in the original Persian: the lament of the reed-flute, the story of the king and the slave girl, and the tale of the goldsmith, each section titled as on Ganjoor.

بخش ۱۰۶ - اظهار معجزهٔ پیغمبر صلی الله علیه و سلم به سخن آمدن سنگ‌ریزه در دست ابوجهل علیه اللعنه و گواهی دادن سنگ‌ریزه بر حقیت محمد صلی الله علیه و سلم به رسالت او
بخش ۱۰۷ - بقیهٔ قصهٔ مطرب و پیغام رسانیدن امیرالمؤمنین عُمَر -رضی الله عنه- به او آنچه هاتف آواز داد
بخش ۱۰۸ - گردانیدن عمر رضی الله عنه نظر او را از مقام گریه کی هستیست به مقام استغراق
بخش ۱۰۹ - تفسیر دعای آن دو فرشته کی هر روز بر سر هر بازاری منادی می‌کنند کی اللهم اعط کل منفق خلفا اللهم اعط کل ممسک تلفا و بیان کردن کی آن منفق مجاهد راه حقست نی مسرف راه هوا
بخش ۱۱۰ - قصهٔ خلیفه کی در کرم در زمان خود از حاتم طائی گذشته بود و نظیر خود نداشت
بخش ۱۱۱ - قصهٔ اعرابی درویش و ماجرای زن با او به سبب قلت و درویشی
بخش ۱۱۲ - مغرور شدن مریدان محتاج به مدعیان مزور و ایشان را شیخ و محتشم و واصل پنداشتن و نقل را از نقد فرق نادانستن و بر بسته را از بر رسته

بخش ۱۱۳ - در بیان آنک نادر افتد کی مریدی در مدعی مزور اعتقاد بصدق ببندد کی او کسی است و بدین اعتقاد به مقامی برسد کی شیخش در خواب ندیده باشد و آب و آتش او را گزند نکند و شیخش را گزند کند ولیکن بنادر نادر
بخش ۱۱۴ - صبر فرمودن اعرابی زن خود را و فضیلت صبر و فقر بیان کردن با زن

بخش ۱۱۵ - نصحیت کردن زن مر شوی را کی سخن افزون از قدم و از مقام خود مگو لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون کی این سخن‌ها اگرچه راستست این مقام توکل ترا نیست و این سخن گفتن فوق مقام و معاملهٔ خود زیان دارد و کبر مقتا عند الله باشد
بخش ۱۱۶ - نصیحت کردن مرد مر زن را کی در فقیران به خواری منگر و در کار حق به گمان کمال نگر و طعنه مزن در فقر و فقیران به خیال و گمان بی‌نوایی خویشتن

بخش ۱۱۷ - در بیان آنک جنبیدن هر کسی از آنجا کی ویست هر کس را از چنبرهٔ وجود خود بیند تابهٔ کبود آفتاب را کبود نماید و سرخ سرخ نماید چون تابه‌ها از رنگها بیرون آید سپید شود از همه تابه‌های دیگر او راست‌گوتر باشد و امام باشد
بخش ۱۱۸ - مراعات کردن زن شوهر را و استغفار کردن از گفتهٔ خویش
بخش ۱۱۹ - در بیان این خبر کی انهن یغلبن العاقل و یغلبهن الجاهل
بخش ۱۲۰ - تسلیم کردن مرد خود را به آنچ التماس زن بود از طلب معیشت و آن اعتراضِ زن را اشارات حق دانستن. به نزد عقلِ هر داننده ای هست، که با گردنده گرداننده ای هست
بخش ۱۲۱ - در بیان آنک موسی و فرعون هر دو مسخر مشیت‌اند چنانک زهر و پازهر و ظلمات و نور و مناجات کردن فرعون بخلوت تا ناموس نشکند
بخش ۱۲۲ - سبب حرمان اشقیا از دو جهان کی خسر الدنیا و الآخرة

بخش ۱۲۳ - حقیر و بی‌خصم دیدن دیده‌های حس صالح و ناقهٔ صالح علیه‌السلام را چون خواهد کی حق لشکری را هلاک کند در نظر ایشان حقیر نماید خصمان را و اندک اگرچه غالب باشد آن خصم و یقللکم فی اعینهم لیقضی الله امرا کان مفعولا
بخش ۱۲۴ - در معنی آنک مرج البحرین یلتقیان بینهما برزخ لا یبغیان

بخش ۱۲۵ - در معنی آنک آنچ ولی کند مرید را نشاید گستاخی کردن و همان فعل کردن کی حلوا طبیب را زیان ندارد اما بیماران را زیان دارد و سرما و برف انگور را زیان ندارد اما غوره را زیان دارد کی در راهست کی لیغفرلک الله ما تقدم من ذنبک و ما تاخر
بخش ۱۲۶ - مخلص ماجرای عرب و جفت او
بخش ۱۲۷ - دل نهادن عرب بر التماس دلبر خویش و سوگند خوردن کی درین تسلیم مرا حیلتی و امتحانی نیست
بخش ۱۲۸ - تعیین کردن زن طریق طلب روزی کدخدای خود را و قبول کردن او
بخش ۱۲۹ - هدیه بردن عرب سبوی آب باران از میان بادیه سوی بغداد به امیرالمؤمنین بر پنداشت آنک آنجا هم قحط آبست
بخش ۱۳۰ - در نمد دوختن زن عرب سبوی آب باران را و مهر نهادن بر وی از غایت اعتقاد عرب

بخش ۱۳۱ - در بیان آنک چنانک گدا عاشق کرمست و عاشق کریم، کرمِ کریم هم عاشق گداست اگر گدا را صبر بیش بود کریم بر در او آید و اگر کریم را صبر بیش بود گدا بر در او آید اما صبر گدا کمال گداست و صبر کریم نقصان اوست
بخش ۱۳۲ - فرق میان آنک درویش است به خدا و تشنهٔ خدا و میان آنک درویش است از خدا و تشنهٔ غیرست
بخش ۱۳۳ - پیش آمدن نقیبان و دربانان خلیفه از بهر اکرام اعرابی و پذیرفتن هدیهٔ او را

بخش ۱۳۴ - در بیان آنک عاشق دنیا بر مثال عاشق دیواریست کی بر او تاب آفتاب زند و جهد و جهاد نکرد تا فهم کند کی آن تاب و رونق از دیوار نیست از قرص آفتابست در آسمان چهارم لاجرم کلی دل بر دیوار نهاد چون پرتو آفتاب به آفتاب پیوست او محروم ماند ابدا و حیل بینهم و بین ما یشتهون
بخش ۱۳۵ - مثل عرب اذا زنیت فازن بالحرة و اذا سرقت فاسرق الدرة
بخش ۱۳۶ - سپردن عرب هدیه را یعنی سبو را به  غلامان خلیفه
بخش ۱۳۷ - حکایت ماجرای نحوی و کشتیبان
بخش ۱۳۸ - قبول کردن خلیفه هدیه را و عطا فرمودن با کمال بی‌نیازی از آن هدیه و از آن سبو
بخش ۱۳۹ - در صفت پیر و مطاوعت وی
بخش ۱۴۰ - وصیت کردن رسول صلی الله علیه و سلم مر علی را کرم الله وجهه کی چون هر کسی به نوع طاعتی تقرب جوید به حق، تو تقرب جوی به صحبت عاقل و بندهٔ خاص تا ازیشان همه پیش‌قدم‌تر باشی
بخش ۱۴۱ - کبودی زدن قزوینی بر شانه‌گاه صورت شیر و پشیمان شدن او به سبب زخم سوزن
بخش ۱۴۲ - رفتن گرگ و روباه در خدمت شیر به شکار
بخش ۱۴۳ - امتحان کردن شیر گرگ را و گفتن کی پیش آی ای گرگ بخش کن صیدها را میان ما
بخش ۱۴۴ - قصه آنکس کی در یاری بکوفت از درون گفت کیست آن گفت منم گفت چون تو توی در نمی‌گشایم هیچ کس را از یاران نمی‌شناسم کی او من باشد برو
بخش ۱۴۵ - ادب کردن شیر گرگ را کی در قسمت بی‌ادبی کرده بود
بخش ۱۴۶ - تهدید کردن نوح علیه‌السلام مر قوم را کی با من مپیچید کی من روپوشم با خدای می‌پیچید در میان این بحقیقت ای مخذولان
بخش ۱۴۷ - نشاندن پادشاه، صوفیانِ عارف را پیش روی خویش تا چشمشان بدیشان روشن شود
بخش ۱۴۸ - آمدن مهمان پیش یوسف علیه‌السلام و تقاضا کردن یوسف علیه‌السلام ازو تحفه و ارمغان
بخش ۱۴۹ - گفتن مهمان یوسف علیه‌السلام کی آینه‌ای آوردمت کی تا هر باری کی در وی نگری روی خوب خویش را بینی مرا یاد کنی
بخش ۱۵۰ - مرتد شدن کاتب وحی به سبب آنک پرتو وحی برو زد آن آیت را پیش از پیغامبر صلی الله علیه و سلم بخواند گفت پس من هم محل وحیم
بخش ۱۵۱ - دعا کردن بلعم با عور کی موسی و قومش را از این شهر کی حصار داده‌اند بی مراد باز گردان و مستجاب شدن دعای او
بخش ۱۵۲ - اعتماد کردن هاروت و ماروت بر عصمت خویش و امیری اهل دنیا خواستن و در فتنه افتادن
بخش ۱۵۳ - باقی قصهٔ هاروت و ماروت و نکال و عقوبت ایشان هم در دنیا بچاه بابل
بخش ۱۵۴ - به عیادت رفتن کر بر همسایهٔ رنجور خویش
بخش ۱۵۵ - اول کسی کی در مقابلهٔ نص قیاس آورد ابلیس بود
بخش ۱۵۶ - در بیان آنک حال خود و مستی خود پنهان باید داشت از جاهلان
بخش ۱۵۷ - قصهٔ مری کردن رومیان و چینیان در علم نقاشی و صورت‌گری
بخش ۱۵۸ - پرسیدن پیغمبر صلی الله علیه و سلم مر زید  را که امروز چونی و چون برخاستی و جواب  گفتن او که اصبحت مؤمنا یا رسول الله
بخش ۱۵۹ - متهم کردن غلامان و خواجه‌تاشان مر لقمان را کی آن میوه‌های ترونده را که می‌آوردیم او خورده است
بخش ۱۶۰ - بقیهٔ قصه زید در جواب رسول صلی الله علیه و سلم
بخش ۱۶۱ - گفتن پیغامبر صلی الله علیه و سلم مر زید را کی این سر را فاش‌تر ازین مگو و متابعت نگهدار
بخش ۱۶۳ - آتش افتادن در شهر به ایام عمر رضی الله عنه
بخش ۱۶۴ - خدو انداختن خصم در روی امیر المؤمنین علی کرم الله وجهه و انداختن امیرالمؤمنین علی شمشیر از دست
بخش ۱۶۵ - سؤال کردن آن کافر از علی کرم الله وجهه کی بر چون منی مظفر شدی شمشیر از دست چون انداختی
بخش ۱۶۶ - جواب گفتن امیر المؤمنین کی سبب افکندن شمشیر از دست چه بوده است  در آن حالت
بخش ۱۶۷ - گفتن پیغامبر صلی الله علیه و سلم به گوش رکابدار امیرالمؤمنین علی کرم الله  وجهه کی کشتن علی بر دست تو خواهد بودن خبرت کردم
بخش ۱۶۸ - تعجب کردن آدم علیه‌السلام از ضلالت  ابلیس لعین و عجب آوردن
بخش ۱۶۹ - بازگشتن به حکایت علی کرم الله وجهه و مسامحت کردن او با خونی خویش
بخش ۱۷۰ - افتادن رکابدار هر باری پیش امیر المؤمنین علی کرم الله وجهه کی ای امیر المؤمنین مرا بکش و ازین قضا برهان
بخش ۱۷۱ - بیان آنک فتح طلبیدن مصطفی صلی الله علیه و سلم مکه را و غیر مکه را جهت دوستی ملک دنیا نبود چون فرموده است الدنیا جیفة بلک بامر بود
بخش ۱۷۲ - گفتن امیر المؤمنین علی کرم الله وجهه با قرین خود کی چون خدو انداختی در روی من نفس من جنبید و اخلاص عمل نماند مانع کشتن تو آن شد

works.title: The Masnavi (abridged), Books I–VI
works.subtitle: The Spiritual Couplets, abridged and translated by E. H. Whinfield
works.author: Jalal al-Din Rumi
works.blurb: Rumi's great Persian Sufi teaching poem in six books, here in E. H. Whinfield's abridged English version, opening with the lament of the reed-flute torn from its reed-bed and moving through tales of the prince and the handmaid, the lion and the beasts, the harper and 'Omar, and the elephant in the dark room.

works.title: The Masque of Judgment
works.subtitle: A Masque-Drama in Five Acts and a Prelude
works.author: William Vaughn Moody
works.blurb: On the eve of the Incarnation the archangel Raphael, half in love with earth, is warned by the Angel of the Pale Horse that God means to judge mankind, and the five acts follow Raphael through Heaven's anguish, the Crucifixion, the Day of Judgment in its valley of the lost, and the Worm that dieth not, until he is left alone at the edge of the battle for Heaven.

works.title: The Masque of Pandora
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A masque on the Greek myth. Hephaestus fashions Pandora from clay and Zeus gives her life; Hermes carries her to Epimetheus, brother of the chained Prometheus, who warns against receiving gifts from the gods. Pandora, given a mysterious casket, cannot resist opening it, and all the evils fly out into the world, while Hope alone remains. Choruses of Graces, Fates, Furies, Dreams and Eumenides comment on the action.

works.title: Maud
works.subtitle: A Monodrama
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: A young man, embittered by his father's ruin and death, finds love and hope in Maud, then loses her in a duel, and passes through madness toward a stern new purpose.

works.title: A Continuation of Lucan's Historicall Poem
works.subtitle: till the death of Iulius Caesar
works.author: Thomas May
works.blurb: Thomas May's own seven-book English epic in heroic couplets, written to carry Lucan's unfinished story of the civil war on from Caesar at Alexandria to his assassination.

works.title: The Mayor of Zalamea
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: Soldiers of Philip II are quartered at Zalamea, and the Captain dishonours the daughter of Pedro Crespo, a prosperous farmer. Crespo, newly made Mayor, arrests the Captain and has him judged and executed, and the King upholds his justice. The one play in the volume FitzGerald says was already well known.

works.title: Measure for Measure
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Duke Vincentio of Vienna pretends to leave the city and, disguised as a friar, hands his strict deputy Angelo the enforcement of laws long neglected. Angelo condemns Claudio to death for fathering a child out of wedlock, then offers to spare him if Claudio’s sister Isabella, a novice nun, will yield herself to him. Isabella refuses, and the Duke, watching in disguise, contrives a bed-trick that substitutes Angelo’s abandoned betrothed Mariana, and finally unmasks himself in a public reckoning of justice and mercy.

works.title: Μήδεια (Medeia)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Medea, a sorceress from Colchis who helped Jason win the Golden Fleece and left her home for him, is cast aside in Corinth when he marries the king's daughter Glauke. Creon banishes her, but she wins one day's grace, wins a promise of refuge in Athens from the childless king Aigeus, and feigns reconciliation with Jason. She sends the princess a poisoned robe and crown, which kill both Glauke and Creon, and then, to wound Jason beyond repair, kills her own two sons. She escapes Corinth in the chariot of her grandfather the Sun. The Greek text is given in the order of the Nauck edition, so that it pairs with the English translations of the same play.

works.title: Medea
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Medea, cast off by Jason and exiled from Corinth, takes vengeance by killing his new bride and her father, and then her own two sons.

works.title: Medea
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: On the day of her husband Jason’s wedding to Creusa, the princess of Corinth, the Colchian sorceress Medea is ordered into exile by King Creon. She wins one day’s grace and spends it on vengeance: she sends the bride a poisoned robe and crown that burn her and her father to death. Then, to wound Jason beyond healing, she kills the two sons she has borne him before his eyes and escapes through the air in a chariot drawn by dragons.

works.title: Medea
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Abandoned in Corinth by Jason, who has taken the king's daughter as his new bride, the sorceress Medea plans a vengeance that will cost her what she loves most. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: मेघदूतम् (Meghaduta)
works.subtitle: The Cloud Messenger, in the original Sanskrit
works.author: Kalidasa
works.blurb: A yaksha, exiled for a year from his home and his wife, sends a monsoon cloud as messenger from the hills of Ramagiri to the Himalayan city of Alaka, describing the route and the beloved who waits there. Kalidasa's best-known lyric, in the slow mandakranta metre.

works.title: মেঘনাদবধ কাব্য (Meghnadbadh Kavya)
works.subtitle: Michael Madhusudan Dutt's Bengali epic in blank verse, in nine sargas, in the original Bengali
works.author: Michael Madhusudan Dutt
works.blurb: Madhusudan's blank-verse epic of the death of Meghnad (Indrajit), son of Ravana, in the war of Lanka, told from the Rakshasa side in nine sargas; the first great epic of modern Bengali literature.

works.title: The Arbitrants
works.subtitle: Epitrepontes; or, Those Who Submit their Case to Arbitration
works.author: Menander
works.blurb: Charisius has left his young wife Pamphila after a child she exposed was born too soon, not knowing that he himself is the father; a charcoal-burner, a slave and a harp-girl bring the exposed child and its ring to light. The play survives in part, from the Cairo papyrus.

works.title: Fragments
works.subtitle: Selections from the unidentified minor fragments
works.author: Menander
works.blurb: Sayings, speeches and one-liners quoted from lost comedies, with the translator's captions, as selected in Allinson's Loeb volume.

sections.title: Fragments Assigned with Doubt to Menander

works.title: The Girl from Samos
works.subtitle: Samia
works.author: Menander
works.blurb: On the day of a wedding, Demeas takes the baby nursed by Chrysis, the Samian girl he keeps, to be his adopted son Moschion's, and in a fit of rage drives her from the house; the neighbour Niceratus is soon drawn in. The play survives in part, from the Cairo papyrus.

works.title: The Shorter Play-Fragments
works.subtitle: The Hero and the fragments of sixty-seven other comedies
works.author: Menander
works.blurb: What survives of Menander's other comedies in Allinson's Loeb volume: a scene of The Hero, the longer passages of The Farmer, The Flatterer, The Hated Man and The Ghost, and the sayings and fragments quoted from dozens of lost plays.

sections.title: The Shearing of Glycera: Other Fragments
The Woman Possessed with a Divinity
The Women who Would Drink Hemlock

works.title: The Shearing of Glycera
works.subtitle: Perikeiromene; or, The Girl Who Gets Her Hair Cut Short
works.author: Menander
works.blurb: The soldier Polemon, jealous after seeing Moschion kiss Glycera, cuts off her hair; she takes refuge in the house next door, where birth-tokens reveal that she and Moschion are brother and sister and that Pataecus is their father. The play survives in part, from the Cairo papyrus.

works.title: The Merchant of Venice
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: To fund his friend Bassanio's courtship of the heiress Portia, the merchant Antonio borrows three thousand ducats from the moneylender Shylock, pledging a pound of his own flesh against default. When Antonio's ships are lost, Shylock demands his bond in open court, and Portia, disguised as a young lawyer, turns the letter of the law against him. Beside the trial run the riddle of the three caskets, the elopement of Shylock's daughter Jessica, and the comedy of the rings.

works.title: Merlin
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
works.blurb: Blank-verse Arthurian narrative in seven parts: the ruin of Camelot and the old enchanter Merlin, held by Vivian in the forest of Broceliande.

works.title: The Mesnevi, Book the First
works.subtitle: Translated and versified by James W. Redhouse
works.author: Jalal al-Din Rumi
works.blurb: The first book of Rumi's great Persian Sufi teaching poem, opening with the lament of the reed-flute torn from its reed-bed, and moving through tales of the prince and the handmaid, the parrot and the oilman, and the lion and the beasts, each tale unfolding a lesson of love and the soul's return to God.

works.title: Metamorphoses
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid’s vast narrative poem in fifteen books, retelling the myths of transformation from the creation of the world to the deification of Julius Caesar.

works.title: Metamorphoses (Golding)
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid’s vast narrative poem in fifteen books, retold in Arthur Golding’s rollicking English fourteeners of 1567. This is the translation Shakespeare knew.

works.title: Metamorphoses (Howard)
works.subtitle: in English blank verse
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid's fifteen books of transformations in the English blank verse of J. J. Howard, a Georgian version printed privately in 1807, with its period elisions intact and the poet's bolder passages deliberately chastened for general readers.

works.title: Metamorphoses (Latin)
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid’s Metamorphoses in the original Latin hexameters: fifteen books of transformation myths, from the creation of the world to the apotheosis of Caesar.

works.title: Metamorphoses (More)
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid’s vast narrative poem in fifteen books, in Brookes More’s American blank verse of 1922, with the translator’s own headings for each tale.

works.title: The Meters of Boethius
works.subtitle: trans. W. J. Sedgefield (1900)
works.author: King Alfred
works.translator: trans. Walter John Sedgefield, King Alfred's Version of the Consolations of Boethius (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1900)

works.title: Metrical Legends of Exalted Characters
works.author: Joanna Baillie
works.blurb: Joanna Baillie's three verse legends of William Wallace, Christopher Columbus and Lady Griseld Baillie, with four shorter ballads of the supernatural.

Lord John of the East: A Ballad
Malcom's Heir: A Tale of Wonder
The Elden Tree: An Ancient Ballad

works.title: M'Fingal
works.subtitle: A Modern Epic Poem, in Four Cantos
works.author: John Trumbull
works.blurb: Hudibrastic satire on a Tory squire in revolutionary Massachusetts.

works.title: Michael Angelo
works.subtitle: A Fragment
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A dramatic poem on the last decades of Michelangelo in Rome, published after Longfellow's death. In scenes of dialogue and monologue it sets the aged sculptor and painter beside Vittoria Colonna and Julia Gonzaga, Benvenuto Cellini, Titian, Vasari and the Popes, and follows him from the Last Judgment to the labour on St. Peter's and the Dead Christ.

works.title: The Mighty Magician
works.subtitle: Taken from Calderón's El Mágico Prodigioso
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: In Antioch the scholar and magician Cipriano sells his soul to the Devil to win the Christian Justina, who resists every spell. Cipriano is converted, and he and Justina are martyred together while Lucifer is left to confess his defeat. This is a different play and a different translation from Shelley's scenes of the same drama.

works.title: The Mikado
works.subtitle: Or, The Town of Titipu
works.author: W. S. Gilbert
works.blurb: In the town of Titipu, Nanki-Poo, the Mikado's son, flees an arranged match with the elderly Katisha and falls in love with Yum-Yum, the ward of Ko-Ko, a cheap tailor raised to Lord High Executioner. When the Mikado orders an execution in Titipu within the month, Ko-Ko must find someone to behead, and the stratagems that follow tangle the whole town.

works.title: Milagros de Nuestra Señora
works.subtitle: Miracles of Our Lady
works.author: Gonzalo de Berceo
works.year: 13th c. (ed. Tomás Antonio Sánchez, Madrid: Antonio de Sancha, 1780)
works.blurb: Twenty-five miracles of the Virgin Mary in Old Spanish cuaderna via, preceded by an allegorical prologue, from Tomás Antonio Sánchez's 1780 edition.

works.title: Milton
works.subtitle: A Poem in 2 Books
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's prophetic epic in which the dead poet Milton returns from eternity to correct his errors, set between the Preface hymn "And did those feet in ancient time" and the vision of the Great Harvest.

works.title: Milton
works.subtitle: In Four Parts
works.author: Edward Bulwer Lytton
works.blurb: A poem in four parts picturing Milton in youth, manhood and age, linked by a thread of romantic fiction drawn from his Italian journey.

works.title: The Minstrel
works.subtitle: or, The Progress of Genius
works.author: James Beattie
works.blurb: A Spenserian poem in two books tracing the growth of a young poet, Edwin, among the hills and shepherds of the Scottish countryside.

works.title: Mirèio
works.subtitle: A Provençal Poem
works.author: Frédéric Mistral
works.blurb: Mistral's Provençal pastoral epic of the farmer's daughter Mirèio and the basket-weaver Vincen, whose love is thwarted by her family and ends at the shrine of the Saints Maries.

works.title: Miss Kilmansegg and Her Precious Leg
works.subtitle: A Golden Legend
works.author: Thomas Hood
works.blurb: Hood's comic narrative of an heiress whose golden leg, bought after a riding accident, makes her fortune and her ruin: a satire on money, marriage and the worship of gold, told in eighteen sections.

works.title: The Moallakát
works.subtitle: The Seven Arabian Poems which were suspended on the Temple at Mecca
works.author: The Mu'allaqat Poets
works.blurb: Seven great odes of pre-Islamic Arabia, said to have been hung on the Kaaba at Mecca, by Imru' al-Qais, Tarafa, Zuhayr, Labid, Antara, Amr ibn Kulthum and al-Harith ibn Hilliza.

sections.title: The Poem of Amru (Amr ibn Kulthum)
The Poem of Hareth (al-Harith ibn Hilliza)

works.title: The Modern Traveller
works.author: Hilaire Belloc
works.blurb: A mock-heroic monologue in which the boastful explorer Mr. Rooter, interviewed by a journalist, tells of his African expeditions and of his dead companions Commander Sin and Captain Blood.

works.title: Мойсей (Moses)
works.author: Ivan Franko
works.blurb: Franko's great poem on the prophet Moses at the end of the forty years in the wilderness, written in terza rima as a prologue addressed to the Ukrainian people and twenty cantos on leadership, sacrifice and the road to a promised land that the leader himself will not enter.

works.author: Atukuri Molla
works.blurb: A woman poet's Telugu Ramayana: the prologue and the first book, from the glory of Ayodhya to the meeting with Parashurama.

works.title: Monachomachia
works.subtitle: czyli wojna mnichów
works.author: Ignacy Krasicki
works.blurb: Krasicki's mock-heroic satire of 1778 in six cantos of ottava rima, in the original Polish: two rival monasteries, Carmelite and Dominican, go to war over a learned disputation, and the lazy, greedy and ignorant monks are laughed at in the manner of the epic.

works.title: Morgante
works.subtitle: Poema in ventotto cantari, in ottava rima
works.author: Luigi Pulci
works.blurb: Pulci's comic epic of Charlemagne's paladins, in which Orlando converts the giant Morgante and the two set out together, ending with the treachery of Gano and the defeat at Roncesvalles, in the original Italian ottava rima. Lord Byron's English version of the first canto is held separately among his poems (The Morgante Maggiore of Pulci).

works.blurb: Moses ibn Ezra's Hebrew verse from Muslim Spain: penitential hymns and prayers for the Days of Awe, Hanukkah and the fast-days, and the twenty-two chapters of the Sefer ha-Anaq, a book of moral quatrains.

works.title: Moses: A Play
works.author: Isaac Rosenberg
works.blurb: Moses, an Egyptian prince, receives Pharaoh’s edict that the slaves are to have their teeth drawn, and meditates on the power rising in him. Among the Hebrews labouring at the pyramids, Koelue, the overseer Abinoah’s daughter, sings for him, while the Hebrews curse him. The play closes with Moses killing an Egyptian as Prince Imra’s soldiers come to arrest him.

works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: Lermontov's narrative poem of the Georgian boy raised in a monastery who escapes into the mountains for three days of freedom and tells the old monk what he saw, in its original Russian.

works.title: Much Ado About Nothing
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: In Messina, Claudio, fresh from the wars, woos Hero with the help of his prince, Don Pedro, while Hero's cousin Beatrice and the soldier Benedick trade barbed wit and swear they will never love. Friends contrive to make each believe the other is secretly in love, even as Don John, the prince's embittered bastard brother, plots to shame Hero on her wedding day. The slander is exposed by the bumbling constable Dogberry and his watch, Hero is restored, and the sparring pair are brought to marriage.

works.blurb: The classical anthology of old Arabian odes compiled by al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi in the eighth century, here in the Arabic of Wikisource.

works.subtitle: 262 prayers in rhymed prose and quatrains
works.author: Khwaja 'Abdullah Ansari of Herat
works.type: Munajat (prayers in rhymed prose and verse)
works.blurb: The Munajat-nama of Khwaja 'Abdullah Ansari, the Pir of Herat: 262 intimate prayers addressed to God in rhymed prose, studded with Persian quatrains. A landmark of Sufi devotional writing.

works.title: Hero and Leander
works.subtitle: The Divine Poem of Musaeus, First of All Books, translated according to the original
works.author: Musaeus
works.blurb: Chapman's rhymed-couplet version of the Greek epyllion of c. AD 500, the story of the priestess Hero and Leander, who swims the Hellespont each night to her torch.

works.title: Musophilus
works.subtitle: Containing a generall defence of all learning
works.author: Samuel Daniel
works.blurb: Samuel Daniel's long verse dialogue in defence of poetry and learning. Philocosmus, the lover of the world, scorns the poet's idle art; Musophilus, the lover of the Muses, answers him at length on fame, the worth of the English language, the dangers of ignorance and the place of learning in a commonwealth. It is dedicated, in a sonnet, to Fulke Greville.

works.title: नैषधीयचरितम् (Naishadhiyacharitam), canto 1
works.subtitle: The Story of Nala, in the original Sanskrit
works.author: Sriharsha
works.blurb: The opening canto of Sriharsha's court epic of King Nala and Damayanti: Nala's glory, learning and conquests, and the swan that is to carry word of him to Damayanti.

works.title: Nala and Damayanti
works.subtitle: An episode of the Mahabharata (Vana Parva)
works.author: Vyasa
works.blurb: The story of King Nala of Nishadha and Damayanti, princess of Vidarbha: the swan messenger, the choice among the gods, the possession of Nala by the demon Kali, the dice, the desertion in the forest and the long wanderings, until husband and wife are reunited and his kingdom restored.

works.title: Of the Nature of Things
works.author: Lucretius
works.blurb: Lucretius's Latin didactic poem De rerum natura, an exposition of Epicurean atomism in six books, rendered into English blank verse by William Ellery Leonard.

works.title: Nepenthe
works.subtitle: A Poem in Two Cantos
works.author: George Darley
works.blurb: Darley's visionary fragment of two cantos: the first of over-joy, the second of excessive melancholy, a poet's flight across desert, river and mountain in search of the nepenthe that would cure both.

works.title: Lives of Eminent Commanders
works.subtitle: John Selby Watson translation, 1853
works.author: Cornelius Nepos
works.blurb: Cornelius Nepos's short biographies of twenty-two Greek and Carthaginian commanders, from Miltiades at Marathon to Hannibal, with a chapter on kings and lives of Cato the Elder and of his friend Atticus, in John Selby Watson's English prose of 1853.

works.title: Nero, Part I
works.subtitle: An Historical Tragedy
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's historical tragedy of the first part of Nero's reign, published in 1885: the young emperor, his mother Agrippina, his tutor Seneca and the prefect Burrus, the poisoning of Britannicus at table, and Agrippina's end at Baiae. Written in blank verse and, as Bridges says in his notes, not intended for the stage.

works.title: Nero, Part II
works.subtitle: From the death of Burrus to the death of Seneca, comprising the conspiracy of Piso
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: The second part of Bridges's history of Nero, published in 1894, carries the story from the death of Burrus to the death of Seneca, taking in the conspiracy of Piso against the emperor and its fatal consequences for Seneca, Lucan and the Stoic circle of Thrasea.

works.title: The New England Tragedies
works.subtitle: Christus: A Mystery, Part III
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: The third part of Longfellow's trilogy Christus: A Mystery, two verse plays on the religious intolerance of colonial New England. John Endicott shows the Puritan governor of Boston persecuting Quakers in 1665, whipping and hanging those who will not conform, while his own son sides with them. Giles Corey of the Salem Farms dramatises the witchcraft delusion of 1692, in which an old farmer, pressed to death for refusing to plead, becomes its martyr. The part closes with the Finale, Saint John wandering the earth, and the Interludes between the parts of the trilogy are printed after the plays.

works.subtitle: A Romance of London

works.blurb: Bulwer Lytton’s satire in heroic couplets on London society, politics and literature, framed by the story of a rescued orphan girl and her benefactor.

works.title: A New Version of the Psalms of David
works.subtitle: Fitted to the Tunes Used in Churches (Tate and Brady)
works.author: Nahum Tate and Nicholas Brady

works.title: Ninfale fiesolano
works.subtitle: Ossia l’innamoramento di Affrico e Mensola
works.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
works.blurb: Boccaccio's pastoral tale in seven parts of ottava rima: the shepherd Affrico loves the nymph Mensola, a follower of Diana, and the story explains the founding of Fiesole and the rivers named for the lovers.

works.title: A Modern Faust
works.subtitle: Verse sections only
works.author: Roden Noel
works.blurb: Noel's long visionary poem of a modern Faust, a pilgrim who goes from faith through doubt and disorder to a vision of order.

works.title: Beatrice
works.subtitle: From Beatrice and Other Poems
works.author: Roden Noel
works.blurb: Roden Noel's long narrative poem in four books, following the dreamer Clement and Beatrice, whose love ends in loss, with lyric songs woven through it.

works.title: Livingstone in Africa
works.author: Roden Noel
works.blurb: A blank-verse narrative in seven cantos of David Livingstone's last years in Africa, his death, and the carrying of his body home, with the lyric 'Mosi-oa-Tunya' set within it.

works.title: Melcha
works.subtitle: From Songs of the Heights and Deeps
works.author: Roden Noel
works.blurb: A narrative poem in three parts about the pensive maiden Melcha, wooed by the fairy knight O'Donoghue and carried under the waters of an Irish lake as his bride.

works.title: Dionysiaca
works.subtitle: Διονυσιακά
works.author: Nonnus of Panopolis
works.blurb: The Greek text of the Dionysiaca, Nonnus of Panopolis's forty-eight-book hexameter epic of Dionysus, the longest surviving poem of antiquity: from the abduction of Europa and the battle of Zeus with Typhoeus, through the wanderings of Cadmus, the births of the god and his Indian campaign, to his triumph and ascent to Olympus. Books 1–16 are given here so far.

works.title: Nordlands Trompet
works.subtitle: eller Beskrivelse over Nordlands Amt
works.author: Petter Dass
works.blurb: Petter Dass's rhymed description of Nordland in northern Norway, its weather, fish, birds, people and parishes, written in the 1690s.

sections.title: Allehaande Fugler og flyvende Dyr i Nordlandene
Svemmende Dyr i det Nordlandske Hav

works.title: O Uraguai
works.author: Basílio da Gama
works.blurb: Basílio da Gama's blank-verse epic in five cantos on the Luso-Spanish campaign against the Jesuit-led Guaraní missions of the Uruguay river (1756).

works.title: Oberon
works.subtitle: A Poem, from the German of Wieland
works.author: Christoph Martin Wieland
works.blurb: Wieland's romance of the knight Huon of Bordeaux, sent by Charlemagne to Babylon and helped by the fairy king Oberon, who has sworn to reconcile with his queen Titania only when a faithful pair keep their vows through every trial; Sotheby's English verse version of the German epic.

works.title: Облако в штанах (A Cloud in Trousers)
works.subtitle: Тетраптих
works.author: Vladimir Mayakovsky
works.blurb: Mayakovsky's first long poem, a 'tetraptych' of love, art, politics and religion in four parts after a prologue, in the original Russian: the lover jilted by Maria, the poet's cry against the age.

works.title: Octavia
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: The emperor Nero's neglected wife Octavia is put aside for Poppaea and finally banished and put to death.

works.title: Octavia
works.subtitle: Attributed to Seneca
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Rome, AD 62. Nero has resolved to divorce his stepsister and wife Octavia, the daughter of the murdered emperor Claudius, and to marry his mistress Poppaea. Agrippina’s ghost curses the wedding, Seneca pleads in vain for restraint, and the people rise in Octavia’s defence. Nero crushes the rising and has Octavia put aboard a ship bound for exile and death on the island of Pandataria. The only surviving Roman historical drama, it was transmitted among Seneca’s tragedies but is generally held not to be his.

works.title: The Odyssey
works.author: Homer
works.translator: trans. S. H. Butcher and A. Lang (1879)
works.blurb: Butcher and Lang's prose translation of Odysseus's ten-year voyage home from Troy, in a deliberately archaic, King James-like English.

works.title: The Odyssey
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Samuel Butler’s prose translation of Odysseus’s ten-year voyage home from Troy, companion to his Iliad.

works.title: The Odyssey
works.subtitle: The Odysseys of Homer, translated by George Chapman
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: George Chapman’s Odyssey, completed in 1614–15 as the companion to his Iliad, rendering the ten-year homecoming of Ulysses in rhymed decasyllabic couplets.

works.title: The Odyssey
works.subtitle: A line-for-line translation in the metre of the original
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: H. B. Cotterill's 1911 English hexameter version of the Odyssey, which keeps to the long line of Homer's own metre and renders the poem line for line.

works.title: The Odyssey
works.subtitle: Translated by William Cowper
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: William Cowper's blank-verse translation of Homer's Odyssey, published in 1791.

works.title: Ὀδύσσεια (Odyssey, Greek text)
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: The Odyssey in the original Homeric Greek, in twenty-four books of dactylic hexameter, with the polytonic accents and breathings as printed in A. T. Murray's Loeb edition (1919).

works.title: The Odyssey
works.subtitle: Done into English verse by William Morris
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: William Morris's rhymed, archaising translation of Homer's Odyssey, published in 1887 in two volumes.

works.title: The Odyssey
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: A. T. Murray’s literal prose translation of Odysseus’s ten-year voyage home from Troy, from the Loeb Classical Library of 1919.

works.title: The Odyssey
works.subtitle: Translated by Alexander Pope, with William Broome and Elijah Fenton
works.author: Homer
works.translator: trans. Alexander Pope, with William Broome and Elijah Fenton (1725–1726)
works.blurb: Alexander Pope's heroic-couplet version of Odysseus's long voyage home from Troy, completed with the help of William Broome and Elijah Fenton.

works.title: The Odyssey (Way)
works.author: Homer
works.blurb: Arthur S. Way’s rhymed verse translation of the Odyssey, in long swinging anapaestic couplets; this is the third, revised edition of 1904, first published in 1880 under the pseudonym “Avia”. Books I–XXIV.

works.title: Oedipus at Colonus
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Blind and exiled, Oedipus comes to the grove of the Eumenides at Colonos near Athens, guided by his daughter Antigone. Theseus gives him shelter and defends him against Creon and the pleas of his son Polynices, and Oedipus passes mysteriously from the sight of men, a blessing to Athens.

works.title: Οἰδίπους ἐπὶ Κολωνῷ (Oidipous epi Kolono)
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: The blind, exiled Oidipous comes to the grove of the Eumenides at Kolonos near Athens, where Theseus shelters him and he is to die. Creon and Polyneikes try to claim him, and he passes mysteriously from the world. The Greek text is given in the order of the Storr edition, so that it pairs with the English prose translation of the same play.

works.title: Oedipus at Colonus
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Old, blind and driven from Thebes, Oedipus reaches a grove of the Eumenides near Athens and learns that here his wanderings are to end. Theseus protects him, Creon tries to carry off his daughters, and Polyneices pleads in vain for a father’s blessing, until a summons of thunder calls Oedipus away to a hidden and holy death.

works.title: Oedipus
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Thebes is ravaged by plague, and Oedipus, searching for the murderer of Laius, discovers that he himself is the guilty man.

works.title: Oedipus
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: A plague is killing Thebes, and King Oedipus, who once saved the city by solving the Sphinx's riddle, sends Creon to Delphi to learn the cause. The god's answer is that the murderer of the old king Laius must be found and driven out. After a grim sacrifice and a summoning of Laius's ghost, the evidence closes in on Oedipus himself, and an old herdsman from Corinth completes the proof: Oedipus is the son of Laius and Jocasta. Jocasta kills herself, and Oedipus blinds himself and goes into exile.

works.title: Oedipus the King
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: A plague lies on Thebes, and Apollo declares that it will lift only when the murderer of King Laius is found. Oedipus vows to find him, and the search leads step by step to the truth about his own birth and to the fulfilment of the oracle: Jocasta hangs herself, and Oedipus blinds himself.

works.title: Οἰδίπους Τύραννος (Oidipous Tyrannos)
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: A plague lies on Thebes, and Oidipous sets out to find the killer of Laios. Step by step he discovers that he himself is the murderer and that Iokaste is his mother. The Greek text is given in the order of the Storr edition, so that it pairs with the English prose translation of the same play.

works.title: Oedipus the King
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: A plague lies on Thebes, and the oracle at Delphi says it will end only when the killer of the old king, Laius, is driven out. Oedipus, who rules the city, swears to find him. His questioning of the prophet Teiresias, of Creon and of Iocasta, and the testimony of two shepherds, bring him step by step to the truth about his own birth, his marriage and the man he killed at the crossroads. Jebb renders the play in prose that keeps the speeches whole.

works.title: おくのほそ道 (Oku no hosomichi)
works.subtitle: The Narrow Road to the Deep North
works.author: Matsuo Bashō
works.blurb: Bashō's travel journal of 1689, written after his journey with Sora through the north of Japan, with its hokku set inside the prose.

sections.title: 画工加右衛門 (The Painter Kaemon)
松島塩がまの画 (Pictures of Matsushima)

works.title: The Old Bush Songs
works.subtitle: Comprising Bush Ballads, Songs of the Bullock Dray and the Overland Routes, Digger’s Ditties, and other Songs of Australian Life
works.author: A. B. Paterson (ed.)
works.blurb: Paterson’s collection of anonymous and half-forgotten songs of the Australian bush: shearers, stockmen, swagmen, diggers, immigrants and bushrangers.

sections.title: A National Song for Australia Felix
It’s Only a Way He’s Got
The Squatter of the Olden Time

works.title: Apu Ollantay: A Drama of the Time of the Incas
works.author: Anonymous (Quechua)
works.blurb: The general Ollantay, a commoner, loves Cusi Coyllur, daughter of the Inca Pachacuti, and secretly fathers her child. When Pachacuti discovers it he imprisons the princess and Ollantay rises in revolt in the fortress of Ollantaytambo. Years later, under Pachacuti's son Tupac Yupanqui, the rebels are tricked, the princess is found, and the lovers are reconciled.

works.title: On Baile’s Strand
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: In a great hall by the sea, a blind man and a fool wait while the High King Concobar binds the hero Cuchullain to an oath of obedience. A young stranger arrives who proves to be Cuchullain’s own unknown son, and the oath drives the father to a tragic deed on the shore. Yeats’s one-act play, taken from the Irish heroic cycle, was first staged in 1904.

works.title: The Only Jealousy of Emer
works.subtitle: A play for dancers
works.author: W. B. Yeats
works.blurb: Cuchulain lies apparently dead on a fisher's litter, his ghost crouching beside him, while his wife Emer and his mistress Eithne Inguba keep watch. A Woman of the Sidhe offers to release him if Emer will give up the thing she most values, the hope of his love. Emer, whose only jealousy is for his love, must choose.

works.title: Ordinalia
works.subtitle: The Cornish mystery cycle: Origo Mundi, Passio Domini Nostri Jhesu Christi, Resurrexio Domini Nostri Jhesu Christi
works.author: Anonymous (Cornish)
works.blurb: The three Middle Cornish mystery plays of the late fourteenth century, the longest body of medieval Cornish: the Creation to Solomon, the Passion of Christ, and the Resurrection, in about 8,700 lines of rhymed stanzas.

works.title: Ordinalia
works.subtitle: Edwin Norris's facing English translation
works.author: Anonymous (Cornish)
works.blurb: Edwin Norris's literal English version of the Cornish Ordinalia (1859), made line for line beside the Middle Cornish text: the Creation to Solomon, the Passion of Christ, and the Resurrection.

works.title: Ὀρέστης (Orestes)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Orestes lies sick and half-mad in Argos six days after killing his mother, tended by his sister Elektra, while the city assembly meets to decide whether he and Elektra must die for the matricide. His uncle Menelaos, newly home from Troy with Helen, offers no real help, and the vote goes against the pair. Orestes and Pylades then plot revenge on Helen, and seize her daughter Hermione to bargain for their lives, while a Phrygian slave describes the attack on Helen in a wild lyric aria. At the moment of crisis Apollo appears above the palace to end the play, Helen is made a goddess, and he arranges the marriages and the trial of Orestes at Athens. The Greek text is given in the order of Nauck's Teubner edition, so that it pairs with the English translation of the same play.

works.title: Orestes
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Six days after the murder of their mother, Orestes lies delirious in Argos while the city votes whether he and his sister Electra must die. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tense late tragedy of madness, desperate plotting and an unexpected divine rescue in English verse.

works.title: Fabula di Orfeo
works.subtitle: La favola d'Orfeo
works.author: Angelo Poliziano
works.blurb: The first secular drama in Italian, composed in a few days for the Gonzaga court of Mantua. The shepherd Aristeo pursues Euridice, who dies of a snakebite; Orfeo charms Pluto and Proserpina into releasing her, loses her again by looking back, swears off women, and is torn apart by the Bacchantes, who close the play with a drunken hymn to Bacchus.

works.title: Orion: An Epic Poem
works.subtitle: In Three Books
works.author: Richard Henry Horne
works.blurb: Horne's allegorical epic of the giant hunter Orion, from his blinding by Oenopion and his cure by the rising sun to his translation among the stars, published at a farthing in 1843.

works.title: Orlando Furioso in English Heroical Verse
works.subtitle: Translated by Sir John Harington from the Italian of Ludovico Ariosto, in forty-six cantos
works.author: Ludovico Ariosto
works.blurb: Ariosto's romance epic of Charlemagne's paladins, Orlando's love-madness, and the love of Ruggiero and Bradamante, in Sir John Harington's Elizabethan ottava rima, the first complete English version.

works.title: Orlando furioso
works.subtitle: Poema in quarantasei canti, in ottava rima
works.author: Ludovico Ariosto
works.blurb: Ariosto's romance epic of Charlemagne's paladins, Orlando's love-madness, and the love of Ruggiero and Bradamante, in the original Italian ottava rima.

works.title: Orlando Furioso
works.subtitle: Translated into English verse from the Italian of Ludovico Ariosto, in forty-six cantos
works.author: Ludovico Ariosto
works.blurb: Ariosto's romance epic of Charlemagne's paladins, Orlando's love-madness, and the love of Ruggiero and Bradamante, in William Stewart Rose's eight-line stanzas.

works.title: Orlando innamorato
works.subtitle: Poema in tre libri, in ottava rima
works.author: Matteo Maria Boiardo
works.blurb: Boiardo's romance epic of Orlando in love with Angelica, the siege of Paris, and the love of Ruggiero and Bradamante, in the original Italian ottava rima. Three books, 69 cantos; the third book breaks off unfinished in its ninth canto.

works.title: Os Lusíadas
works.author: Luís de Camões
works.blurb: Camões's national epic of Vasco da Gama's voyage to India and the story of Portugal, in ten cantos of ottava rima.

works.title: Os Timbiras
works.subtitle: Poema americano
works.author: Gonçalves Dias
works.blurb: Gonçalves Dias's unfinished Indianist epic of the Timbira people of Maranhão, in blank hendecasyllables: an invocation of the dead warriors and their piagas, then four cantos of councils, rites and war.

works.title: Osman
works.subtitle: Epic poem in twenty cantos (composed c. 1621–1638)
works.author: Ivan Gundulić
works.blurb: Gundulić's unfinished Baroque epic of the Ragusan poet, in octosyllabic quatrains, on the Ottoman defeat at Khotyn and the death of the young Sultan Osman II; the lost cantos XIV and XV are supplied by Ivan Mažuranić.

works.title: Osorio
works.subtitle: A Tragedy
works.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
works.blurb: Coleridge's first tragedy, written at Nether Stowey in 1797 for Sheridan and Drury Lane, where it was rejected that December; it was not printed until 1873. Set in Spain under Philip II, during the persecution of the Moors, it follows Albert, long believed dead, who comes back disguised as a sorcerer to face his treacherous younger brother Osorio. It is the earlier form of the play that Coleridge reworked in 1813 as Remorse.

works.title: The Tragedy of Othello, the Moor of Venice
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Othello, the Moor who commands Venice's forces, secretly marries Desdemona, the daughter of the senator Brabantio, and is sent to defend Cyprus against the Turks. His ensign Iago, passed over for promotion, poisons his mind with the lie that Desdemona is unfaithful to him with the lieutenant Cassio. Driven to jealous rage by a lost handkerchief and Iago's insinuations, Othello smothers Desdemona in her bed, and learns the truth too late to do anything but take his own life.

works.title: Otho the Great
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Five Acts
works.author: John Keats and Charles Armitage Brown
works.blurb: Otho the Great, Emperor of Germany, has put down a rebellion led by his own son Ludolph and by Conrad, Duke of Franconia, who has changed sides in time to share the victory. Ludolph has meanwhile fought for his father in disguise as a mysterious Arab warrior, and is reconciled to him, only to be married at once to Conrad's sister Auranthe. Auranthe and Conrad have slandered Otho's niece Erminia to clear their own way; the Abbot Ethelbert, the Hungarian prince Gersa and the knight Albert bring the plot to light, and the play ends in the frenzy and death of Ludolph. Keats wrote the verse in 1819 to a plan drawn up by Brown.

works.title: Otuel
works.subtitle: The Auchinleck romance of the Saracen Otuel
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A Middle English couplet romance of Charlemagne. The Saracen champion Otuel comes to Charles's court as King Garsie's envoy, fights Roland to a standstill, is converted when a white dove lights on his head, marries the emperor's daughter Belisent and helps the Christians destroy Garsie's host.

works.title: The Owl and the Nightingale
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: On a summer evening an Owl and a Nightingale fall to quarrelling in a hidden dell, each pouring scorn on the other's song, habits and usefulness, until they agree to put their case to Master Nicholas of Guildford and fly off to find him.

works.title: पदमावत (Padmavat)
works.author: Malik Muhammad Jayasi
works.blurb: A Sufi love-romance in Awadhi, in which the king of Chittor wins the Sinhala princess Padmavati and loses her to the siege of the sultan of Delhi.

works.title: The Painter of His Own Dishonour
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: A nobleman-painter, Don Juan Roca, brings his bride Serafina to Naples, where the Prince of Orsino is smitten with her. Her former suitor Alvaro, long believed drowned, returns to carry her off, and Juan, in the name of his honour, kills them both. FitzGerald's free version of Calderón's El pintor de su deshonra.

works.title: Palestine
works.subtitle: A Prize Poem
works.author: Reginald Heber
works.blurb: A prize poem on the fall of Jerusalem and the promised restoration of the Holy Land, recited at Oxford in 1803.

works.title: The Palice of Honour
works.subtitle: Compylit be M. Gawine Dowglas, Bischop of Dunkeld
works.author: Gavin Douglas
works.blurb: Douglas's dream-vision of 1501, dedicated to James IV: a poet, condemned by Venus's court for slandering love, is pardoned at the intercession of Calliope and led by the Muses to the Palace of Honour, where Venus, the poets and the exemplary dead of history pass before him.

sections.title: The Author directis his Buik to the Richt Nobill and Illuster Prince Iames the Feird, King of Scottis

works.title: Palicio
works.subtitle: A Romantic Drama in Five Acts in the Elizabethan manner
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Bridges's romantic drama in five acts, in the Elizabethan manner, first published in 1890. The scene is Palermo and the hills above Monreale under the Spanish occupation of Sicily, where the brigand Giovanni Palicio, the viceroy Hugo and his court, and the lovers Margaret and Livio are drawn into a web of intrigue.

works.title: ವಿಕ್ರಮಾರ್ಜುನ ವಿಜಯ (Pampa Bharata), Ashvasas 12-13
works.subtitle: Vikramarjuna Vijaya, the Pampa Bharata: the twelfth and thirteenth ashvasas, in Old Kannada
works.author: Pampa (Adikavi Pampa)
works.blurb: Pampa's tenth-century champu retelling of the Mahabharata with Arjuna as its hero: the twelfth ashvasa, which opens with the night battle and the death of Ghatotkacha, and the thirteenth, in the war's later days, in the original Old Kannada.

works.title: Master Thaddeus; or, The Last Foray in Lithuania
works.subtitle: A Polish Tale of the Years 1811 and 1812
works.author: Adam Mickiewicz
works.blurb: Mickiewicz's national epic of Lithuania in twelve books, a story of feuding noble families, a lost love and the coming of Napoleon's army in 1811-12, here in the first English translation, in blank verse, by Maude Ashurst Biggs.

sections.title: Book IV: Diplomacy and the Chase
Book XII: Let Us Love One Another

works.title: Pan Tadeusz; or, The Last Foray in Lithuania
works.author: Adam Mickiewicz
works.blurb: Mickiewicz's national epic of the last foray in Lithuania, set in 1811–12 on the eve of Napoleon's invasion of Russia: a quarrel between two noble families, a young man's return to the family estate, and a love story, in twelve books full of hunts, feasts, mushroom-gathering and nostalgia for a vanished Poland.

sections.title: Book IV: Diplomacy and the Chase
Book XII: Let Us Love One Another!

works.title: Pan Tadeusz, czyli ostatni zajazd na Litwie
works.subtitle: Historia szlachecka z roku 1811 i 1812 we dwunastu księgach wierszem
works.author: Adam Mickiewicz
works.blurb: Mickiewicz's national epic in twelve books and an epilogue, written in Paris after the failed uprising of 1830-31: a tale of two feuding noble families, a lost love and the coming of Napoleon's army to Lithuania in 1811-12, in thirteen-syllable rhymed couplets. Here in the original Polish.

works.title: Paolo and Francesca
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Four Acts
works.author: Stephen Phillips
works.blurb: Giovanni Malatesta, the lame tyrant of Rimini, takes the young Francesca, daughter of the lord of Ravenna, as his bride and sends his handsome brother Paolo to fetch her. Paolo and Francesca fall silently in love; he tries to flee to the wars and even buys poison rather than betray his brother. Giovanni, warned by his old blind nurse Angela and goaded by his cousin Lucrezia, learns the truth. Paolo returns, and they confess their love while reading of Launcelot and Guenevere. Giovanni finds them together and kills them both.

works.title: Paracelsus
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Browning's first acknowledged work follows the sixteenth-century physician and alchemist Paracelsus through five parts, from the aspiration that drives him from Würzburg to the long reckoning of his death in Salzburg, in a drama of the mind rather than of events.

works.title: Paradise Lost
works.subtitle: A Poem in Twelve Books
works.author: John Milton
works.blurb: Milton’s epic of the war in Heaven and the fall of man — twelve books of blank verse, from Satan’s rebellion to the expulsion from Eden.

works.title: Paradise Regain'd
works.subtitle: A Poem in Four Books
works.author: John Milton
works.blurb: The brief epic sequel: Christ in the wilderness, tempted by Satan and refusing every worldly power.

works.title: The Paradiso (Wicksteed)
works.subtitle: Prose translation by Philip H. Wicksteed (Temple Classics)
works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.blurb: Dante's ascent through the spheres of Heaven in Philip H. Wicksteed's plain, literal prose for the Temple Classics, printed in 1899 as the facing English of the Italian text.

works.title: Il Giorno
works.subtitle: Il Mattino, Il Mezzogiorno, Il Vespro, La Notte
works.author: Giuseppe Parini
works.blurb: Parini's satirical blank-verse poem that follows a young nobleman through his day, from morning toilette to night-time gaming, in mock instruction.

works.title: The Paris Psalter (Old English)
works.subtitle: The metrical Psalms 51–150: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: An Old English verse rendering of Psalms 51–150, preserved in a tenth-century Paris manuscript that gives the first fifty psalms in prose.

works.title: The Parliament of Fowls
works.subtitle: The Assembly of Fowls
works.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
works.blurb: A Valentine's Day dream vision in which birds of every rank gather before Nature to choose their mates — often read as an allegory of courtship and royal marriage.

works.title: Parzival: A Knightly Epic
works.subtitle: Translated from the Middle High German of Wolfram von Eschenbach
works.author: Wolfram von Eschenbach
works.blurb: Weston's 1894 verse rendering, the first complete English Parzival, in long rhyming couplets.

works.title: The Passage of the Red Sea
works.author: Reginald Heber
works.blurb: A poem on the Israelites' crossing of the Red Sea and the overthrow of Pharaoh's host.

sections.title: The Passage of the Red Sea

works.title: The Pastime of Pleasure
works.subtitle: An Allegorical Poem
works.author: Stephen Hawes
works.blurb: Hawes's allegorical romance in rhyme royal: the young Graunde Amoure learns the seven liberal arts in the Tower of Doctrine, wins the hand of La Bell Pucell by slaying giants and monsters, and is brought through age and death to the judgement of Fame, Time and Eternity.
