works.title: சிலப்பதிகாரம் (Silappatikaram)
works.subtitle: The Tale of the Anklet: the prologue and the thirty cantos, in the original Tamil
works.author: Ilango Adigal
works.blurb: The story of Kovalan, Kannagi and Madhavi, and of the anklet that brought down the city of Madurai, told in song, verse and rhythmic prose by the Chera prince turned ascetic Ilango Adigal.

works.title: The Sinless Child
works.author: Elizabeth Oakes Smith
works.blurb: A visionary ballad in seven parts: Eva, the fatherless cottage girl whom neighbours call the Sinless Child, reads the spiritual meaning of flowers, birds and sorrow, meets the repentant Albert Linne, and passes from the world.

works.title: Sir Amadace
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Sir Amadace, ruined by his own open-handedness, sets out with what money is left and finds a dead man refused burial because of his debts. He spends everything to lay the corpse in the ground, and the favour is repaid when a mysterious White Knight helps him win a princess and a kingdom, on one terrible condition.

works.title: Sir Eglamour of Artois
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme romance of Sir Eglamour, who wins the love of Christabel, daughter of the Earl of Artois, by slaying a giant and a monstrous boar, and by killing a dragon at Rome. After long separation, their child, carried off by a griffin, grows up to be a knight and, unknowing, is wed to his own mother, until a token reveals the truth and the family is reunited.

works.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
works.subtitle: A Middle-English Arthurian Romance
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A green-skinned knight rides into Arthur's Christmas feast with an impossible challenge; Sir Gawain's answer sends him on a year-long quest that tests his courage, his courtesy, and his honesty alike.

works.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: A green-skinned knight rides into Arthur's Christmas feast with an impossible challenge; Sir Gawain's answer sends him on a year-long quest that tests his courage, his courtesy, and his honesty alike. Here the poem is rendered in rhymed, bobbed-and-wheeled stanzas.

works.title: Sir Gawayne and the Grene Knyȝt (Middle English text)
works.subtitle: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
works.author: Gawain Poet
works.blurb: The original alliterative Middle English of the great Arthurian romance: a green-skinned knight rides into Camelot at Christmas, and Gawain's answer to his beheading game leads him through a year of trial to the castle of Bertilak, the temptations of the lady, and the green girdle.

works.title: Sir Isumbras
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme romance of a proud and prosperous knight who is warned by a bird to choose penance in this life. He loses wealth, wife and three sons, serves as a smith and a palmer, and at last regains all by God's mercy and wins a Christian kingdom from the Saracens.

works.title: Launfal
works.subtitle: Sir Launfal
works.author: Thomas Chestre
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme Breton lay of about 1,040 lines, adapted from Marie de France's Lanval and the anonymous Graelent: a knight of Arthur's court, impoverished and slighted by Guinevere, is loved by the fairy Tryamour.

works.title: Sir Orpheo
works.subtitle: Sir Orfeo
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A Middle English Breton lay of about 510 lines, the Orpheus story moved into fairyland: King Orpheo's queen Heurodis is carried off by the king of Faerie, and Orpheo gives up his crown to live as a harper in the wilderness, follows the fairy riders into their country, and wins her back with his playing.

works.title: Sir Perceval of Galles
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A tail-rhyme romance of the boy Perceval, reared in the wilds by his widowed mother, who rides to Arthur's court, avenges his father's death on the Red Knight and wins a lady's release from a Saracen sultan.

works.title: Sir Tristrem
works.subtitle: A verse rendering
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: Tristrem, son of Roland Riis and of Blancheflower, King Mark's sister, is brought up by the loyal Rohant and educated in the courtly arts before he comes to his uncle Mark in Cornwall. He kills the Irish champion Moraunt, is healed by Ysonde, wins her as Mark's bride, and shares with her a love that survives suspicion, banishment and exile.

works.title: Sister Songs
works.subtitle: An Offering to Two Sisters
works.author: Francis Thompson
works.blurb: Published in 1895, Sister Songs is Thompson’s offering to Monica and Madeline (Sylvia) Meynell, daughters of his patrons Wilfrid and Alice Meynell. It moves from a Proem addressed to Spring through two long parts to a closing Inscription.

works.title: Слово о пълку Игоревѣ (Slovo o polku Igoreve)
works.subtitle: The Lay of Igor's Campaign, in Old East Slavic (Old Russian), the 1800 first edition
works.author: Anonymous (The Lay of Igor's Campaign)
works.blurb: The Old Russian text of the only surviving epic of medieval Kievan Rus', on Prince Igor Svyatoslavich's ill-fated raid on the Polovtsy in 1185, as first printed by Musin-Pushkin in 1800 in pre-reform spelling and set as prose paragraphs.

sections.title: Слово о пълку Игоревѣ (Slovo o polku Igoreve)

works.title: Smrť Jánošíkova
works.subtitle: The Death of Jánošík
works.author: Ján Botto
works.blurb: Botto's ballad-epic of the outlaw Jánošík, hero of the Tatra highlands, who is taken, tried and executed; a landmark of Slovak Romantic poetry, first printed in 1862.

works.title: Smrt Smail-age Čengića
works.subtitle: The Death of Smail-aga Čengić
works.author: Ivan Mažuranić
works.blurb: Mažuranić's Romantic epic in five cantos on the death of the Ottoman lord Smail-aga Čengić at the hands of Montenegrin highlanders, first published in 1846.

works.title: Soledades
works.author: Luis de Góngora
works.blurb: Góngora's unfinished masterpiece of culteranismo: a shipwrecked youth, cast ashore, wanders through a pastoral landscape and a rustic wedding in silvas of dense Latinate splendour.

works.title: Solomon and Saturn
works.subtitle: The poetic dialogues
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.translator: trans. J. M. Kemble, The Dialogue of Salomon and Saturnus (Ælfric Society, 1848)
works.blurb: Old English verse dialogues in which the wise King Solomon answers the riddling questions of the Chaldean prince Saturn.

works.title: Solomon and Saturn (Old English)
works.subtitle: The poetic dialogues: Old English text
works.author: Anonymous (Old English)
works.blurb: Old English verse dialogues in which the wise King Solomon answers the riddling questions of the Chaldean prince Saturn.

works.title: Solomon on the Vanity of the World
works.subtitle: A Poem in Three Books
works.author: Matthew Prior
works.blurb: Prior's longest poem: Solomon looks for happiness in knowledge, pleasure and power, and finds that all is vanity. Each book opens with the poet's prose argument.

works.title: The Song of Hiawatha
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A trochaic epic drawing on Ojibwe legend, following the life of the hero Hiawatha — his childhood, wooing, feats, and eventual departure — in a rhythm modeled on the Finnish Kalevala.

sections.title: The Son of the Evening Star

works.title: The Song of the Merchant Kalashnikov
works.subtitle: A Song of the Tzar Ivan Vasilyevich, of the Young Oprichnik and of the Bold Merchant Kalashnikov
works.author: Mikhail Lermontov
works.blurb: In the Moscow of Ivan the Terrible, the merchant Kalashnikov fights and kills the Tsar's favourite oprichnik to avenge the insult to his wife, and pays for it on the block.

works.title: The Song of Los
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Los sings the long history of the laws and religions that bound Africa and Asia, until Orc's fires break out in Europe and America.

works.title: The Song of Roland
works.subtitle: La Chanson de Roland
works.author: Anonymous (Old French)
works.blurb: Betrayed by his stepfather Ganelon, Charlemagne's nephew Roland holds the pass at Roncevaux against the Saracens, refuses to sound his horn until too late, and dies a martyr; the Emperor then avenges him.

works.title: The Song of Roland
works.subtitle: La Chanson de Roland
works.author: Anonymous (Old French)
works.blurb: John O'Hagan's version renders the epic of Roland's last stand at Roncevaux in rhymed octosyllabic couplets, divided into three Parts and numbered laisses, with scene headings of his own.

sections.title: Part I: The Treason of Ganelon
Part II: The Prelude of the Great Battle (Laisses LXXXIII–CXLVII)
Part II: The Great Battle Continued (Laisses CXLVIII–CXCVII)

works.title: The Song of Songs
works.subtitle: Authorized Version of the Song of Solomon.
works.author: The Bible (Authorized King James Version)
works.blurb: An anthology of Hebrew love lyrics, traditionally ascribed to Solomon.

works.title: The Sorcerer
works.author: W. S. Gilbert
works.blurb: Alexis Pointdextre, newly betrothed to Aline, is so taken with the notion of love as a cure for all social ills that he engages John Wellington Wells, a family sorcerer, to dose the whole village of Ploverleigh with a love potion. Everyone who drinks falls in love with the first person they meet on waking, with absurd results, until the spell can be undone only by a sacrifice.

works.title: Sordello
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Browning's long narrative poem in six books follows the thirteenth-century Mantuan troubadour Sordello through the Guelf and Ghibelline wars of northern Italy, and is chiefly a study of the growth and failure of a poet's soul.

works.title: A Soul's Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A two-part drama set in the Italian town of Faenza. In the verse first act, "the poetry of Chiappino's life", the blustering republican Chiappino quarrels with his friend Luitolfo and strikes down the tyrannical Provost. In the prose second act the people make him Provost in turn, and the Pope's Legate Ogniben quietly takes his measure.

works.title: The Romaunce of the Sowdone of Babylone and of Ferumbras His Sone Who Conquerede Rome
works.subtitle: The Sowdone of Babylone
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A Middle English romance in rhymed quatrains. The Saracen Soudan Laban of Babylon sacks Rome; his son Ferumbras is defeated and converted, and his daughter Floripas helps the imprisoned peers of Charlemagne win their freedom before Charles himself defeats Laban in Spain. Preserved in a single manuscript.

works.title: The Spagnoletto
works.subtitle: A Play in Five Acts
works.author: Emma Lazarus
works.blurb: Naples, about 1655: the painter Josef Ribera, called the Spagnoletto, rose from beggary in Rome to the favour of princes, and he idolises his younger daughter Maria-Rosa. When she is wooed by Don John of Austria, the viceroy's son, her passion leads her into a fatal secret that breaks her father's mind. Lazarus's blank-verse tragedy follows his revenge and her flight to a Palermo convent.

works.title: The Spanish Gypsy
works.author: George Eliot
works.blurb: A dramatic poem of fifteenth-century Spain, in five books. Fedalma, a Gypsy foundling brought up in the household of the Duke Silva, is about to marry him when her father Zarca, chief of the Zincali, claims her for the cause of his people. She renounces her love, and after her father's death sails with the exiled Gypsies for Africa. It mixes narrative blank verse, dramatic dialogue with named speakers, and songs.

works.title: The Spanish Student
works.subtitle: A Play in Three Acts
works.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
works.blurb: A verse play set in Spain. The student Victorian loves Preciosa, a gypsy dancer of Madrid, whom the profligate Count of Lara also pursues. Her gypsy guardian, jealousies and a slandering plot divide the lovers, and the story passes from Madrid to the Guadarrama mountains, with serenades and gypsy songs set within the dialogue, before her true parentage is revealed.

works.title: The Spanish Tragedy
works.subtitle: Containing the lamentable end of Don Horatio and Bel-imperia, with the pitiful death of old Hieronimo
works.author: Thomas Kyd
works.blurb: The ghost of the Spanish courtier Don Andrea, slain in battle, is led back from the underworld by Revenge to watch his killer Balthazar punished. Instead he sees Andrea's friend Horatio murdered in his father's arbour and Hieronimo, the Knight-Marshall of Spain, driven half mad by grief as he seeks justice from a corrupt court. Hieronimo at last stages a play before the court in which the real deaths are carried out.

works.title: The Spirit of Discovery by Sea
works.subtitle: A Descriptive and Historical Poem
works.author: William Lisle Bowles
works.blurb: A blank-verse poem in five books on the history of maritime discovery, from the Ark to the voyages of the eighteenth century.

works.title: The Historie of Squyer Meldrum
works.author: Sir David Lyndsay
works.blurb: Lyndsay's verse romance of William Meldrum of Cleish and Binns, a Fife laird: a gallant, fighting, loving squire who defends a lady from robbers, wins a tournament in Ireland and a wife at home, and dies in his bed, leaving a Testament that is part mock-heroic, part valediction.

sections.title: The Historie of Squyer William Meldrum, of Cleische and Bynnis
The Testament of the Nobill and Vailyeand Squyer William Meldrum of the Bynnis

works.title: The Squyr of Lowe Degre
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A romance of about 1,130 lines in rhymed couplets: a squire of low degree loves the king of Hungary's daughter. She bids him win fame in arms abroad, the king's steward betrays him, and after seven years of mourning over a body she wrongly takes to be his, the princess finds him alive and they are married.

works.title: The St. Lawrence and the Saguenay
works.author: Charles Sangster
works.blurb: Sangster's voyage poem, a lover's journey down the St. Lawrence and up the Saguenay in 110 Spenserian stanzas, with lyrics sung along the way.

sections.title: The St. Lawrence and the Saguenay

works.title: Le Morte Arthur
works.subtitle: The stanzaic Morte Arthur
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: An English verse romance of about 1400 in eight-line stanzas, telling the last days of King Arthur: the love of Lancelot and Guinevere, the Maid of Ascolot, the war between Arthur and Lancelot, Mordred's treason, the passing of Arthur and the deaths of Lancelot and Guinevere. It was a main source of Malory's last books.

works.title: Stanze per la giostra
works.author: Angelo Poliziano
works.blurb: Poliziano's unfinished ottava rima poem on the joust won by Giuliano de' Medici in 1475, breaking off after two books with Giuliano's love for Simonetta Cattaneo and the vision of Venus's realm.

works.title: The Story of Rimini
works.author: Leigh Hunt
works.blurb: Hunt's retelling of the story of Paolo and Francesca, from Dante's Inferno, in four cantos of heroic couplets: the bride fetched to Rimini, her journey, the fatal passion and its end.

works.title: Strafford: A Tragedy
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Browning's first play, written for the actor Macready. Thomas Wentworth, Earl of Strafford, King Charles I's chief minister, returns from Ireland to face the Parliamentary party led by his old friend John Pym. Betrayed by the weak King he serves, Strafford is impeached and condemned, and the play ends with their last meeting before his execution.

works.title: Such Stuff as Dreams Are Made Of
works.subtitle: A drama taken from Calderón's La Vida es Sueño
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: Basilio, King of Poland, confines his son Segismund from birth because of a prophecy, then drugs him and lets him wake in the palace for a day to test it. FitzGerald's free version of La vida es sueño, whose title he turns into a joke on the stolen phrase.

works.title: The Lives of the Twelve Caesars
works.subtitle: With the Lives of the Grammarians, Rhetoricians and Poets
works.author: Suetonius
works.translator: trans. Alexander Thomson, revised by T. Forester (1855)
works.blurb: Suetonius's lives of the Caesars from Julius to Domitian, with his surviving short Lives of grammarians, rhetoricians and poets, in Alexander Thomson's translation (1796) as revised by T. Forester for Bohn's Classical Library (1855). Thomson's own essays on the history and literature of each period are omitted.

works.title: The Sugar-Cane
works.subtitle: A Poem in Four Books
works.author: James Grainger
works.blurb: A georgic poem in blank verse on the cultivation of sugar-cane in the British West Indies, in four books: soils and planting, pests and storms, the sugar-works, and the management of enslaved labourers. Grainger wrote it after practising medicine on St Kitts; it was much praised in its day and is now chiefly read as a document of the Caribbean plantation economy.

works.title: ਸੁਖਮਨੀ ਸਾਹਿਬ (Sukhmani Sahib)
works.subtitle: ਗਉੜੀ ਸੁਖਮਨੀ ਮਃ ੫
works.author: Guru Arjan
works.blurb: The 'Jewel of Peace', Guru Arjan's long meditation on the divine Name in twenty-four ashtapadis of eight stanzas each, each opening with a salok; included in the Adi Granth (1604) in the Gauri measure.

works.title: The Suppliant Maidens
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: The fifty daughters of Danaus flee Egypt to escape forced marriage to their cousins, the sons of Aegyptus, and beg sanctuary at Argos. King Pelasgus must choose between sheltering them and war; the Argive assembly votes to protect them, and the Egyptian herald's threats are turned back as the maidens give thanks.

works.title: The Suppliants
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: After the failed assault on Thebes, the mothers of the fallen Argive champions come as suppliants to Eleusis, begging Theseus to recover their sons’ unburied bodies. Persuaded by his mother Aethra, Theseus faces down Thebes’ herald, wins the battle, and returns the dead for burial, while Evadne leaps onto her husband’s pyre; Athena closes the play with an oath binding Argos to Athens.

works.title: Ἱκέτιδες (Hiketides)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Argive mothers whose sons died before Thebes kneel at the altar of Demeter at Eleusis, and Aithra persuades her son Theseus to recover the bodies from the Thebans. Theseus argues with a Theban herald, who defends tyranny and threatens war, then wins the battle and brings the dead home for burial. Capaneus, struck down by Zeus's lightning, is burned on a pyre of his own, and his wife Evadne leaps onto it to die beside him, leaving her father Iphis desolate. Athena appears at the end to bind Argos by oath never to attack Athens, and the sons of the dead chieftains take up their fathers' ashes.

works.title: Ἱκέτιδες (Hiketides)
works.author: Aeschylus
works.blurb: The Greek text of this tragedy by Aeschylus in the Smyth Loeb edition, set out by episode and choral division, so that it can be read beside the English verse translation of the same play.

works.title: The Suppliants
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: After the failed assault of the Seven against Thebes, the mothers of the fallen Argive chiefs come to Eleusis and beg Theseus to win back the unburied bodies of their sons. Arthur Way renders Euripides' tragedy in rhymed English verse, with the choral odes in lyric measures.

works.title: Suze sina razmetnoga
works.subtitle: Religious poem in three laments (first printed Venice, 1622)
works.author: Ivan Gundulić
works.blurb: Gundulić's first printed work, a monologue of repentance in three laments, Sin, Recognition and Contrition, voiced by the Prodigal Son of the Gospel of Luke.

works.title: The Vision of Vasavadatta
works.subtitle: Svapna-Vasavadattam, translated by A. C. Woolner and Lakshman Sarup
works.author: Bhasa
works.translator: A. C. Woolner and Lakshman Sarup (1930)
works.blurb: Woolner and Sarup's English version of the Sanskrit play, in which the Vatsa king Udayana, believing his queen Vasavadatta burnt alive, marries the princess of Magadha, while the queen, in disguise, waits in her household. In the fifth act he dreams of her, wakes and sees her go.

works.title: स्वप्नवासवदत्तम् (Svapnavasavadatta)
works.subtitle: The Vision of Vasavadatta, in the original Sanskrit
works.author: Bhasa
works.blurb: A Sanskrit play in six acts attributed to Bhasa: the Vatsa king Udayana, believed to have lost his queen Vasavadatta in a fire, marries Padmavati of Magadha, while Vasavadatta, in disguise, serves in her household. In the fifth act the sleeping king dreams of her and half wakes to see her; hence the title.

works.title: Oedipus Tyrannus; or, Swellfoot the Tyrant
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Two Acts, Translated from the Original Doric
works.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
works.blurb: Shelley's Aristophanic farce transforms the Queen Caroline affair into a Theban comedy: King Swellfoot and his ministers scheme to put Iona Taurina, the Queen, on trial, while the Swinish Multitude of the people grunts in her defence. Written at Pisa in 1819 as George IV sought to divorce his wife, it was published anonymously in 1820 and suppressed within days.

works.title: Sylvia; or, The May Queen
works.subtitle: A Lyrical Drama
works.author: George Darley
works.blurb: A lyrical drama set in the Apennines. The traveller Romanzo falls in love with Sylvia, May Queen of a glen shared between the fairy queen Morgana and Ararach, king of the fiends. The fiends plot to seize Sylvia and to torment Romanzo with a phantom show, while the comic servant Andrea, transformed by the fiends, blunders between the two parties, until the fairy host drives off the fiends and the lovers are reunited. Blank verse, songs and comic prose.

works.title: Syphilis
works.subtitle: A Poetical History of the French Disease
works.author: Girolamo Fracastoro
works.blurb: Fracastoro's Latin didactic poem on the origin, nature and cure of the new disease that gave syphilis its name, in Nahum Tate's English couplets.

works.title: The Life and Death of Julius Agricola
works.subtitle: Church and Brodribb translation, 1876
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1876)
works.blurb: Tacitus's memoir of his father-in-law Gnaeus Julius Agricola, governor of Britain, from his boyhood in Gaul through the campaigns against the Caledonians to his death under Domitian, in Church and Brodribb's English prose of 1876.

sections.title: The Life and Death of Julius Agricola

works.title: The Annals
works.subtitle: Church and Brodribb translation, 1876
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1876)
works.blurb: Tacitus's annals of the Roman Empire from the death of Augustus through the reigns of Tiberius, Claudius and Nero, in the surviving books (I–VI and XI–XVI), in Church and Brodribb's English prose of 1876.

works.title: A Dialogue on Oratory
works.subtitle: Church and Brodribb translation, 1877
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1877)
works.blurb: A conversation set in the reign of Vespasian among the orators Marcus Aper, Julius Secundus, Vipstanus Messalla and the poet Curiatius Maternus on why eloquence has declined since the age of Cicero, in Church and Brodribb's English prose of 1877.

works.title: Germania
works.subtitle: The Origin and Situation of the Germans
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1876)
works.blurb: Tacitus's short ethnography of the Germanic peoples beyond the Rhine and Danube, their land, customs, government, war and religion, and the tribe-by-tribe survey that follows, in Church and Brodribb's English prose of 1876.

works.title: The History
works.subtitle: Church and Brodribb translation, 1864
works.author: Tacitus
works.translator: trans. Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1864)
works.blurb: Tacitus's account of the civil wars of AD 69 and the Flavian accession: Galba, Otho and Vitellius, the rise of Vespasian and the revolt of Civilis on the Rhine, in the English prose of Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb (1864). The surviving books end mid-narrative.

works.title: The Histories
works.subtitle: Fyfe translation, 1912
works.author: Tacitus
works.blurb: Tacitus's account of the civil wars of AD 69 and the Flavian accession: Galba, Otho and Vitellius, the rise of Vespasian, the revolt of Civilis on the Rhine and the siege of Jerusalem, in W. Hamilton Fyfe's English prose of 1912. The surviving books end mid-narrative.

works.title: The Táin
works.subtitle: Táin Bó Cúailnge, the Cattle-Raid of Cooley, in English verse
works.author: Anonymous (Old Irish)
works.blurb: The central epic of the Ulster cycle in Mary Hutton's English blank verse: Queen Maev of Connaught and King Ailill gather the Four Fifths of Ireland to seize the Brown Bull of Cooley, and the boy-hero Cúchulainn (her Cucullin) holds the Ulster border alone until Ulster rises. It opens with the tale of how the poets recovered the lost Táin from the ghost of Fergus.

works.title: The Taking of Ilios
works.subtitle: Prose translation by A. W. Mair
works.author: Tryphiodorus
works.blurb: A short late-antique epic on the last night of the Trojan War, from the building of the wooden horse to the sacrifice of Polyxena.

works.title: A Tale of Eternity
works.subtitle: The Haunted Hurst
works.author: Gerald Massey
works.blurb: Gerald Massey's long narrative poem of haunting and the afterlife, in seven parts, first published in 1870.

works.title: The Tale of Gamelyn
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A younger son, Gamelyn, is cheated of his inheritance and kept in servitude by his elder brother. He wrestles his way to fame, escapes his bonds, and becomes king of the outlaws in the greenwood. When his brother has him arraigned, Gamelyn returns, takes the judge's seat and hangs the corrupt justice, the sheriff and the jury. The story is the source of Shakespeare's As You Like It.

works.title: A Tale of Paraguay
works.subtitle: Dedication, Proem and four cantos (1825)
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: Southey's Spenserian tale of the Guarani Indian pair Quiara and Monnema, left alone by a plague of smallpox, and of their son Yeruti and daughter Mooma, whom the Jesuit missionary Dobrizhoffer receives into the mission of St Joachin; written in 1824-25 and dedicated to his daughter Edith May.

works.title: Tamburlaine the Great: Part 1
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: Marlowe's first great play, in blank verse, follows the Scythian shepherd Tamburlaine from his seizure of the Persian crown to his triumph over Bajazeth, the Soldan of Egypt and the city of Damascus.

works.title: Tamburlaine the Great: Part 2
works.author: Christopher Marlowe
works.blurb: The sequel in blank verse follows Tamburlaine through the death of Zenocrate, the killing of his faint-hearted son Calyphas and the burning of Babylon, to his own death.

works.title: The Taming of the Shrew
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: A tinker, Christopher Sly, is tricked by a Lord into believing he is a nobleman, and a company of players performs the play-within-a-play for him. In Padua, Baptista will not let his gentle younger daughter Bianca marry until his sharp-tongued elder daughter Katherina has a husband, so the fortune-hunting Petruchio woos Katherina and sets about taming her by contradiction and deprivation. While Bianca's suitors scheme and exchange disguises, Petruchio wins a wager at the final feast when Katherina alone obeys her husband's summons.

works.title: 牡丹亭 (Mudan ting) — The Peony Pavilion
works.author: Tang Xianzu
works.blurb: The Nanan prefect's daughter Du Liniang falls asleep in her garden, dreams of a young scholar, Liu Mengmei, and wastes away of longing for him. She paints her own portrait, dies, and is buried under a plum tree. Three years later Liu finds the portrait, her ghost visits him, and with the help of the underworld judge and his own devotion he opens her tomb and she lives again. They marry in the face of her father's disbelief, a rebel siege and Liu's imprisonment, until the emperor sets all right. Written in sung verse in fifty-five scenes, it is the great romance of the Chinese stage; the dream scene, 驚夢, is its most famous passage.

works.title: Tartuffe; or, The Hypocrite
works.author: Molière
works.blurb: Orgon, a prosperous Parisian householder, has taken the pious Tartuffe into his home and fallen wholly under his spell, promising him his daughter's hand and his fortune. Orgon's family, led by the sharp-tongued maid Dorine and his wife Elmire, try to open his eyes to the impostor, who is in fact scheming to seize the house and seduce Elmire. Molière's comedy of religious hypocrisy was banned for five years after its first performance in 1664.

works.title: Temora: An Ancient Epic Poem
works.subtitle: In Eight Books
works.author: James Macpherson
works.blurb: Ossian's epic of Cairbar's murder of King Cormac and Fingal's expedition to Ireland to restore the throne, ending in the battle with Cathmor, in measured prose.

works.title: The Tempest
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Prospero, the usurped Duke of Milan, has lived twelve years on an enchanted island with his daughter Miranda, served by the spirit Ariel and the savage Caliban. When his enemies sail past, he raises a storm and wrecks their ship, and through illusion, music and a courtship between Miranda and Ferdinand he brings them to repentance. In the end he forgives his brother, frees Ariel, and abjures his magic.

works.title: The Temple of Nature
works.subtitle: or, The Origin of Society
works.author: Erasmus Darwin
works.blurb: Darwin's last poem, published after his death, traces in four cantos the progress of life from its first stirrings in the ocean to the rise of mind, society and morality. Written in heroic couplets, it versifies his evolutionary speculations in the mysteries of an ancient temple.

sections.title: Canto III. Progress of the Mind
Canto IV. Of Good and Evil

works.title: Adelphi
works.subtitle: The Brothers
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's last comedy: two brothers, one strict and one indulgent, raise two sons between them, and a scandal, a stolen music-girl and a clever slave test both methods of upbringing, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Andria
works.subtitle: The Fair Andrian
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's first comedy: a young Athenian's secret love for a girl from Andros, a father's pretended wedding plans, and a clever slave, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Eunuchus
works.subtitle: The Eunuch
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's most popular comedy: a courtesan, a boastful captain, a disguised young man and a parasite, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Heautontimorumenos
works.subtitle: The Self-Tormentor
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's play of two fathers and their sons: a harsh old man punishes himself with farm labour for driving his son abroad, while his neighbour's son and a scheming slave run up a courtesan's bills, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Hecyra
works.subtitle: The Mother-in-Law
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's most reversed play, twice driven from the stage: a young husband's secret guilt, a wife in hiding and a wrongly blamed mother-in-law, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Phormio
works.subtitle: The Scheming Parasite
works.author: Terence
works.blurb: Terence's most celebrated comedy of intrigue: a parasite weds a penniless girl to a young Athenian by a trick at law, and two old brothers are caught out by a secret that Phormio holds, in Riley's literal prose.

works.title: Teseida delle nozze d'Emilia
works.subtitle: La Teseide
works.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
works.blurb: Boccaccio's epic in twelve books of ottava rima, the first of its kind in Italian: the rivalry of Arcita and Palemone for Emilia, the source of Chaucer's Knight's Tale.

works.title: Il Tesoretto
works.author: Brunetto Latini
works.blurb: Brunetto Latini’s allegorical poem in rhymed settenari, a dream-vision in which the poet, returning from an embassy to Castile, loses his way in a wood and meets Nature, Virtue and Love before his penitence.

works.title: The Testament of a Prime Minister
works.author: John Davidson
works.blurb: The fourth of Davidson's blank-verse Testaments, spoken from his deathbed by a Prime Minister who ruled Britain and its Empire as a materialist and a doubter. He tells of a vision of Hell, of an English God made for the rich, and of the poor of London's riverside, and ends by affirming that matter, in man, has become conscious of itself.

sections.title: The Testament of a Prime Minister

works.title: The Testament of Beauty
works.subtitle: A Poem in Four Books
works.author: Robert Bridges
works.blurb: Published on Bridges's eighty-fifth birthday, in his last year as Poet Laureate, this long meditative poem in loose Alexandrines sets out his philosophy of beauty as the meeting-point of instinct and spirit in the mind of man. It is in four books: Introduction, Selfhood, Breed and Ethick.

works.title: The Testament of John Davidson
works.author: John Davidson
works.blurb: Davidson's last Testament, published in the year before his death. Turned out of the world, a speaker builds himself a palace in the Milky Way and lives on light and sound, until he descends to earth to die by his own hand; on the way he meets the goddess Athene and the old gods, and argues with them about death, power and the self-knowledge of matter. A light-hearted 'Honeymoon' stands before it as prologue, and the song of 'The Last Journey' follows as epilogue.

works.title: Thalaba the Destroyer
works.author: Robert Southey
works.blurb: An Arabian romance in twelve books, in irregular unrhymed verse: the orphan Thalaba is chosen to destroy the sorcerers of the Domdaniel caverns that murdered his family.

works.title: The Apostle
works.subtitle: Az apostol
works.author: Sándor Petőfi
works.blurb: Petőfi's long poem of democratic faith: the foundling Szilveszter, raised in cruelty, grows up to become a wandering preacher of liberty and brotherhood, here in twenty parts in English verse by William N. Loew.

works.title: The Blameless Prince
works.author: Edmund Clarence Stedman
works.blurb: A romance in verse of a queen, her prince and the lady he loves, told in a gentle, tragic key.

works.title: The Bride's Prelude
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: An unfinished narrative poem begun in 1848: on the morning of Aloyse's wedding she tells her sister Amelotte the story of her lost love.

works.title: The Bridge
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Hart Crane
works.blurb: Hart Crane’s long poem of America, taking the Brooklyn Bridge as its emblem: from Columbus’s landfall in Ave Maria through the Pocahontas section, Cutty Sark, the Whitmanic Cape Hatteras, the Three Songs, Quaker Hill and The Tunnel, to the closing hymn of Atlantis.

sections.title: II. Powhatan’s Daughter: 1. The Harbor Dawn
V. Three Songs: 2. National Winter Garden

works.title: The Cenci
works.subtitle: A Tragedy in Five Acts
works.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
works.blurb: Shelley's blank-verse tragedy of the Roman nobleman Francesco Cenci, whose cruelty to his family drives his daughter Beatrice to plot his murder; she is tried and executed for the deed. Based on a sixteenth-century Roman crime, it was written in 1819.

works.title: The Doctor
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, Second Series: 1
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: The longest of the Fo'c's'le Yarns: a seaman's tale in rhymed Manx dialect of the Doctor and the people around him, told to a forecastle audience that suspects him of spinning stories.

works.title: The Excursion
works.author: William Wordsworth
works.blurb: Wordsworth's nine-book blank-verse poem follows the poet, the Wanderer, the Solitary and the Pastor through a Lake District excursion in which grief and despondency are met with reflections on nature, faith, human suffering and the moral life.

sections.title: Book Sixth: The Church-yard among the Mountains
Book Seventh: The Church-yard among the Mountains (continued)
Book Ninth: Discourse of the Wanderer, and an Evening Visit to the Lake

works.title: The Golden Violet
works.author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.)
works.blurb: A frame poem of a two-day minstrel contest in Provence for the prize of the Golden Violet, in which each minstrel sings his or her own tale.

sections.title: The Broken Spell: The First Provençal Minstrel's Lay
The Falcon: The Lay of the Norman Knight
The Dream: The Lay of the Scottish Minstrel
The Child of the Sea: The Lay of the Second Provençal Bard
The Ring: The German Minnesinger's Tale
The Queen of Cyprus: The Provençal Lady's Lay
The Rose: The Italian Minstrel's Tale
The Haunted Lake: The Irish Minstrel's Legend
The Wreath: Tale of the Moorish Bard
Sir Walter Manny at His Father's Tomb: The English Knight's Ballad

works.title: The Improvisatrice
works.author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.)
works.blurb: An Italian poet-improvisatrice tells her own story of art, song and an unhappy love for Lorenzo, with the songs and tales she sings along the way as their own sections.

sections.title: Song (Farewell! we shall not meet again)

works.title: The Indiaman
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, Third Series: 3
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A seaman's dialect yarn of Fanny Graeme, who caught her frock boarding at the Prince's dock, and of Peter Young, whom she married.

works.title: The Inn Album
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: A blank-verse tale in eight parts of a young man, an older cardsharp and the woman between them, set in the parlour of a country inn.

works.title: The Jacquerie
works.subtitle: A Fragment
works.author: Sidney Lanier
works.blurb: Lanier's unfinished early narrative poem about the French peasant revolt known as the Jacquerie, left in five chapters.

works.title: The King's Tragedy
works.subtitle: James I. of Scots, 20th February 1437
works.author: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
works.blurb: A ballad in which Catherine Douglas, called Kate Barlass, tells the murder of King James I of Scotland in 1437.

works.title: The Lost Pleiad
works.author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.)
works.blurb: A story from the stars: the legend of the Pleiad that left her sisters, and what it costs a heavenly love to touch the earth.

works.title: The Manx Witch
works.subtitle: A Story of the Laxdale Mines
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A dialect-verse story of the Laxdale mines, in which a witch's spells trouble Nessy Brew and the miners who court her.

works.title: The Passing Bell
works.author: John S. B. Monsell
works.blurb: A meditation in five parts on the old custom of tolling the church bell for a dying soul, each part turning its warning on a different temptation: the man of business, the domestic man, the young and giddy, the sinful, and the pastor.

works.title: The Piper
works.subtitle: A Play in Four Acts
works.author: Josephine Preston Peabody
works.blurb: Hamelin, 1284. A strolling player with a pipe, who has watched the burghers break their promise to pay him for freeing the town of rats, returns to the market-place and leads the children away. Peabody's verse play, which won the Stratford-upon-Avon prize in 1910, makes the old legend a drama of greed, grief and the pull of music, centred on the lame boy Jan and the town's guilt.

works.title: The Prelude
works.subtitle: or Growth of a Poet's Mind
works.author: William Wordsworth
works.blurb: Wordsworth's blank-verse autobiography traces the growth of his imagination from boyhood in the Lake District through Cambridge, London and revolutionary France to the recovery of his poetic vocation.

sections.title: Book I: Introduction — Childhood and School-time
Book VI: Cambridge and the Alps
Book VIII: Retrospect — Love of Nature Leading to Love of Man
Book XII: Imagination and Taste, How Impaired and Restored
Book XIII: Imagination and Taste, How Impaired and Restored (concluded)

works.title: The Princess
works.subtitle: A Medley
works.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
works.blurb: Tennyson's blank-verse medley of a prince who woos Princess Ida, founder of a women's university, framed by a summer fete at Vivian-place and broken by its famous songs, among them 'Tears, idle tears' and 'The splendour falls'.

works.title: The Progress of Liberty
works.author: Mary Robinson
works.blurb: Mary Robinson's blank-verse poem on liberty, in two books, printed in the third volume of her posthumous Poetical Works of 1806.

works.title: The Ring and the Book
works.author: Robert Browning
works.blurb: Browning's twelve-book epic retells a seventeenth-century Roman murder trial through the conflicting voices of the town, the lawyers, the killer, his victim and the Pope.

sections.title: I. The Ring and the Book
VIII. Dominus Hyacinthus de Archangelis, Pauperum Procurator
IX. Juris Doctor Johannes-Baptista Bottinius, Fisci et Rev. Cam. Apostol. Advocatus
XII. The Book and the Ring

works.title: The Russiadde
works.subtitle: A Fragment of an Ancient Epic Poem, Supposed to Have Been Written by Gilbert Hume, a Sutor of Selkirk
works.author: James Hogg
works.blurb: Hogg's burlesque fragment of an epic, in two books, supposedly by a Selkirk cobbler.

works.title: The Schoolmasters
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, Second Series: 3
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A shorter dialect yarn on the three schools of the parish and their masters, told by the speaker of the earlier Christmas Rose.

works.title: The Seasons
works.author: James Thomson
works.blurb: Thomson's blank-verse poem on the four seasons of the year, with a closing hymn, a landmark of eighteenth-century nature poetry.

works.title: The Task
works.subtitle: A Poem, in Six Books
works.author: William Cowper
works.blurb: Begun as a joke on the subject of a sofa, The Task grew into Cowper’s masterpiece — a long, ruminative blank-verse walk through rural retirement, nature, solitude, and faith.

sections.title: Book V: The Winter Morning Walk
Book VI: The Winter Walk at Noon

works.title: The Temple of Glass
works.author: John Lydgate
works.blurb: A Chaucerian dream vision in which the poet, carried in sleep to a temple of glass, overhears a lady and her knightly lover lament and console each other in unrequited love — modelled closely on Chaucer's House of Fame and Parliament of Fowls.

works.title: The Troubadour
works.author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.)
works.blurb: A verse romance in four cantos of the troubadour Raymond, set in Provence, with songs and tales worked into the story.

works.title: The Venetian Bracelet
works.author: Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.)
works.blurb: A tale of Venice in fourteen numbered parts, centred on a serpent bracelet and the doomed love of Amenaide.

works.title: The Wanderer
works.subtitle: A Vision, in Five Cantos
works.author: Richard Savage
works.blurb: A visionary meditation in heroic couplets, in which a wanderer in retirement weighs the still life against the active and finds that misfortune can refine the mind.

works.title: Thebaid
works.author: Statius
works.blurb: Statius’s epic of the war of the Seven against Thebes, in twelve books, from the quarrel of Oedipus’s sons to the burial of the dead.

works.title: The First Book of Statius's Thebais
works.author: Statius
works.blurb: Pope's youthful heroic-couplet version of the first book of Statius's epic of the war of the Seven against Thebes, from the curse of Oedipus to the hymn to Apollo at the court of Adrastus.

works.title: Θεόγνιδος Ἐλεγεῖαι (The Elegies of Theognis, Greek text)
works.author: Theognis of Megara
works.blurb: The whole body of elegiac verse that has come down under the name of Theognis of Megara: some 1,389 lines of maxims, political warnings, drinking songs and love poems addressed mostly to a young man, Cyrnus, followed by a second book of poems to boys. The Greek text is that of Bergk's 1868 edition, set out elegy by elegy.

works.title: The Theogony
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: Elton’s blank-verse version of Hesiod’s account of the birth of the gods, from Chaos and Earth through the Titans to the victory of Zeus.

works.title: Theogony
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: Hesiod’s account of the birth of the gods, from Chaos and Earth through the Titans to the victory of Zeus, opened by his own story of being called to poetry by the Muses on Mount Helicon.

works.title: Θεογονία (Theogonia)
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: The Greek text of Hesiod’s account of the birth of the gods, from Chaos and Earth through the Titans to the victory of Zeus, opened by the poet’s own story of being called to song by the Muses on Mount Helicon.

works.title: Theogony
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: A prose version of Hesiod’s account of the origin of the gods, opening with the Muses of Helikon and tracing the line from Chaos and Earth through the Titans to the rule of Zeus and the unions of gods with mortals.

works.title: The Characters
works.author: Theophrastus
works.translator: trans. Charles E. Bennett and William A. Hammond (1902)
works.blurb: Thirty brief sketches of human failings, from the Dissembler and the Flatterer to the Late Learner and the Vicious Man, drawn with a few bold strokes.

works.title: The City of Dreadful Night
works.author: James Thomson (B.V.)
works.blurb: James Thomson's poem of a nocturnal city of despair, in twenty-one numbered sections, with an epigraph from Dante, one from Leopardi and a Proem.

works.title: Three Judgments at a Blow
works.author: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
works.blurb: In the Aragon of Pedro IV, a quarrel between two noble houses and a blow struck in the dark bring three sentences down together on the House of Urrea and the King's Minister. The title is Calderón's own riddle, answered in the closing lines: three judgments summed up in a single blow.

works.title: The History of the Grecian War
works.subtitle: The war between Athens and Sparta, 431–404 BC, in eight books
works.author: Thucydides
works.blurb: Thucydides' unfinished account of the war between Athens and Sparta, in the first English translation made directly from the Greek, by the philosopher Thomas Hobbes, in the seventeenth-century English of the 1843 Molesworth edition.

works.title: History of the Peloponnesian War
works.subtitle: The war between Athens and Sparta, 431–404 BC, in eight books
works.author: Thucydides
works.blurb: Thucydides' unfinished account of the twenty-seven years' war between Athens and Sparta, including Pericles' Funeral Oration and the Melian Dialogue, in Richard Crawley's translation.

works.title: Thyestes
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Atreus feigns reconciliation with his brother Thyestes and takes revenge by serving him a feast of his own sons.

works.title: Thyestes
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: The ghost of Tantalus and a Fury drive the house of Pelops to a new crime. King Atreus, pretending reconciliation, lures his exiled brother Thyestes home to share the throne. Atreus slaughters Thyestes’ sons, and at a banquet serves their flesh to their father, who learns what he has eaten only when the severed heads are shown to him. The play ends in Thyestes’ helpless curse upon his brother.

works.title: Tiriel
works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: The blind and aged king Tiriel curses his sons, wanders to the vales of Har, and dies at last before the feet of his gentle, childlike parents.

works.title: The Maiden’s Vow (Tiruppavai)
works.subtitle: Andal’s Tiruppavai in English verse
works.author: Andal
works.blurb: Twenty-four of the thirty stanzas of Andal’s Tiruppavai in J. S. M. Hooper’s English verse, each numbered as its Tamil pasuram: the cowherd girls rouse one another and the sleeping Krishna to bathe in Margali and ask for the drum.

works.title: திருப்பாவை (Tiruppavai)
works.subtitle: The Maiden’s Vow, in Tamil
works.author: Andal
works.blurb: Thirty pasurams in which the young Andal, as a cowherd girl, calls her friends from sleep to bathe in the month of Margali and win the favour of Krishna: the best-known poem of the Tamil Alvars, sung every winter in Vaishnava temples.

works.title: 'Tis Pity She's a Whore
works.author: John Ford
works.blurb: In Parma the scholar Giovanni confesses to his friar that he loves his sister Annabella, and the two become secret lovers. When she is found to be with child she is hastily married to the nobleman Soranzo, whose servant Vasques coaxes the truth out of her tutoress Putana. The play closes at Soranzo's birthday feast, where Giovanni appears with a terrible proof of his love.

works.title: The Tragedy of Titus Andronicus
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Titus Andronicus, returning to Rome after a war against the Goths, has Tamora's eldest son put to death in sacrifice and kills his own son Mutius, and Tamora, made empress, takes revenge through her sons Chiron and Demetrius, who rape Lavinia, Titus's daughter, and cut off her hands and tongue. Two more of Titus's sons are executed on a false charge, and Titus loses a hand to a false bargain for their lives. Titus kills Chiron and Demetrius, bakes them in a pie served to Tamora, then kills Lavinia and Tamora; Saturninus kills Titus and is killed in turn, leaving Lucius to rule Rome and Aaron to be buried to the chest and left to starve.

works.title: Toldi estéje
works.subtitle: Költői beszély
works.author: János Arany
works.blurb: Arany's verse sequel to Toldi: the aged Miklós Toldi, withdrawn to his estate at Nagyfalu and brooding over the king's neglect, is drawn back to court and to one last combat. Six cantos of eight-line stanzas, begun in 1847 and published in 1854; the elegiac close of the Toldi trilogy.

works.title: Toldi
works.subtitle: Költői beszély
works.author: János Arany
works.blurb: Arany's verse romance of Miklós Toldi, the Hungarian peasant giant who, scorned by his brother, flees to the reeds, returns to Buda and wins the king's favour by defeating a Czech champion. Twelve cantos of eight-line stanzas; the poem that made Arany famous.

works.title: The Hollanders in Nova Zembla
works.subtitle: 1596–1597: An Arctic Poem
works.author: Hendrik Tollens
works.blurb: The wintering of Willem Barents and Jacob van Heemskerck’s Dutch crew on Novaya Zemlya in 1596–97, told in twelve cantos of blank verse.

sections.title: Canto V. The Building of the Hut

works.title: Tommy Big-Eyes
works.subtitle: Fo'c's'le Yarns, First Series: IV
works.author: Thomas Edward Brown
works.blurb: A dialect yarn about Tommy Gellin, a shy man with a head of his own, and how he won his darling little wife.

works.title: Torrent of Portyngale
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: A Middle English verse romance in tail-rhyme stanzas. Torrent, the son of a Portuguese earl, loves the king's daughter Desonell, is sent to fight giants and a dragon, and after many adventures is crowned emperor of Rome. Preserved in a single fifteenth-century manuscript.

works.title: Towards Democracy
works.subtitle: Complete Edition in Four Parts
works.author: Edward Carpenter
works.blurb: Carpenter's long free-verse chant in the manner of Whitman, begun in 1881: a single continuing poem of freedom, simplicity and comradeship, followed by three further parts of shorter poems on the city, nature, love and the coming of a new social life.

works.title: The Trachinian Maidens
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Deianira, fearing she is losing Heracles to the captive princess Iole, sends him a robe smeared with what she believes is the centaur Nessus' love-charm. It is a poison, and Heracles is carried home in agony to die on a pyre on Mount Oeta, while Deianira takes her own life.

works.title: Τραχίνιαι (Trachiniai)
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Deianeira, waiting at Trachis for Herakles, sends him a robe smeared with what she believes is a love-charm from the dying centaur Nessos. It is poison, and Herakles' agony and her suicide follow. The Greek text is given in the order of the Storr edition, so that it pairs with the English prose translation of the same play.

works.title: Trachiniae
works.author: Sophocles
works.blurb: Left alone for fifteen months while Heracles is away at war, Deianeira learns that he has sent home a captive princess, Iole, as his new love. To win him back she smears a robe with what the dying centaur Nessus told her was a love-charm, and sends it to him. It is a deadly poison. Jebb's plain, close English prose follows the Greek of Sophocles.

works.title: The Tragedy of Man
works.subtitle: A dramatic poem in fifteen scenes
works.author: Imre Madách
works.blurb: Adam and Eve, newly cast out of Eden, are shown by Lucifer in a series of dreams the future course of humankind, from Egypt, Athens and Rome to the medieval church, Renaissance Prague, revolutionary Paris, a mechanised London and a frozen end of the world. In each dream Adam takes up a new ideal and sees it fail. Waking from the last, he is ready to end his life, until Eve tells him she is to bear a child and God bids him to strive and to trust.

works.title: The Tragedie of Mariam, the Faire Queene of Jewry
works.author: Elizabeth Cary, Viscountess Falkland
works.blurb: Herod, King of Judaea, is reported dead at Rome, and his wife Mariam, who has long hated him for the murder of her brother and grandfather, finds she cannot rejoice. Her mother Alexandra and Herod's sister Salome quarrel over her, while Salome plots to be rid of her husband Constabarus so that she may marry the Arabian Silleus. Herod returns alive, a cup of poison is falsely charged against Mariam, and on Salome's scheming she is beheaded. Too late, Herod is struck with a frantic remorse. The play is the first original tragedy in English to be published by a woman, and each act ends with a Chorus.

works.title: Trial by Jury
works.author: W. S. Gilbert
works.blurb: In a London court of justice, Angelina sues Edwin for breach of promise of marriage. The jury is sympathetic to the plaintiff, the defendant pleads youthful inconstancy, and the Learned Judge, once a briefless barrister who won his place by marrying a rich attorney's elderly daughter, settles the matter by proposing to Angelina himself. Gilbert's first collaboration with Sullivan to reach the stage as a one-act comic opera.

works.title: Le Roman de Tristan
works.subtitle: Old French text (the surviving fragment)
works.author: Béroul
works.blurb: The older, rougher of the two great twelfth-century Tristan poems in French: the lovers' flight to the forest of Morrois, the leper episode, the oath on the relics, and the lovers' parting, in octosyllabic couplets.

works.title: Tristia
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid’s elegies of exile in the original Latin: five books of laments and appeals written from Tomis on the Black Sea.

works.title: The Tristia
works.subtitle: Ovid's Lament from Exile, Books I–V, prose translation by Henry T. Riley
works.author: Ovid
works.blurb: Ovid's five books of elegies written after Augustus banished him to Tomi on the Black Sea, in Riley's prose: the voyage into exile, letters to his wife and friends, pleas for mercy, and the long autobiographical elegy of Book IV.

works.title: Tristram of Lyonesse
works.author: Algernon Charles Swinburne
works.blurb: Swinburne's retelling of the Arthurian love story of Tristram and Iseult in rhymed heroic couplets: a Prelude and nine cantos, from the sailing of the Swallow to the lovers' death and the sailing of the Swan.

works.title: Tristram
works.subtitle: A Poem
works.author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
works.blurb: Blank-verse narrative in ten parts, the last of Robinson's Arthurian poems: the love of Tristram and Isolt of Ireland, the Cornish court of King Mark, and Isolt of the white hands in Brittany.

works.blurb: Petrarch's allegorical procession in terza rima, in which Love, Chastity, Death, Fame, Time and Eternity each triumph in turn.

works.title: The Triumphs of Love and Innocence
works.subtitle: A Tragicomedy
works.author: Anne Finch, Countess of Winchilsea
works.blurb: Written about 1688 and never meant for the stage, this tragicomedy in five acts is set in the palace of the Great Master of the Knights of Rhodes, where the exiled Queen of Cyprus has taken refuge. The Venetian-backed General Lauredan arrives to carry her off, while Blanfort, the Great Master's nephew, loves the Queen and has abandoned Marina, who serves him in disguise as a page. After intrigues, a duel and a charge of treachery, constancy is rewarded and the lovers are reconciled.

works.title: Trivia
works.subtitle: Or, The Art of Walking the Streets of London
works.author: John Gay
works.blurb: Gay's mock-georgic on London on foot — shoes, coats, weather signs, the dangers of day and night — in three books of couplets, with the tale of Cloacina and the origin of the shoeblack.

works.title: Troades
works.subtitle: The Latin original
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: The fallen women of Troy await the Greek ships and learn that the dead Achilles demands the sacrifice of Polyxena and the death of Hector's son Astyanax.

works.title: Troades
works.subtitle: The Trojan Women
works.author: Seneca
works.blurb: Troy has fallen and the Greek fleet waits on the shore for a wind. The ghost of Achilles demands the sacrifice of the princess Polyxena, and the prophet Calchas declares that Hector’s little son Astyanax must die before the Greeks can sail. Hecuba and Andromache, captives awaiting their allotment to Greek masters, are made to watch as the boy is torn from his hiding-place in Hector’s tomb and the girl is led to her death.

works.title: Troilus and Cressida
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Seven years into the siege of Troy, the young prince Troilus, sick with love, enlists Cressida's uncle Pandarus to bring him to her bed, and the two swear eternal faith. Almost at once Cressida is traded to the Greek camp in exchange for the captured Antenor, where she yields to Diomedes while Troilus looks on. Around this affair the Greek leaders quarrel, Akhilleus sulks in his tent with Patroclus, Ajax is puffed up as a champion, and Thersites rails at the whole war. Hector is killed by Akhilleus' Myrmidons, and the play closes on Troy's coming fall and Pandarus' bitter epilogue.

works.title: Troilus and Criseyde
works.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
works.blurb: In rime royal, Chaucer tells how the Trojan prince Troilus wins the love of Criseyde through her uncle Pandarus, and then loses her to the Greek camp, in the original Middle English.

works.title: Τρῳάδες (Troiades)
works.author: Euripides
works.blurb: Troy has fallen and its women wait in the captured camp to be shared out among the Greek chiefs. Poseidon and Athena plot the Greeks' ruin on the voyage home; Hekabe, Kassandra and Andromache learn their fates, Astyanax is thrown from the walls, and the city burns. The Greek text is given in the order of the Nauck edition, so that it pairs with the English translation of the same play.

works.title: Troy Book
works.author: John Lydgate
works.blurb: Lydgate's immense retelling of the Trojan War, made at the request of Prince Henry (later Henry V) and finished about 1420. Working from Guido delle Colonne's Latin Historia destructionis Troiae, he tells the whole story in rhyming couplets: Jason and Medea and the first destruction of Troy (Book I), the rebuilding of the city and the abduction of Helen (II), the war and the death of Hector (III-IV), and the treason that ends Troy, followed by the Greeks' disastrous homecomings (V). Chaucer is honoured throughout as Lydgate's master, and the poem closes with an Envoy to the prince.

works.title: تحفة الاحرار (Tuhfat al-Ahrar)
works.subtitle: Jami's didactic masnavi (1481), the second poem of the Haft Awrang, in the original Persian
works.author: Jami
works.blurb: Jami's 'Gift of the Free', a mystical-ethical masnavi in twenty maqalas, each a discourse on a moral or spiritual theme with illustrative tales, written for his friend and shaykh's circle in 1481.

works.title: Twelfth Night; or, What You Will
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Shipwrecked on the coast of Illyria, Viola disguises herself as the page Cesario and enters the service of Duke Orsino, who loves the Countess Olivia, who in turn falls for the disguised Viola. Meanwhile Olivia's kinsmen and servants gull her pompous steward Malvolio with a forged love letter, while Viola's twin brother Sebastian, believed drowned, turns up to untangle the confusions of identity and desire. Feste the fool sings the songs that frame the play's wistful mirth.

works.title: The Two Foscari
works.subtitle: An Historical Tragedy
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's historical tragedy in five acts, written at Ravenna in June and July 1821. It dramatises the downfall of Francesco Foscari, Doge of Venice, whose son Jacopo is tortured and condemned to exile by the Council of Ten, in the presence of his wife Marina. The play is set in the Ducal Palace and keeps to the unities of time and place.

works.title: The Two Gentlemen of Verona
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Valentine leaves Verona for the court at Milan, where he falls in love with Silvia, the Duke's daughter. His friend Proteus, who has abandoned his own beloved Julia, follows him there, betrays Valentine to the Duke and presses his suit on Silvia. Valentine is banished and becomes captain of a band of outlaws, until Proteus's treachery is exposed in the forest, friendship is renewed, and Julia, who has followed in the disguise of a page, wins back her faithless lover.

works.title: Un coup de dés jamais n'abolira le hasard
works.author: Stéphane Mallarmé
works.blurb: Mallarmé's last great poem, a single sentence scattered across the page in varying type, in which a shipwrecked Master hesitates over a throw of the dice.

works.subtitle: A Season in Hell, in the original French
works.author: Arthur Rimbaud
works.blurb: Rimbaud’s only book of his own making, a short, feverish prose confession in nine parts, written in 1873, which looks back on a life of revolt, vision and failure.

works.subtitle: Rama’s Later Story, in the original Sanskrit
works.author: Bhavabhuti
works.blurb: Bhavabhuti’s play on the later story of Rama in seven acts: the banished Sita, the sorrow of Rama, the shadow-vision of their past at Panchavati, and the reunion of the family through the twin sons Lava and Kusha, who are raised by the sage Valmiki.

works.author: William Blake
works.blurb: Blake's unfinished first epic, in nine Nights, on the fall of Albion, the Ancient Man, into the strife of the Four Zoas and his redemption.

works.title: The Vespers of Palermo
works.subtitle: A Tragedy, in Five Acts
works.author: Felicia Hemans
works.blurb: Sicily, 1282, under the yoke of Charles of Anjou. The exiled Count di Procida returns in disguise and plots a rising with the nobleman Montalba. His son Raimond, who loves Constance, the sister of the French viceroy Eribert, is drawn into the conspiracy, while Eribert presses his suit on Vittoria, widow-in-grief of the murdered Conradin. At the signal of the Vesper-bell the Sicilians rise and massacre their oppressors. Raimond, bound by an oath, must choose between his love and his country, and the play ends in tragedy.

works.blurb: Gorgani's Persian romance of the Parthian-era lovers Vis and Ramin, composed about 1054 at the Seljuk court in Isfahan: among the oldest surviving Persian romances, here in Ganjoor's section order.

works.subtitle: In twelve parts (1821)

Byron's parody of the same title is a different poem.

works.blurb: Vitruvius’s only surviving work and the one complete architectural treatise of antiquity, addressed to Augustus: the education of the architect, city sites, materials, temples, public and private buildings, water, clocks and machines, in the English translation of Morris Hicky Morgan.

works.title: Volpone; or, The Fox
works.author: Ben Jonson
works.blurb: The Venetian magnifico Volpone feigns a mortal illness so that the greedy Voltore, Corbaccio and Corvino will compete to be named his heir, each loading him with gifts, while his parasite Mosca plays them against one another. When Volpone's lust for Corvino's virtuous wife Celia and Mosca's own ambition tip the scheme out of control, the two cheats are hauled before the Venetian magistrates and punished for their trickery.

works.title: The Voyage of Columbus
works.author: Samuel Rogers
works.blurb: Rogers's unfinished narrative of the first Atlantic crossing, set out as translated fragments in twelve cantos, from the mutinous voyage to the discoverer's last days.

works.title: The Voyage of St. Brendan
works.subtitle: A.D. 545
works.author: Denis Florence MacCarthy
works.blurb: MacCarthy’s poem on the legendary sea voyage of St. Brendan of Clonfert to the western isles, in six parts.

works.title: A Voyage to the Isle of Love
works.author: Aphra Behn
works.blurb: Lisander's verse letter to his friend Lysidas, telling of his voyage to the Isle of Love, his happiness with Aminta, her death, and his lonely exile.

The Prospect and Bower of Bliss

works.title: The Wallace
works.subtitle: The Life and Acts of Sir William Wallace of Ellerslie
works.author: Blind Hary
works.blurb: Blind Hary's Older Scots epic in eleven bukes, in rhyming couplets, on the life, battles and betrayal of the Scottish champion Sir William Wallace.

works.title: Waltharius
works.subtitle: The Song of Walter of Aquitaine
works.author: Anonymous (Medieval Latin)
works.blurb: A Latin hexameter epic of Walter of Aquitaine, Hildegund and the flight from Attila's court, long attributed to Ekkehard I of St Gall.

works.title: 西廂記 (Xi xiang ji) — The Story of the Western Wing
works.author: Wang Shifu
works.blurb: The student Zhang Jun-rui meets Cui Ying-ying, the daughter of a dead prime minister, at the Temple of Universal Salvation, and a rebel siege, a clever maid named Hongniang and a stolen night of love bring them together against her mother's wishes. Written in Yuan-dynasty zaju form across five books of four acts each, with long sung arias in rhymed tunes, it is the most loved Chinese love drama, famous for its farewell scene at the Pavilion of Parting and for its happy reunion.

works.title: Wat o' the Cleuch
works.subtitle: A parody of Walter Scott
works.author: James Hogg
works.blurb: Hogg's parody of Walter Scott's border romances, in three cantos, from The Poetic Mirror, in which he imitated the principal living poets of Britain.

works.title: Werner
works.subtitle: Or, The Inheritance: A Tragedy
works.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron
works.blurb: Byron's five-act tragedy, written between December 1821 and January 1822 and published in November 1822. It is adapted from Harriet Lee's tale Kruitzner in her Canterbury Tales. Werner, an impoverished exile whose inheritance is at stake, robs the nobleman Stralenheim, who is his rival for the family estates, and his son Ulric's secret act brings the family to ruin; the action is set at the close of the Thirty Years' War.

works.title: Wesele
works.subtitle: Dramat w 3 aktach (The Wedding, in the original Polish)
works.author: Stanisław Wyspiański
works.blurb: Wyspiański's verse drama of 1901 on a Bronowice wedding at which the guests meet the ghosts of Polish history and fail to act on the call to rise, in Polish.

works.title: The White Devil
works.author: John Webster
works.blurb: Vittoria Corombona, a Venetian beauty, and Brachiano, Duke of Brachiano, are lovers, and her brother Flamineo arranges the murders of her husband Camillo and the Duke's wife Isabella to clear their way. Vittoria is arraigned for the crimes by Cardinal Monticelso and, though she defies her accusers, is condemned to a house of convertites. Brachiano carries her off, but Isabella's brother, the Duke of Florence, plots revenge through the banished Count Lodovico, who poisons the Duke. In the last act the lovers and Flamineo are shot down by disguised assassins, and Giovanni, Brachiano's son, orders justice on the murderers.

works.title: The Texts of the White Yajurveda (Vājasaneyi-Saṃhitā)
works.author: The Rishis of the Yajur Veda
works.blurb: The sacrificial liturgy of the Adhvaryu priests in forty books, from the New and Full Moon rites to the Horse Sacrifice (Books XXII–XXV, XXIX), closing with the Isa Upanishad (Book XL).

works.title: Who Can Be Happy and Free in Russia?
works.subtitle: Verse translation
works.author: Nikolay Nekrasov
works.blurb: Seven peasants, freed from serfdom in 1861, wander Russia asking who lives happily and at ease: the priest, the landowner, the merchant or the Tsar.

works.title: Wilhelm Tell
works.subtitle: Schauspiel
works.author: Friedrich Schiller
works.blurb: Schiller's last completed play, in blank verse: the Swiss cantons of Schwytz, Uri and Unterwalden rise against their Austrian bailiffs. Wilhelm Tell, forced by the tyrant Gessler to shoot an apple from his son's head, kills him in the hollow way near Küssnacht, and the three cantons swear their league of freedom.

works.title: Van den vos Reynaerde
works.subtitle: Comburg manuscript (A)
works.author: Willem die Madocke maecte
works.blurb: The Middle Dutch beast epic of Reynaert the fox, who is summoned to the court of King Nobel the lion and talks his way out of death; the Comburg text, with the original spelling.

works.title: William of Palerne
works.subtitle: Middle English alliterative romance (William and the Werwolf), ed. W. W. Skeat (EETS Extra Series 1, 1867)
works.author: Anonymous (Middle English)
works.blurb: William, the child-prince of Apulia, is carried off by a werwolf who is really a Spanish prince bewitched by his stepmother. Raised by a cowherd and then at the Roman emperor's court, William falls in love with the emperor's daughter Melior, and the two flee in bearskins and then in hartskins, guided and guarded by the werwolf, until William wins a kingdom, the werwolf is restored to his own shape, and William is crowned emperor of Rome. The poem, about 5,500 lines, was made c. 1350 for Humphrey de Bohun, Earl of Hereford, from the French romance Guillaume de Palerne.

works.title: William Tell
works.subtitle: A Play in Five Acts
works.author: Friedrich Schiller
works.blurb: In the Swiss cantons oppressed by the Austrian bailiffs, Werner Stauffacher, Walter Furst and Arnold of Melchthal bind the men of Schwytz, Uri and Unterwald in a league of liberation at the Rutli. Wilhelm Tell, who keeps clear of conspiracy, is forced by the tyrant Gessler to shoot an apple from his own son's head; afterwards he waits in a hollow way near Kussnacht and kills Gessler with his crossbow. The cantons rise and break the castles, and Tell is hailed as their deliverer.

works.title: The Winter’s Tale
works.author: William Shakespeare
works.blurb: Leontes, King of Sicilia, is seized by a sudden jealousy and accuses his pregnant queen, Hermione, of adultery with his oldest friend, Polixenes of Bohemia. He casts out the newborn Perdita, defies the oracle of Apollo, and loses both his son and, as he believes, his wife. Sixteen years pass, announced by the figure of Time, and Perdita, raised by shepherds in Bohemia, falls in love with Prince Florizel amid a sheep-shearing feast enlivened by the rogue Autolycus and his songs. The lovers flee to Sicilia, where the truth comes out and a statue of Hermione, in Paulina’s house, comes to life.

works.title: A Woman Killed with Kindness
works.author: Thomas Heywood
works.blurb: Master Frankford, a country gentleman, takes into his house the penniless Wendoll and is betrayed by him with his wife Anne. Finding them out, Frankford does not kill but banishes her to a distant manor, and her shame and remorse slowly starve her to death. A second plot follows Sir Charles Mountford, ruined by a feud over hawking and rescued by the very enemy whose kindness he repays.

works.title: Works and Days
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: Elton’s rhymed-couplet version of Hesiod’s poem of advice to his brother Perses, with the myths of Pandora and the Five Ages, farming lore and a calendar of days.

works.title: Works and Days
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: Hesiod’s poem of advice to his idle brother Perses, mixing the myths of Pandora and the Five Ages with farming lore, moral counsel and a calendar of lucky and unlucky days.

works.title: Ἔργα καὶ Ἡμέραι (Erga kai Hemerai)
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: The Greek text of Hesiod’s poem of advice to his idle brother Perses, mixing the myths of Pandora and the Five Ages with farming lore, moral counsel and a calendar of lucky and unlucky days.

works.title: Works and Days
works.author: Hesiod
works.blurb: A prose version of Hesiod’s poem of counsel to his brother Perses, with the tales of Prometheus, Pandora and the five ages of men, the praise of honest labour, a farmer’s and sailor’s calendar, and a list of lucky and unlucky days.

works.title: Agesilaus
works.subtitle: An Encomium
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's encomium of Agesilaus II, the Spartan king whom he served and befriended: his birth, his campaigns in Asia and Greece, his piety, courage, self-mastery and simple way of life, closing with a summary of his virtues.

works.title: Anabasis
works.subtitle: The March of the Ten Thousand, in seven books
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's own account of how ten thousand Greek mercenaries marched into Persia with Cyrus the Younger, lost their leader at Cunaxa, and fought their way back to the sea.

works.title: Anabasis
works.subtitle: The March of the Ten Thousand, in seven books
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's own account of how ten thousand Greek mercenaries marched into Persia with Cyrus the Younger, lost their leader at Cunaxa, and fought their way back to the sea.

works.title: The Apology
works.subtitle: Socrates' Defence to the Jury
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's account of why Socrates, on trial for his life, chose to speak as he did and to welcome death as better than a long old age.

works.title: Cyropaedia: The Education of Cyrus
works.subtitle: The education and rule of Cyrus the Great, in eight books
works.author: Xenophon
works.translator: trans. Henry Graham Dakyns, rev. F. M. Stawell (1914)
works.blurb: Xenophon's romance-like life of Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian empire: his Persian upbringing, his campaigns, and his ideal of the ruler who wins willing obedience.

works.title: Cyropaedia: The Education of Cyrus
works.subtitle: The education and rule of Cyrus the Great, in eight books
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's romance-like life of Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian empire: his Persian upbringing, his campaigns, and his ideal of the ruler who wins willing obedience.

works.title: The Economist
works.subtitle: Oeconomicus: a Treatise on the Science of the Household, in the Form of a Dialogue
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's dialogue on the management of a household and estate: Socrates and Critobulus discuss wealth and farming, and Socrates recalls the model gentleman Ischomachus, his methods and his instruction of his young wife.

works.title: Hellenica
works.subtitle: A history of Greek affairs from 411 to 362 BC, in seven books
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's continuation of Thucydides: the closing years of the Peloponnesian War, the Spartan ascendancy, and the rise and fall of Theban power down to the battle of Mantinea.

works.title: Hellenica
works.subtitle: A history of Greek affairs from 411 to 362 BC, in seven books
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's continuation of Thucydides: the closing years of the Peloponnesian War, the Spartan ascendancy, and the rise and fall of Theban power down to the battle of Mantinea.

works.title: Memorabilia
works.subtitle: Recollections of Socrates, in four books
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's recollections of Socrates in word and deed, written to answer the charges on which Athens put him to death and to show him as the best and happiest of men.

works.title: Memorabilia
works.subtitle: Recollections of Socrates, in four books
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's recollections of Socrates in word and deed, written to answer the charges on which Athens put him to death and to show him as the best and happiest of men.

works.title: The Polity of the Athenians (attributed to Xenophon)
works.subtitle: The work of the anonymous author known as the Old Oligarch
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: A short pamphlet on the Athenian democracy, handed down among Xenophon's works but written by an unknown author, which argues that the democracy, though not to be praised, preserves itself by sound means.

works.title: The Polity of the Lacedaemonians
works.subtitle: On the laws and institutions of Sparta
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: Xenophon's account of the Spartan constitution: the laws Lycurgus gave Sparta, which train its citizens from birth to old age, and the covenant between king and state.

works.title: The Symposium
works.subtitle: The Banquet
works.author: Xenophon
works.blurb: A dinner given by the wealthy Callias for the youth Autolycus, at which Socrates and his friends each say what they most prize, and the evening closes with a mimed wedding of Dionysus and Ariadne.

works.title: Y Gododdin
works.subtitle: The Book of Aneirin, 97 numbered stanzas
works.author: Aneirin
works.blurb: The Welsh elegy for the war-band of Mynyddog, lost at the battle of Catraeth, in the manuscript spelling of the Book of Aneirin, in 97 numbered stanzas.

works.title: The Yashts
works.subtitle: Hymns to the yazatas, from the Zend-Avesta, Part II
works.author: The Avesta
works.blurb: The twenty-two Yashts of the Younger Avesta, hymns of praise to Ahura Mazda and the yazatas, from Mithra and Anahita to the Fravashis, in James Darmesteter’s prose translation of 1883.
